lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],For this question, refer to the KnightMotives Automotive case study. KnightMotives has deployed its new Dealer Tools on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), and you are supporting performance of the GKE workloads. Some Pods are stateful.  
  
To prevent these Pods from using an unlimited amount of CPU, you configured resource limits on the Deployments. You determined that the Pods were allocated too much CPU and, at times, consume drastically less. You want to optimize resource use while allowing maximum flexibility if load increases. What should you do?

options.text: Configure resource requests per Deployment. Set resource requests slightly above the typical CPU usage observed during monitoring.
Configure resource requests per Deployment. Ensure the requests are equal to the current limits.
Enable vertical Pod autoscaling on each Deployment. Ensure the autoscaling mode is set to Auto.
Enable horizontal Pod autoscaling on each Deployment. Ensure the minimum number of Pods is lower than the currently configured amount in the Deployment.

questions.explanation:
GKE Vertical Pod Autoscaling analyzes workload usage over time and automatically adjusts container CPU and memory resource requests and limits. Its `Auto` mode applies those adjustments as workload requirements change, which rightsizes over-allocated Pods while retaining capacity to adapt to higher usage. Horizontal Pod Autoscaling changes the number of Pod replicas rather than correcting per-Pod CPU allocation. [Google Cloud: Vertical Pod autoscaling](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/verticalpodautoscaler)

**Learn more:** [Vertical Pod autoscaling | Google Kubernetes Engine](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/verticalpodautoscaler) · [Scale container resource requests and limits | Google Kubernetes Engine](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/vertical-pod-autoscaling)

questions.domain: Designing and planning a cloud solution architecture
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are migrating your on-premises solution to Google Cloud in multiple phases. You will use Cloud VPN to keep a connection between your on-premises systems and Google Cloud until the migration is complete. You need to ensure that all on-premises systems remain reachable during this time. How should you arrange your Google Cloud networking?

options.text: Use the same IP range on Google Cloud as you use on-premises
Use the same IP range on Google Cloud as you use on-premises for your primary IP range and use a secondary range that does not overlap with the range you use on-premises
Use an IP range on Google Cloud that does not overlap with the range you use on-premises
Use an IP range on Google Cloud that does not overlap with the range you use on-premises for your primary IP range and use a secondary range with the same IP range as you use on-premises

questions.explanation:
Cloud VPN requires non-overlapping Google Cloud VPC and on-premises IP ranges for unambiguous routing. If the same subnet range exists in both places, routes for the on-premises range cannot be used through the VPN (or are ignored with dynamic routing), so traffic for that range stays within the VPC rather than reaching the on-premises systems.

**Learn more:** [Order of routes | Cloud VPN](https://docs.cloud.google.com/network-connectivity/docs/vpn/concepts/order-of-routes) · [Cloud VPN overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/network-connectivity/docs/vpn/concepts/overview)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are configuring a new regional environment for your business requirements. You intend to migrate more than 2 TB of data from the `us-central1` region to the `asia-southeast1` region. The transfer must take place as quickly as possible. If it is interrupted, the operation must continue from where it stopped and copy only new or changed objects. What should you do?

options.text: Use the gcloud storage cp command to copy the objects. Be careful to manage potential naming conflicts to ensure data integrity.
Utilize Storage Transfer Service (STS) to migrate objects to the destination bucket in the target region. Once the transfer is complete, delete the original source bucket objects.
Use the gcloud storage rsync --recursive command to replicate the source bucket to a new target bucket in the us-west1 region.
Leverage Cloud Composer to orchestrate a data pipeline that copies objects from the source bucket to the destination bucket.

questions.explanation:
Storage Transfer Service is designed for large Cloud Storage bucket migrations and provides managed performance, reliability, and retry handling. It can resume a paused transfer operation from the point at which it was paused, and its transfers are incremental by default, so later runs transfer only objects that changed after the initial transfer.

**Learn more:** [Transfer between Cloud Storage buckets](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage-transfer/docs/cloud-storage-to-cloud-storage) · [Manage transfers](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage-transfer/docs/manage-transfers)

A record number of users are attempting to use the service, but many are receiving 503 errors and experiencing very slow response times. What should they investigate first?

options.text: Verify that the database is online
Verify that the project quota hasn't been exceeded
Verify that the new feature code did not introduce any performance bugs
Verify that the load-testing team is not running their tool against production

questions.explanation:

Your organization stores sensitive data in a Cloud Storage bucket. Because of regulatory requirements, the company must be able to rotate the encryption key that protects the bucket’s data. The data will be processed in Dataproc. You want to follow Google-recommended security practices. What should you do?

options.text: Create a key with Cloud Key Management Service (KMS). Encrypt the data using the encrypt method of Cloud KMS.
Create a key with Cloud Key Management Service (KMS). Set the encryption key on the bucket to the Cloud KMS key.
Generate a GPG key pair. Encrypt the data using the GPG key. Upload the encrypted data to the bucket.
Generate an AES-256 encryption key. Encrypt the data in the bucket using the customer-supplied encryption keys feature.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Storage supports customer-managed encryption keys (CMEKs) from Cloud Key Management Service. Configuring a Cloud KMS key as the bucket’s encryption key lets Cloud Storage perform server-side encryption while the organization controls key rotation, permissions, and lifecycle through Cloud KMS.

**Learn more:** [Customer-managed encryption keys | Cloud Storage](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/encryption/customer-managed-keys) · [CMEK key rotation | Cloud Key Management Service](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kms/docs/cmek-rotation)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Dress4Win has asked for your advice on migrating its on-premises MySQL deployment to the cloud.  
  
They want to minimize downtime and performance impact on their on-premises solution during the migration.  
  
Which approach should you recommend?

options.text: Create a dump of the on-premises MySQL master server, and then shut it down, upload it to the cloud environment, and load into a new MySQL cluster.
Setup a MySQL replica server/slave in the cloud environment, and configure it for asynchronous replication from the MySQL master server on-premises until cutover.
Create a new MySQL cluster in the cloud, configure applications to begin writing to both on premises and cloud MySQL masters, and destroy the original cluster at cutover.
Create a dump of the MySQL replica server into the cloud environment, load it into: Google Cloud Datastore, and configure applications to read/write to Cloud Datastore at cutover.

questions.explanation:
Asynchronous replication from the on-premises MySQL primary to a cloud replica keeps the cloud copy continuously synchronized while the existing deployment remains online. After replication catches up, applications can be redirected during a brief cutover, minimizing downtime and avoiding the consistency risks of simultaneous writes to separate masters. Google Cloud documents replication from an external MySQL server as a migration approach that achieves minimum downtime.

**Learn more:** [About replicating from an external server | Cloud SQL for MySQL](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/mysql/replication/external-server)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to establish a private connection between your Compute Engine instances and your on-premises data center. The connection must provide at least 20 Gbps, and you want to follow Google-recommended practices. How should you configure the connection?

options.text: Create a VPC and connect it to your on-premises data center using Dedicated Interconnect.
Create a VPC and connect it to your on-premises data center using a single Cloud VPN.
Create a Cloud Content Delivery Network (Cloud CDN) and connect it to your on-premises data center using Dedicated Interconnect.
Create a Cloud Content Delivery Network (Cloud CDN) and connect it to your on-premises datacenter using a single Cloud VPN.

questions.explanation:
Dedicated Interconnect directly connects an on-premises network to Google’s network and supports capacity using one or more 10-Gbps circuits, so it can meet a 20-Gbps requirement. The connection is attached to a VPC network, which provides connectivity for Compute Engine instances. A single Cloud VPN tunnel does not provide comparable throughput, and Cloud CDN is not a hybrid private-connectivity service.

**Learn more:** [Dedicated Interconnect overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/network-connectivity/docs/interconnect/concepts/dedicated-overview) · [Cloud VPN overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/network-connectivity/docs/vpn/concepts/overview)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company runs a stateless application on a Compute Engine instance. The application is heavily used during normal business hours and lightly used outside those hours. Users report that the application is slow during peak periods. You need to optimize the application's performance. What should you do?

options.text: Create a snapshot of the existing disk. Create an instance template from the snapshot. Create an autoscaled managed instance group from the instance template.
Create a snapshot of the existing disk. Create a custom image from the snapshot. Create an autoscaled managed instance group from the custom image.
Create a custom image from the existing disk. Create an instance template from the custom image. Create an autoscaled managed instance group from the instance template.
Create an instance template from the existing disk. Create a custom image from the instance template. Create an autoscaled managed instance group from the custom image.

questions.explanation:
An autoscaled managed instance group adds VM instances as workload demand rises and removes them as demand falls, which suits a stateless application with peak-hour load. Managed instance groups are created from an instance template; creating a custom image from the existing disk allows that template to reproduce the application’s VM configuration consistently.

**Learn more:** [Autoscaling groups of instances | Compute Engine | Google Cloud Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/autoscaler) · [Create instance templates | Compute Engine | Google Cloud Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instance-templates/create-instance-templates)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has a Google Cloud project that uses BigQuery for data warehousing. It has a VPN tunnel between its on-premises environment and Google Cloud, configured with Cloud VPN. The security team wants to prevent data exfiltration by malicious insiders, compromised code, and accidental oversharing.  
  
What should the company do?

options.text: Configure Private Google Access for on-premises only.
Perform the following tasks: 1. Create a service account. 2. Give the BigQuery JobUser role and Storage Reader role to the service account. 3. Remove all other IAM access from the project.
Configure VPC Service Controls and configure Private Google Access.
Configure Private Google Access.

questions.explanation:
VPC Service Controls establishes a service perimeter around BigQuery and other supported Google-managed services, restricting access and data movement to mitigate exfiltration by insiders, compromised credentials or code, and unintended sharing. Private Google Access enables the on-premises private hosts, connected through Cloud VPN, to reach Google APIs within that protected perimeter.

**Learn more:** [Overview of VPC Service Controls](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/overview) · [Private Google Access with VPC Service Controls](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/private-connectivity?hl=en)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A small subset of API requests to your microservices-based application takes a very long time. You know that each API request can traverse many services.  
  
You want to identify which service takes the longest in those situations. What should you do?

options.text: Set timeouts on your application so that you can fail requests faster
Send custom metrics for each of your requests to Stackdriver Monitoring
Use Stackdriver Monitoring to look for insights that show when your API latencies are high
Instrument your application with Stackdriver Trace in order to break down the request latencies at each microservice

questions.explanation:
Cloud Trace (formerly Stackdriver Trace) is a distributed tracing system that captures request latency and spans for operations such as RPC calls. Instrumenting each microservice lets a single request be traced across services and its per-service durations compared, revealing the service responsible for the longest portion of the request.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Trace overview](https://cloud.google.com/trace/docs/overview) · [Instrument for Cloud Trace](https://cloud.google.com/trace/docs/setup)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work with a data-warehousing team that performs data analysis. The team must process data from external partners, but that data contains personally identifiable information (PII). You need to process and store the data without storing any of the PIIE data. What should you do?

options.text: Create a Dataflow pipeline to retrieve the data from the external sources. As part of the pipeline, use the Cloud Data Loss Prevention (Cloud DLP) API to remove any PII data. Store the result in BigQuery.

Create a Dataflow pipeline to retrieve the data from the external sources. As part of the pipeline, store all non-PII data in BigQuery and store all PII data in a Cloud Storage bucket that has a retention policy set.

Ask the external partners to upload all data on Cloud Storage. Configure Bucket Lock for the bucket. Create a Dataflow pipeline to read the data from the bucket. As part of the pipeline, use the Cloud Data Loss Prevention (Cloud DLP) API to remove any PII data. Store the result in BigQuery.

Ask the external partners to import all data in your BigQuery dataset. Create a dataflow pipeline to copy the data into a new table. As part of the Dataflow bucket, skip all data in columns that have PII data

questions.explanation:
Sensitive Data Protection (formerly Cloud DLP) can detect PII and apply de-identification transformations such as masking, replacement, or removal. Applying those transformations in a Dataflow ingestion pipeline before writing to BigQuery ensures that the stored warehouse output contains no PII, while retaining the non-sensitive data for analysis.

**Learn more:** [De-identifying sensitive data](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sensitive-data-protection/docs/deidentify-sensitive-data) · [Using Sensitive Data Protection with BigQuery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sensitive-data-protection/docs/dlp-bigquery)

A company develops rendering software that users can download from its website. The company has customers worldwide and wants to minimize latency for every customer while following Google-recommended practices.  
  
How should the files be stored?

options.text: Save the files in a Multi-Regional Cloud Storage bucket.
Save the files in a Regional Cloud Storage bucket, one bucket per zone of the region.
Save the files in multiple Regional Cloud Storage buckets, one bucket per zone per region.
Save the files in multiple Multi-Regional Cloud Storage buckets, one bucket per multi-region.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Storage recommends multi-region bucket locations for cross-geography data access and content serving. Storing the downloadable content in a multi-regional bucket for each multi-region places it across the major geographic areas, supporting low-latency access for global customers.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has chosen to make a major revision to its API to provide better experiences for its developers. It must keep the old API version available and deployable while allowing new customers and testers to try the new API. It wants to retain the same SSL and DNS records to serve both APIs.  
  
What should it do?

options.text: Configure a new load balancer for the new version of the API
Reconfigure old clients to use a new endpoint for the new API
Have the old API forward traffic to the new API based on the path
Use separate backend pools for each API path behind the load balancer

questions.explanation:
A URL map on an HTTPS/Application Load Balancer can route requests by URL path to different backend services while retaining one frontend IP address, DNS name, and SSL configuration. Assigning each API path to its own backend pool enables the old and new API versions to remain independently available and deployable.

**Learn more:** [URL maps overview | Cloud Load Balancing](https://docs.cloud.google.com/load-balancing/docs/url-map-concepts)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company and one of its partners each own a Google Cloud project in separate organizations. Your company’s project (`prj-a`) runs in Virtual Private Cloud (`vpc-a`). The partner’s project (`prj-b`) runs in `vpc-b`. Two instances run in `vpc-a`, and one instance runs in `vpc-b`. The subnets defined in the two VPCs do not overlap. You need to ensure that every instance can communicate with the others through internal IP addresses while minimizing latency and maximizing throughput. What should you do?

options.text: Set up a network peering between vpc-a and vpc-b.
Set up a VPN between vpc-a and vpc-b using Cloud VPN.

Configure IAP TCP forwarding on the instance in vpc-b, and then launch the following gcloud command from one of the instances in vpc-a gcloud: gcloud compute start-iap-tunnel INSTANCE_NAME_IN_VPC_8 22 \ --local-host-port=localhost:22

1. Create an additional instance in vpc-a. 2. Create an additional instance in vpc-b. 3. Install OpenVPN in newly created instances. 4. Configure a VPN tunnel between vpc-a and vpc-b with the help of OpenVPN.

questions.explanation:
VPC Network Peering connects VPC networks across different projects and organizations and exchanges private subnet routes when their address ranges do not overlap. It provides internal-IP connectivity, and peering traffic has the same latency and throughput as traffic within a single VPC.

**Learn more:** [VPC Network Peering](https://cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/vpc-peering) · [Set up and manage VPC Network Peering](https://cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/using-vpc-peering)

questions.domain: Designing and planning a cloud solution architecture
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A retail company’s most critical application is its online payment-processing system. The business requires that the system survive a complete zonal outage while minimizing cost. You need a design that can handle a zonal failure. What should you do?

options.text: Deploy the application in an active-active configuration using managed instance groups (MIGs) in two different regions, fronted by a global external HTTP(S) Load Balancer and backed by a multi-regional database like Spanner.
Deploy the application on a regional MIG to provide high availability across multiple zones in the primary region.
Configure the regional MIG to use only Spot VMs to aggressively minimize operational costs while maintaining high availability.
Deploy the application on Compute Engine instances across multiple regions, and rely on daily snapshots for recovery to achieve the lowest possible cost.

questions.explanation:
A regional managed instance group distributes application instances across multiple zones in the same region, protecting the workload from a zonal failure because instances in the remaining zones can continue serving traffic. This provides the required zonal resilience without the additional cost and complexity of an active-active multi-region architecture.

**Learn more:** [About regional MIGs](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instance-groups/regional-migs)

questions.domain: Designing and planning a cloud solution architecture
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are deploying an application to Google Cloud as part of a system. The Google Cloud application must communicate, over a private network, with applications in a non-Google Cloud environment. The anticipated average throughput is 200 kbps.  
  
The business requires:  
  
- 99.99% system availability  
- Cost optimization  
  
You need to design connectivity between the locations to satisfy these business requirements. What should you provision?

options.text: An HA Cloud VPN gateway connected with two tunnels to an on-premises VPN gateway.
A Classic Cloud VPN gateway connected with two tunnels to an on-premises VPN gateway.
Two HA Cloud VPN gateways connected to two on-premises VPN gateways. Configure each HA Cloud VPN gateway to have two tunnels, each connected to different on-premises VPN gateways.
A Classic Cloud VPN gateway connected with one tunnel to an on-premises VPN gateway.

questions.explanation:
HA VPN can provide a 99.99% availability SLA when VPN tunnels are configured on both interfaces of the HA VPN gateway. A pair of tunnels to the on-premises peer provides the required redundant connectivity with fewer billed gateway and tunnel resources than deploying two HA VPN gateways and four tunnels. Classic VPN provides a 99.9% SLA, so it does not meet the availability requirement.

**Learn more:** [Cloud VPN overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/network-connectivity/docs/vpn/concepts/overview) · [HA VPN topologies](https://docs.cloud.google.com/network-connectivity/docs/vpn/concepts/topologies)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],As part of Dress4Win’s cloud-migration plans, they want to establish a managed logging and monitoring system to handle spikes in traffic load. They want to ensure that:  
  
- The infrastructure can be notified when it must scale up or down to accommodate usage ebbing and flowing throughout the day.  
- Their administrators are automatically notified when the application reports errors.  
- They can filter aggregated logs to debug one part of the application across many hosts.  
  
Which Google Stackdriver features should they use?

options.text: Logging, Alerts, Insights, Debug
Monitoring, Trace, Debug, Logging
Monitoring, Logging, Alerts, Error Reporting
Monitoring, Logging, Debug, Error Report

questions.explanation:
Cloud Monitoring provides metric monitoring and alerting policies for changing load conditions. Cloud Logging aggregates, searches, and filters log data across infrastructure. Alerts deliver notifications to administrators, and Error Reporting aggregates and identifies application errors.

**Learn more:** [Google Cloud Observability documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/observability) · [Alerting overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/monitoring/alerts)

questions.domain: Analyzing and optimizing technical and business processes
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company runs a Kubernetes application that retrieves messages from Pub/Sub and writes them to Filestore. Because the application is simple, it was deployed as one pod. The infrastructure team analyzed Pub/Sub metrics and found that the application cannot process messages in real time; most wait minutes before processing. You need to scale the I/O-intensive elaboration process. What should you do?

options.text: Use kubectl autoscale deployment APP_NAME --max 6 --min 2 --cpu-percent 50 to configure Kubernetes autoscaling deployment.
Configure a Kubernetes autoscaling deployment based on the subscription/push_request_latencies metric.
Use the --enable-autoscaling flag when you create the Kubernetes cluster.
Configure a Kubernetes autoscaling deployment based on the subscription/num_undelivered_messages metric.

questions.explanation:
A Horizontal Pod Autoscaler should scale the consumer deployment from the Pub/Sub subscription backlog. `subscription/num_undelivered_messages` reports the number of unacknowledged messages waiting in the subscription, directly indicating that consumers are not keeping up. It is more suitable than CPU utilization for an I/O-intensive workload, because CPU usage may not reflect processing saturation.

**Learn more:** [Optimize Pod autoscaling based on metrics | Google Kubernetes Engine](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/tutorials/autoscaling-metrics)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to ensure that Dress4Win’s sales and tax records stay available for occasional auditor review for at least 10 years.  
  
Cost optimization is the highest priority.  
  
Which cloud services should you select?

options.text: Google Cloud Storage Coldline to store the data, and gsutil to access the data.
Google Cloud Storage Nearline to store the data, and gsutil to access the data.
Google Bigtabte with US or EU as location to store the data, and gcloud to access the data.

BigQuery to store the data, and a web server cluster in a managed instance group to access the data. Google Cloud SQL mirrored across two distinct regions to store the data, and a Redis cluster in a managed instance group to access the data.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Storage Coldline is a very-low-cost, highly durable storage class for data that is read or modified at most once per quarter. Its 90-day minimum storage duration is compatible with 10-year retention, and objects can be retrieved with gsutil. Nearline is designed for data accessed about once per month, while database and compute services introduce unnecessary cost for long-term, infrequently viewed records.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Storage storage classes](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/storage-classes)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],All Compute Engine instances in your VPC must be able to connect to an Active Directory server on specified ports. No other traffic leaving the instances is permitted. You want to enforce this with VPC firewall rules.  
  
How should you configure the firewall rules?

options.text: Create an egress rule with priority 1000 to deny all traffic for all instances. Create another egress rule with priority 100 to allow the Active Directory traffic for all instances.
Create an egress rule with priority 100 to deny all traffic for all instances. Create another egress rule with priority 1000 to allow the Active Directory traffic for all instances.
Create an egress rule with priority 1000 to allow the Active Directory traffic. Rely on the implied deny egress rule with priority 100 to block all traffic for all instances.
Create an egress rule with priority 100 to allow the Active Directory traffic. Rely on the implied deny egress rule with priority 1000 to block all traffic for all instances.

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud VPC firewall rules evaluate lower numeric priorities before higher numeric priorities. An egress allow rule at priority 100 for the required Active Directory ports takes precedence over a deny-all egress rule at priority 1000. This allows the required connections and denies all other egress traffic. The implied egress action is allow, so it cannot be used to block remaining traffic.

**Learn more:** [VPC firewall rules](https://cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/firewalls)

questions.domain: Designing and planning a cloud solution architecture
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],For this question, refer to the Dress4Win case study. You want to make sure that your on-premises architecture satisfies business requirements before migrating your solution.  
  
Which change should you make to the on-premises architecture?

options.text: Replace RabbitMQ with Google Pub/Sub.
Downgrade MySQL to v5.7, which is supported by Cloud SQL for MySQL.
Resize compute resources to match predefined Compute Engine machine types.
Containerize the micro-services and host them in Google Kubernetes Engine.

questions.explanation:
Sizing on-premises compute resources to align with predefined Compute Engine machine types makes the workload’s CPU and memory requirements directly portable to the target virtual-machine configurations. Compute Engine predefined machine types provide fixed vCPU and memory combinations, so aligning resource sizing before migration helps validate that the target environment can meet the workload requirements.

**Learn more:** [General-purpose machine family for Compute Engine](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/general-purpose-machines)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company collects all web-traffic data in Google Analytics 360 and stores it in BigQuery. Each country has a separate dataset, and every dataset contains multiple tables.  
  
You want analysts in each country to view and query data only for their own country.  
  
How should you configure the access rights?

options.text: Create a group per country. Add analysts to their respective country-groups. Create a single group 'all_analysts', and add all country-groups as members. Grant the 'all_analysts' group the IAM role of BigQuery jobUser. Share the appropriate dataset with view access with each respective analyst country-group.

Create a group per country. Add analysts to their respective country-groups. Create a single group 'all_analysts', and add all country-groups as members. Grant the 'all_analysts' group the IAM role of BigQuery jobUser. Share the appropriate tables with view access with each respective analyst country-group.

Create a group per country. Add analysts to their respective country-groups. Create a single group 'all_analysts', and add all country-groups as members. Grant the 'all_analysts' group the IAM role of BigQuery dataViewer. Share the appropriate dataset with view access with each respective analyst country- group.

Create a group per country. Add analysts to their respective country-groups. Create a single group 'all_analysts', and add all country-groups as members. Grant the 'all_analysts' group the IAM role of BigQuery dataViewer. Share the appropriate table with view access with each respective analyst country-group.

questions.explanation: Running queries requires permission to create BigQuery jobs, and reading the data requires read access. Granting the combined analyst group the BigQuery Job User role allows its members to create query jobs, while granting each country-specific group view access to only its corresponding dataset allows access to all tables in that dataset and prevents access to other countries’ datasets.

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company sends batches of sensitive transaction data from its application-server VMs to Cloud Pub/Sub for processing and storage. What is the Google-recommended method for the application to authenticate to the required Google Cloud services?

options.text: Ensure that VM service accounts are granted the appropriate Cloud Pub/Sub IAM roles.
Ensure that VM service accounts do not have access to Cloud Pub/Sub, and use VM access scopes to grant the appropriate Cloud Pub/Sub IAM roles.
Generate an OAuth2 access token for accessing Cloud Pub/Sub, encrypt it, and store it in Cloud Storage for access from each VM.
Create a gateway to Cloud Pub/Sub using a Cloud Function, and grant the Cloud Function service account the appropriate Cloud Pub/Sub IAM roles.

questions.explanation:
Applications running on Compute Engine VMs should authenticate by using the attached service account through Application Default Credentials. The service account must receive only the Cloud Pub/Sub IAM roles required for the workload, which authorizes it to publish or otherwise access Pub/Sub resources.

**Learn more:** [How Application Default Credentials works](https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/application-default-credentials) · [Authenticate to Compute Engine](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/authentication)

questions.domain: Designing and planning a cloud solution architecture
questions.question:
Your company anticipates a sharp growth in both the number and size of Apache Spark and Hadoop jobs run in its local data center. You want to use the cloud to scale for this upcoming demand with the least operational effort and code changes possible.  
  
Which product should you use?

options.text: Google Cloud Dataflow
Google Cloud Dataproc
Google Compute Engine
Google Kubernetes Engine

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud Dataproc is a fully managed Apache Spark and Apache Hadoop service. It provisions, manages, monitors, and scales clusters for existing Spark and Hadoop workloads, minimizing both cluster-administration effort and application changes.\
\
**Learn more:** [Dataproc FAQ](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataproc/docs/resources/faq)

questions.domain: Designing and planning a cloud solution architecture
questions.question:
Your company anticipates a sharp growth in both the number and size of Apache Spark and Hadoop jobs run in its local data center. You want to use the cloud to scale for this upcoming demand with the least operational effort and code changes possible.  
  
Which product should you use?

options.text: Google Compute Engine unmanaged instance groups and Network Load Balancer
Google Compute Engine managed instance groups with auto-scaling
Google Cloud Dataproc to run Apache Hadoop jobs to process each test
Google App Engine with Google StackDriver for logging

questions.explanation:
Compute Engine managed instance groups with autoscaling run identical Linux VM test workers from an instance template and automatically add capacity as workload demand increases. This enables parallel execution of the existing C++ tests with little application change, reducing full-suite completion time. Managed instance groups provide autoscaling; unmanaged instance groups require the VM fleet to be managed manually.

**Learn more:** [Autoscaling groups of instances | Compute Engine](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/autoscaler) · [Instance groups | Compute Engine](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instance-groups?hl=en)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],The JencoMart security team requires that all Google Cloud Platform infrastructure be deployed under a least-privilege model, with administrative separation of duties between production and development resources.  
  
Which Google domain and project structure should you recommend?

options.text: Create two G Suite accounts to manage users: one for development/test/staging and one for production. Each account should contain one project for every application
Create two G Suite accounts to manage users: one with a single project for all development applications and one with a single project for all production applications
Create a single G Suite account to manage users with each stage of each application in its own project
Create a single G Suite account to manage users with one project for the development/test/staging environment and one project for the production environment

questions.explanation:
A single organizational domain with a separate project for every application stage provides distinct IAM policy boundaries for development, test, staging, and production resources. Project-level role assignments can limit administrators to only their assigned environment and application, supporting least privilege and separation of duties. Google Cloud identifies projects as core organizational units for resources and permissions, and IAM enables granular access to specific resources.

**Learn more:** [About the Google Cloud resource hierarchy](https://cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/cloud-platform-resource-hierarchy) · [Access control for projects with IAM](https://cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/access-control-proj)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Dress4Win wants to become familiar with deploying applications to the cloud by quickly deploying some applications as-is. They have requested your recommendation.  
  
What should you advise?

options.text: Identify self-contained applications with external dependencies as a first move to the cloud.
Identify enterprise applications with internal dependencies and recommend these as a first move to the cloud.
Suggest moving their in-house databases to the cloud and continue serving requests to on-premise applications.
Recommend moving their message queuing servers to the cloud and continue handling requests to on-premise applications.

questions.explanation:
Self-contained applications are suitable early candidates for an as-is, lift-and-shift migration because their limited scope reduces migration complexity and risk. Moving shared databases or messaging infrastructure ahead of the applications that use them creates hybrid dependencies, and enterprise applications with internal dependencies require more planning and coordination.

**Learn more:** [What is cloud migration? Strategy and process](https://cloud.google.com/learn/cloud-migration)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A few days after JencoMart migrates its user-credentials database to Google Cloud Platform and shuts down the old server, the new database server stops responding to SSH connections. It is still correctly serving database requests to the application servers.  
  
What three steps should you take to diagnose the problem? (Choose three.)

options.text: Delete the virtual machine (VM) and disks and create a new one
Delete the instance, attach the disk to a new VM, and investigate
Take a snapshot of the disk and connect to a new machine to investigate
Check inbound firewall rules for the network the machine is connected to
Connect the machine to another network with very simple firewall rules and investigate
Print the Serial Console output for the instance for troubleshooting, activate the interactive console, and investigate

questions.explanation:
A VM that continues serving production traffic should be diagnosed without deleting it or detaching its active boot disk. Check ingress firewall rules for SSH access, create a snapshot for isolated investigation on a separate VM, and use serial-port output plus interactive serial-console access to diagnose operating-system or network issues when SSH is unavailable.

**Learn more:** [Troubleshooting SSH errors | Compute Engine | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/troubleshooting/troubleshooting-ssh-errors) · [Troubleshooting using the serial console | Compute Engine | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/troubleshooting/troubleshooting-using-serial-console)

You are responsible for securing data that Dress4Win stores in Cloud Storage. You have already created Google Groups and added the appropriate users to those groups. Follow Google best practices and implement the simplest design that meets the requirements.

options.text: Assign custom IAM roles to the Google Groups you created in order to enforce security requirements. Encrypt data with a customer-supplied encryption key when storing files in Cloud Storage.
Assign custom IAM roles to the Google Groups you created in order to enforce security requirements. Enable default storage encryption before storing files in Cloud Storage.
Assign predefined IAM roles to the Google Groups you created in order to enforce security requirements. Utilize Google's default encryption at rest when storing files in Cloud Storage.

questions.explanation:

You must upgrade the EHR connection to meet its requirements. The redesigned connection must support business-critical needs while meeting the same network and security policy requirements. What should you do?

options.text: Add a new Dedicated Interconnect connection.
Upgrade the bandwidth on the Dedicated Interconnect connection to 100 G.
Add three new Cloud VPN connections.
Add a new Carrier Peering connection.

questions.explanation:
A Dedicated Interconnect connection cannot be upgraded in place to a higher link type. Moving to 100 Gbps requires provisioning a new 100-Gbps Dedicated Interconnect connection alongside the existing connection and migrating traffic to it. This retains the private, high-availability Interconnect architecture appropriate for business-critical workloads.

**Learn more:** [Modify Dedicated Interconnect connections](https://docs.cloud.google.com/network-connectivity/docs/interconnect/how-to/dedicated/modifying-interconnects) · [Dedicated Interconnect overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/network-connectivity/docs/interconnect/concepts/dedicated-overview)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are responsible for architecting a critical ecommerce application. The application's web frontends run on Compute Engine instances deployed across multiple zones in one region. The architecture must be highly available and self-healing. If a zone becomes unavailable, the system must automatically recreate the lost capacity in the remaining available zones. To maximize efficiency, ensure that every provisioned compute resource actively handles traffic during normal operations, and that user traffic is automatically and seamlessly routed away from any failed instance or zone. What should you do?

options.text: Configure a regional external Application Load Balancer with a primary regional managed instance group (MIG) as its backend service, and configure a second regional MIG as a failover backend.

Create a single regional unmanaged instance group spanning all three zones. Place a regional external Application Load Balancer in front of the group, and configure its backend service with a health check.

Create a single regional managed instance group (MIG) configured to span all three zones. Place a regional external Application Load Balancer in front of the MIG, and configure its backend service with a health check.
Create three separate zonal managed instance groups (MIGs), and use Cloud DNS with weighted routing to distribute traffic across the public IP address of an instance in each MIG.

questions.explanation:
A regional managed instance group distributes managed VMs across multiple zones in a region and provides managed recovery for failed instances. A regional external Application Load Balancer uses backend health checks to make only healthy instances eligible for new requests, automatically steering traffic away from unhealthy instances or a failed zone. This uses all healthy instances as active backend capacity instead of reserving an idle failover group.

**Learn more:** [About regional MIGs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instance-groups/regional-migs) · [Instance groups](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instance-groups)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],As part of its new application experience, Dress4Wm lets customers upload images of themselves.  
  
Each customer has exclusive control over who can view these images.  
  
Customers must be able to upload images with minimal latency and see their images quickly on the main application page when they log in.  
  
Which configuration should Dress4Win use?

options.text: Store image files in a Google Cloud Storage bucket. Use Google Cloud Datastore to maintain metadata that maps each customer's ID and their image files.
Store image files in a Google Cloud Storage bucket. Add custom metadata to the uploaded images in Cloud Storage that contains the customer's unique ID.

Use a distributed file system to store customers' images. As storage needs increase, add more persistent disks and/or nodes. Assign each customer a unique ID, which sets each file's owner attribute, ensuring privacy of images.

Use a distributed file system to store customers' images. As storage needs increase, add more persistent disks and/or nodes. Use a Google Cloud SQL database to maintain metadata that maps each customer's ID to their image files.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Storage is a managed object store suited to storing and serving image files. Firestore in Datastore mode provides a scalable, high-performance NoSQL store for application data, so it can maintain an efficient customer-ID-to-image-object mapping for fast retrieval at login. Custom object metadata is descriptive data rather than an access-control mechanism; viewing rights must be enforced through the application and Cloud Storage IAM or ACL configuration.

**Learn more:** [Datastore Overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/datastore/docs/concepts/overview?hl=en) · [Cloud Storage Object Metadata](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/metadata?hl=en)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your machine learning (ML) engineers rely on self-hosted Jupyter notebooks for work such as data preparation, model training, and fine-tuning. The operations team subsequently deploys these models across various environments. You want to give ML engineers maximum flexibility, encourage collaboration through a common toolset, and use Google Cloud’s scalability while adhering to Google-recommended practices. What should you do?

options.text: Use AutoML for machine learning and Cloud Deploy for model deployment.
Use Colab Enterprise for machine learning and DevOps for model deployment.
Use Vertex AI for machine learning and machine learning operations (MLOps) for model deployment.
Use TensorFlow for machine learning and Cloud Deploy for model deployment.

questions.explanation:
Vertex AI provides a unified platform for data engineering, data science, and ML engineering workflows, enabling teams to collaborate with a common toolset and use Google Cloud’s scalable infrastructure. Its end-to-end MLOps capabilities support automating and scaling the ML lifecycle, including model deployment and management.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to Vertex AI](https://cloud.google.com/ai-platform/docs?o=7639)

questions.domain: Designing and planning a cloud solution architecture
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],For this item, refer to the Helicopter Racing League (HRL) case study. HRL needs a cost-effective way to store race data, including telemetry. It must retain all historical records, train models using only the prior season’s data, and accommodate growth in both data volume and the information collected. You must propose a data solution. Based on HRL’s business requirements and the objectives stated by CEO S. Hawke, what should you do?

options.text: Use Firestore for its scalable and flexible document-based database. Use collections to aggregate race data by season and event.
Use Cloud Spanner for its scalability and ability to version schemas with zero downtime. Split race data using season as a primary key.
Use BigQuery for its scalability and ability to add columns to a schema. Partition race data based on season.
Use Cloud SQL for its ability to automatically manage storage increases and compatibility with MySQL. Use separate database instances for each season.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery is a scalable analytical data warehouse suited to retaining and querying growing telemetry datasets. Its table schemas can be extended with additional columns as new data attributes are collected. Partitioning race data by season allows model-training queries to filter to the prior season while retaining historical records; partition pruning skips nonmatching partitions, reducing scanned data and query cost.

**Learn more:** [BigQuery: Modifying table schemas](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/managing-table-schemas) · [BigQuery: Introduction to partitioned tables](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/partitioned-tables)

questions.domain: Designing and planning a cloud solution architecture
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your employer, a financial services company, recently acquired a popular fintech startup. The startup's core application is a monolithic Python application running on a managed instance group of Compute Engine virtual machines with one large PostgreSQL database. Your development team faces slow deployment cycles, and the monolithic architecture of the startup's core application makes integrating new ML-powered fraud-detection models difficult. You need a long-term strategy that increases developer agility and positions the company to use Google Cloud's advanced data and AI capabilities for future innovation. What should you do?

options.text: Deploy the ML fraud detection model to a Vertex AI endpoint. Create a REST API for the model and modify the monolithic Python application to call this endpoint for real-time fraud analysis.
Containerize the application, deploy it to Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), and migrate the PostgreSQL database to Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL.
Propose a phased, event-driven migration to a microservices architecture. Use Pub/Sub for asynchronous communication and deploy the fraud models on Vertex AI endpoints.

Migrate the PostgreSQL database to Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL. Replicate the data into BigQuery using Datastream, and then train and deploy the fraud detection models directly within BigQuery using BigQuery ML.

questions.explanation:
A phased migration to microservices lets teams deploy and evolve business capabilities independently instead of releasing a tightly coupled monolith. Pub/Sub provides asynchronous, decoupled event communication between services, allowing fraud-detection and future data consumers to be added without tightly integrating them into the original application. Vertex AI endpoints provide managed online model deployment and prediction serving.

**Learn more:** [What is Pub/Sub?](https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/overview) · [Event-driven architecture with Pub/Sub](https://docs.cloud.google.com/solutions/event-driven-architecture-pubsub)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company is creating a new architecture to support its data-focused business strategy. You are responsible for configuring the network. Your company’s mobile and web-facing applications will be deployed on-premises, while all data analysis will take place in GCP. The plan is to process and load 7 years of archived `.csv` files totaling 900 TB of data, and then continue loading 10 TB of data each day. You currently have an existing 100-MB internet connection.  
  
Which actions will meet your company’s needs?

options.text: Compress and upload both archived files and files uploaded daily using the gsutil ג€

Lease a Transfer Appliance, upload archived files to it, and send it to Google to transfer archived data to Cloud Storage. Establish a connection with Google using a Dedicated Interconnect or Direct Peering connection and use it to upload files daily.

Lease a Transfer Appliance, upload archived files to it, and send it to Google to transfer archived data to Cloud Storage. Establish one Cloud VPN Tunnel to VPC networks over the public internet, and compress and upload files daily using the gsutil ג€

Lease a Transfer Appliance, upload archived files to it, and send it to Google to transfer archived data to Cloud Storage. Establish a Cloud VPN Tunnel to VPC networks over the public internet, and compress and upload files daily.

questions.explanation:
Transfer Appliance is designed to securely ship high-capacity data to Google for upload to Cloud Storage, making it suitable for a 900 TB historical backlog. A 100 Mbps internet connection cannot sustain a 10 TB daily transfer; an enterprise-grade Dedicated Interconnect or Direct Peering connection provides the substantially higher network capacity required for ongoing uploads. A Cloud VPN tunnel over the public internet does not remove the underlying internet-bandwidth limitation.

**Learn more:** [Transfer Appliance overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/transfer-appliance/docs/4.0/overview) · [Cloud Interconnect overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/network-connectivity/docs/interconnect/concepts/overview)

Your development team has built a mobile game app. You want to test the new app on Android and iOS devices across a variety of configurations. You need testing to be efficient and cost-effective. What should you do?

options.text: Upload your mobile app to the Firebase Test Lab, and test the mobile app on Android and iOS devices.
Create Android and iOS VMs on Google Cloud, install the mobile app on the VMs, and test the mobile app.
Create Android and iOS containers on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), install the mobile app on the containers, and test the mobile app.
Upload your mobile app with different configurations to Firebase Hosting and test each configuration.

questions.explanation:
Firebase Test Lab provides managed cloud testing for Android and iOS apps across a range of devices and configurations, including device models, OS versions, locales, and orientations. This makes it the appropriate scalable, cost-effective mobile testing service.

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company stores sensitive data in Cloud Storage buckets. Data analysts have Identity and Access Management (IAM) permissions to read those buckets. You need to prevent data analysts from retrieving bucket data when they are outside the office network. What should you do?

options.text: 1. Create a VPC Service Controls perimeter that includes the projects with the buckets. 2. Create an access level with the CIDR of the office network.
1. Create a firewall rule for all instances in the Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) network for source range. 2. Use the Classless Inter-domain Routing (CIDR) of the office network.

1. Create a Cloud Function to remove IAM permissions from the buckets, and another Cloud Function to add IAM permissions to the buckets. 2. Schedule the Cloud Functions with Cloud Scheduler to add permissions at the start of business and remove permissions at the end of business.
1. Create a Cloud VPN to the office network. 2. Configure Private Google Access for on-premises hosts.

questions.explanation:
VPC Service Controls provides a context-based security perimeter for Cloud Storage that is independent of IAM. Applying an access level based on the office network’s public CIDR range to the perimeter allows authorized requests from that network while denying otherwise authorized requests originating outside it.

**Learn more:** [Allow access to protected resources from outside a perimeter](https://cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/use-access-levels) · [Design access levels](https://cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/access-level-design)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],TerramEarth has outfitted all connected trucks with servers and sensors that collect telemetry data. Next year, they intend to use the data to train machine-learning models. They want to store this data in the cloud while lowering costs.  
  
What should they do?

options.text: Have the vehicle's computer compress the data in hourly snapshots, and store it in a Google Cloud Storage (GCS) Nearline bucket
Push the telemetry data in real-time to a streaming dataflow job that compresses the data, and store it in Google BigQuery
Push the telemetry data in real-time to a streaming dataflow job that compresses the data, and store it in Cloud Bigtable
Have the vehicle's computer compress the data in hourly snapshots, and store it in a GCS Coldline bucket

questions.explanation:
Cloud Storage Coldline is a very-low-cost, durable storage class for infrequently accessed data and is intended for data read or modified no more than once per quarter. Retaining compressed telemetry snapshots for model training the following year satisfies its 90-day minimum storage duration and minimizes at-rest storage cost compared with Nearline. [Google Cloud Storage classes](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/storage-classes)

**Learn more:** [Cloud Storage storage classes](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/storage-classes)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company operates nationwide and intends to use GCP for several batch workloads, including some that are not time-critical. You must also use HIPAA-certified GCP services and manage service costs.  
  
How should you design the solution to follow Google best practices?

options.text: Provision preemptible VMs to reduce cost. Discontinue use of all GCP services and APIs that are not HIPAA-compliant.
Provision preemptible VMs to reduce cost. Disable and then discontinue use of all GCP services and APIs that are not HIPAA-compliant.
Provision standard VMs in the same region to reduce cost. Discontinue use of all GCP services and APIs that are not HIPAA-compliant.
Provision standard VMs to the same region to reduce cost. Disable and then discontinue use of all GCP services and APIs that are not HIPAA-compliant.

questions.explanation:
Preemptible VMs provide substantially lower-cost compute and are appropriate for fault-tolerant, interruptible batch workloads. For HIPAA workloads involving PHI, Google Cloud instructs customers to disable or otherwise ensure they do not use products that are not explicitly covered by the Business Associate Agreement; disabling and discontinuing such services meets that control.

**Learn more:** [HIPAA Compliance on Google Cloud](https://cloud.google.com/security/compliance/hipaa) · [Preemptible VM instances](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instances/preemptible?hl=en)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A production database virtual machine on Google Compute Engine uses an ext4-formatted persistent disk for its data files. The database is about to exhaust its available storage.  
  
How can you resolve this issue with the least downtime?

options.text: In the Cloud Platform Console, increase the size of the persistent disk and use the resize2fs command in Linux.
Shut down the virtual machine, use the Cloud Platform Console to increase the persistent disk size, then restart the virtual machine
In the Cloud Platform Console, increase the size of the persistent disk and verify the new space is ready to use with the fdisk command in Linux
In the Cloud Platform Console, create a new persistent disk attached to the virtual machine, format and mount it, and configure the database service to move the files to the new disk
In the Cloud Platform Console, create a snapshot of the persistent disk restore the snapshot to a new larger disk, unmount the old disk, mount the new disk and restart the database service

questions.explanation:
A Google Compute Engine Persistent Disk can be increased while it remains attached to a running VM. An ext4 data filesystem must then be extended with `resize2fs` to make the added capacity usable, avoiding the downtime of shutting down the VM or migrating data to another disk.

**Learn more:** [Change the size of a Persistent Disk](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/disks/resize-persistent-disk)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],For this question, use the Dress4Win case study. Given the stated business requirements, how would you automate deployment of the web and transactional data layers?

options.text: Deploy Nginx and Tomcat using Cloud Deployment Manager to Compute Engine. Deploy a Cloud SQL server to replace MySQL. Deploy Jenkins using Cloud Deployment Manager.
Deploy Nginx and Tomcat using Cloud Launcher. Deploy a MySQL server using Cloud Launcher. Deploy Jenkins to Compute Engine using Cloud Deployment Manager scripts.
Migrate Nginx and Tomcat to App Engine. Deploy a Cloud Datastore server to replace the MySQL server in a high-availability configuration. Deploy Jenkins to Compute Engine using Cloud Launcher.
Migrate Nginx and Tomcat to App Engine. Deploy a MySQL server using Cloud Launcher. Deploy Jenkins to Compute Engine using Cloud Launcher.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Deployment Manager provides repeatable, version-controlled infrastructure-as-code, matching Dress4Win's stated need to automate provisioning; deploying Nginx and Tomcat on Compute Engine and replacing the on-premises MySQL server with the fully managed Cloud SQL service directly satisfies the transactional-data-layer migration. Cloud Datastore is a NoSQL service and cannot be a drop-in MySQL replacement, and Cloud Launcher does not provide the automation/deployment-as-code capability the requirements call for.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Deployment Manager overview](https://cloud.google.com/deployment-manager/docs)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An application is deployed on Anthos clusters (previously Anthos GKE). Under your company’s SRE practices, you must receive an alert when request latency exceeds a specified threshold for a defined period. What should you do?

options.text: Install Anthos Service Mesh on your cluster. Use the Google Cloud Console to define a Service Level Objective (SLO), and create an alerting policy based on this SLO.
Enable the Cloud Trace API on your project, and use Cloud Monitoring Alerts to send an alert based on the Cloud Trace metrics.

Use Cloud Profiler to follow up the request latency. Create a custom metric in Cloud Monitoring based on the results of Cloud Profiler, and create an Alerting policy in case this metric exceeds the threshold.
Configure Anthos Config Management on your cluster, and create a yaml file that defines the SLO and alerting policy you want to deploy in your cluster.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Service Mesh (formerly Anthos Service Mesh) supports latency service-level objectives based on service telemetry. A latency SLO defines the latency threshold and compliance period, and Cloud Monitoring can create an alerting policy from that SLO so alerts reflect the service’s SRE objective.

**Learn more:** [Creating SLOs — Cloud Service Mesh](https://docs.cloud.google.com/service-mesh/docs/observability/create-slo) · [Creating an alerting policy for an SLO — Cloud Service Mesh](https://docs.cloud.google.com/service-mesh/docs/observability/alert-policy-slo)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company runs an application across multiple Compute Engine instances. You must ensure that the application can communicate with an on-premises service over internal IPs with high throughput and minimal latency. What should you do?

options.text: Use OpenVPN to configure a VPN tunnel between the on-premises environment and Google Cloud.
Configure a direct peering connection between the on-premises environment and Google Cloud.
Use Cloud VPN to configure a VPN tunnel between the on-premises environment and Google Cloud.
Configure a Cloud Dedicated Interconnect connection between the on-premises environment and Google Cloud.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Dedicated Interconnect supplies a direct physical connection between the on-premises network and Google’s network, avoiding the public internet and providing scalable, high-capacity, low-latency connectivity to VPC resources through VLAN attachments and Cloud Router.

**Learn more:** [Dedicated Interconnect overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/network-connectivity/docs/interconnect/concepts/dedicated-overview) · [Cloud Interconnect overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/network-connectivity/docs/interconnect/concepts/overview?hl=en)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A Compute Engine managed instance group has an outage: every instance restarts after 5 seconds. A health check is configured, but autoscaling is disabled. Your Linux-expert colleague has offered to investigate the problem. You need to ensure that he can access the VMs. What should you do?

options.text: Grant your colleague the IAM role of project Viewer
Perform a rolling restart on the instance group
Disable the health check for the instance group. Add his SSH key to the project-wide SSH Keys
Disable autoscaling for the instance group. Add his SSH key to the project-wide SSH Keys

questions.explanation:
A managed instance group uses an application health check for autohealing; an unhealthy VM can be repaired by recreating it. Removing or disabling that health-check autohealing prevents the rapid replacement cycle so the VM can be investigated. For VMs using metadata-based SSH access, a public key in project metadata permits SSH access to all project VMs unless project-wide SSH keys are blocked.

**Learn more:** [Set up an application-based health check and autohealing](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instance-groups/autohealing-instances-in-migs?hl=en) · [Add SSH keys to VMs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/connect/add-ssh-keys?hl=en)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has a Google Workspace account and a Google Cloud Organization. Some company developers have created Google Cloud projects outside the Google Cloud Organization.  
  
You want to design an Organization structure that lets developers create projects while preventing them from modifying production projects. You want to manage policies centrally for all projects and apply more restrictive policies to production projects.  
  
You want to minimize disruption to users and developers as business needs change in the future. You want to follow Google-recommended practices. How should you design the Organization structure?

options.text: 1. Create a second Google Workspace account and Organization. 2. Grant all developers the Project Creator IAM role on the new Organization. 3. Move the developer projects into the new Organization. 4. Set the policies for all projects on both Organizations. 5. Additionally, set the production policies on the original Organization.

1. Create a folder under the Organization resource named ג€Production.ג€ 2. Grant all developers the Project Creator IAM role on the new Organization. 3. Move the developer projects into the new Organization. 4. Set the policies for all projects on the Organization. 5. Additionally, set the production policies on the ג€Productionג€ folder.

1. Create folders under the Organization resource named ג€Developmentג€ and ג€Production.ג€ 2. Grant all developers the Project Creator IAM role on the ג€Developmentג€ folder. 3. Move the developer projects into the ג€Developmentג€ folder. 4. Set the policies for all projects on the Organization. 5. Additionally, set the production policies on the ג€Productionג€ folder.

1. Designate the Organization for production projects only. 2. Ensure that developers do not have the Project Creator IAM role on the Organization. 3. Create development projects outside of the Organization using the developer Google Workspace accounts. 4. Set the policies for all projects on the Organization. 5. Additionally, set the production policies on the individual production projects.

questions.explanation:
Folders provide hierarchy levels for grouping projects and applying IAM and Organization Policy controls. Granting Project Creator on the Development folder allows developers to create projects in that folder without granting project-creation access in Production. Policies attached to the Organization apply to descendant projects, while policies attached to the Production folder can impose stricter controls on its projects. Moving developer projects into the Development folder places them under centralized governance.

**Learn more:** [About resource hierarchy](https://cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/cloud-platform-resource-hierarchy) · [Manage projects within folders](https://cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/manage-projects-within-folder)

You must design a solution for global load balancing based on the requested URL path. You must ensure operational reliability and end-to-end in-transit encryption in accordance with Google best practices.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create a cross-region load balancer with URL Maps.
Create an HTTPS load balancer with URL Maps.
Create appropriate instance groups and instances. Configure SSL proxy load balancing.
Create a global forwarding rule. Configure SSL proxy load balancing.

questions.explanation:
An HTTPS Application Load Balancer provides global load balancing, terminates HTTPS using TLS certificates, and uses a URL map to route HTTP(S) requests to different backends according to URL paths. SSL proxy load balancing operates at Layer 4 and cannot make URL-path routing decisions.

**Learn more:** [External Application Load Balancer overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/load-balancing/docs/https) · [URL maps overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/load-balancing/docs/url-map-concepts)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company plans to perform a lift-and-shift migration of its Linux RHEL 6.5+ virtual machines. The virtual machines run in an on-premises VMware environment. You want to migrate them to Compute Engine by following Google-recommended practices. What should you do?

options.text: 1. Define a migration plan based on the list of the applications and their dependencies. 2. Migrate all virtual machines into Compute Engine individually with Migrate for Compute Engine.

1. Perform an assessment of virtual machines running in the current VMware environment. 2. Create images of all disks. Import disks on Compute Engine. 3. Create standard virtual machines where the boot disks are the ones you have imported.
1. Perform an assessment of virtual machines running in the current VMware environment. 2. Define a migration plan, prepare a Migrate for Compute Engine migration RunBook, and execute the migration.

1. Perform an assessment of virtual machines running in the current VMware environment. 2. Install a third-party agent on all selected virtual machines. 3. Migrate all virtual machines into Compute Engine.

questions.explanation:
Google’s VM migration lifecycle calls for assessing the source environment and workloads, planning the migration, and deploying the VMs to Compute Engine with Migrate to Virtual Machines. This service is designed for lift-and-shift migration of VMware vSphere VMs and supports replication, testing, and final cutover; a migration runbook helps execute that planned migration consistently.

**Learn more:** [Migration journey with Migrate to Virtual Machines](https://docs.cloud.google.com/migrate/virtual-machines/docs/5.0/discover/migrating-vms-migrate-for-compute-engine-getting-started) · [VM migration process](https://docs.cloud.google.com/migrate/virtual-machines/docs/5.0/discover/lifecycle)

options.text: Google Cloud Dedicated Interconnect
Google Cloud VPN connected to the data center network
A NAT and TLS translation gateway installed on-premises
A Google Compute Engine instance with a VPN server installed connected to the data center network

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud Dedicated Interconnect provides direct private connectivity between an on-premises network and Google’s network and is designed to transfer large data volumes. Its high-capacity links are suitable for continuous replication of a 4 TB database with frequent large updates, whereas Cloud VPN tunnels have substantially lower per-tunnel bandwidth.

Your company has a Google Cloud project that uses BigQuery for data warehousing with pay-per-use pricing. You need to monitor queries in real time to identify the most expensive queries and the users who spend the most. What should you do?

options.text: 1. In the BigQuery dataset that contains all the tables to be queried, add a label for each user that can launch a query. 2. Open the Billing page of the project. 3. Select Reports. 4. Select BigQuery as the product and filter by the user you want to check.
1. Create a Cloud Logging sink to export BigQuery data access logs to BigQuery. 2. Perform a BigQuery query on the generated table to extract the information you need.
1. Create a Cloud Logging sink to export BigQuery data access logs to Cloud Storage. 2. Develop a Dataflow pipeline to compute the cost of queries split by users.
1. Activate billing export into BigQuery. 2. Perform a BigQuery query on the billing table to extract the information you need.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery audit logs record user activity, including jobs and queries. Exporting the relevant BigQuery Data Access logs to a BigQuery dataset through a Cloud Logging sink makes the log data available for SQL analysis by submitting user and billed query volume. Cloud Billing exports are intended for billing analysis and have variable reporting and export latency, so they do not provide the required real-time, per-user query monitoring.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to audit logs in BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/introduction-audit-workloads) · [Route logs to supported destinations](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/export/configure_export_v2)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],For this question, refer to the KnightMotives Automotive case study. KnightMotives manages supplier data and pricing in a central MySQL database at headquarters (HQ). Only HQ personnel are permitted to modify the data. Each local plant maintains a copy of the data in its own MySQL database, often with a different database schema or version. Every night, a batch job exports any product or price changes from the central HQ database in XML format and stores the updated data on a central FTP server. Each local plant must download this XML file and update its local system with the new information. Data retained by some plants has become inconsistent with the source data because of XML parsing issues. HQ wants to easily confirm that every change is applied correctly at each plant.

A large enterprise is developing a file-processing pipeline on Google Cloud. The pipeline receives raw files that a fleet of hundreds of Compute Engine virtual machines (VMs) in one region subsequently accesses for parallel processing. These VMs require concurrent, low-latency read and write access to a shared file system. You must implement a storage solution that provides the highest possible throughput to reduce the total processing time. What should you do?

options.text: Use a multi-region Cloud Storage bucket to store the files.
Create a Filestore Enterprise instance in the same region as the VMs. Mount the Filestore file share on each Compute Engine VM.
Create a Filestore Zonal instance in each zone where the VMs are running. Mount the Filestore file share on each Compute Engine VM.
Create a Regional Persistent Disk and attach it to all VMs in multi-writer mode.

questions.explanation:
A Filestore Enterprise instance is a managed regional NFS file share that Compute Engine VMs can mount concurrently, providing a single shared file system with low-latency access. This meets the requirement for hundreds of VMs across one region, unlike object storage, separate zonal file systems, or multi-writer block storage that requires specialized coordination and is not intended as a directly shared general-purpose file system.

**Learn more:** [About instance performance | Filestore](https://docs.cloud.google.com/filestore/docs/performance) · [Persistent Disk | Compute Engine](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/disks/persistent-disks?hl=en)

Your company has recently acquired another company with infrastructure in Google Cloud. Each company has its own Google Cloud organization. Both companies use a Shared Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) to provide network connectivity for their applications. Some subnets used by the two companies overlap. To integrate both businesses, the applications need private network connectivity. These applications are not on overlapping subnets. You want to provide connectivity with minimal re-engineering. What should you do?

options.text: Set up VPC peering and peer each Shared VPC together.
Migrate the projects from the acquired company into your company's Google Cloud organization. Re-launch the instances in your companies Shared VPC.
Set up a Cloud VPN gateway in each Shared VPC and peer Cloud VPNs.
Configure SSH port forwarding on each application to provide connectivity between applications in the different Shared VPCs.

questions.explanation:
VPC Network Peering rejects peering configurations when subnet IP ranges overlap. Cloud VPN provides an IPsec connection between VPC networks and can be configured to carry traffic only for the non-overlapping application subnet ranges that require connectivity, avoiding an address-renumbering or instance-redeployment effort.

**Learn more:** [VPC Network Peering](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/vpc-peering?hl=en) · [Cloud VPN overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/network-connectivity/docs/vpn/concepts/overview)
