lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your architecture requires centralized collection, within your project, of all administrator activity and VM system logs.  
  
How should you collect logs from both VMs and services?

options.text: All admin and VM system logs are automatically collected by Stackdriver.
Stackdriver automatically collects admin activity logs for most services. The Stackdriver Logging agent must be installed on each instance to collect system logs.
Launch a custom syslogd compute instance and configure your GCP project and VMs to forward all logs to it.
Install the Stackdriver Logging agent on a single compute instance and let it collect all audit and access logs for your environment.

questions.explanation:
Admin Activity audit logs are automatically generated for Google Cloud services that provide audit logging. VM operating-system logs must be sent from each VM by a logging agent; the legacy Stackdriver Logging agent streams those system logs to Cloud Logging. The current preferred replacement for new workloads is the Ops Agent, which likewise runs on each Compute Engine instance.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Audit Logs overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/audit?hl=en) · [Google Cloud Observability agents](https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/agent)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company uses Google Cloud. Under the Organization, you have two folders: Finance and Shopping. Development-team members belong to a Google Group, and that development-team group has the Project Owner role assigned at the Organization level. You need to prevent the development team from creating resources in projects within the Finance folder. What should you do?

options.text: Assign the development team group the Project Viewer role on the Finance folder, and assign the development team group the Project Owner role on the Shopping folder.
Assign the development team group only the Project Viewer role on the Finance folder.
Assign the development team group the Project Owner role on the Shopping folder, and remove the development team group Project Owner role from the Organization.
Assign the development team group only the Project Owner role on the Shopping folder.

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud IAM allow-policy bindings inherit down the resource hierarchy, and the effective allow policy is the union of inherited and locally assigned roles. A Viewer role on Finance cannot override an Owner role inherited from the Organization. Remove the group’s Organization-level Owner binding and assign Owner only on the Shopping folder, so the role applies to Shopping projects but not Finance projects.

**Learn more:** [Using resource hierarchy for access control](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/resource-hierarchy-access-control) · [Understanding allow policies](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/allow-policies)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A BigQuery project contains several users. For auditing, you need to determine how many queries each user executed during the past month. What should you do?

options.text: Connect Google Data Studio to BigQuery. Create a dimension for the users and a metric for the amount of queries per user.
In the BigQuery interface, execute a query on the JOBS table to get the required information.
Use 'bq show' to list all jobs. Per job, use 'bq ls' to list job information and get the required information.
Use Cloud Audit Logging to view Cloud Audit Logs, and create a filter on the query operation to get the required information.

questions.explanation:
The project-level `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS` view contains metadata for all BigQuery jobs in a project, including `user_email`, `creation_time`, and `job_type`. Filtering it to last-month `QUERY` jobs and grouping by `user_email` produces the per-user query counts; its job history retention covers the requested period.

**Learn more:** [BigQuery INFORMATION_SCHEMA JOBS view](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/information-schema-jobs)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are migrating an application that uses MySQL from on-premises to Google Cloud. The application will run on Compute Engine and use Cloud SQL. You want to cut over to the Compute Engine deployment with minimal downtime and without customer data loss. You also want to migrate the application with minimal modifications and determine the cutover strategy.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: 1. Set up Cloud VPN to provide private network connectivity between the Compute Engine application and the on-premises MySQL server. 2. Stop the on-premises application. 3. Create a mysqldump of the on-premises MySQL server. 4. Upload the dump to a Cloud Storage bucket. 5. Import the dump into Cloud SQL. 6. Modify the source code of the application to write queries to both databases and read from its local database. 7. Start the Compute Engine application. 8. Stop the on-premises application.

1. Set up Cloud SQL proxy and MySQL proxy. 2. Create a mysqldump of the on-premises MySQL server. 3. Upload the dump to a Cloud Storage bucket. 4. Import the dump into Cloud SQL. 5. Stop the on-premises application. 6. Start the Compute Engine application.

1. Set up Cloud VPN to provide private network connectivity between the Compute Engine application and the on-premises MySQL server. 2. Stop the on-premises application. 3. Start the Compute Engine application, configured to read and write to the on-premises MySQL server. 4. Create the replication configuration in Cloud SQL. 5. Configure the source database server to accept connections from the Cloud SQL replica. 6. Finalize the Cloud SQL replica configuration. 7. When replication has been completed, stop the Compute Engine application. 8. Promote the Cloud SQL replica to a standalone instance. 9. Restart the Compute Engine application, configured to read and write to the Cloud SQL standalone instance.

1. Stop the on-premises application. 2. Create a mysqldump of the on-premises MySQL server. 3. Upload the dump to a Cloud Storage bucket. 4. Import the dump into Cloud SQL. 5. Start the application on Compute Engine.

questions.explanation:
Cloud SQL replication from an external MySQL server is designed to migrate self-managed MySQL data to Google Cloud with minimal downtime. Keeping the Compute Engine application connected to the on-premises database while Cloud SQL replicates preserves normal writes; after replication catches up, stopping the application, promoting the Cloud SQL replica to a standalone primary, and repointing the application provides a short, controlled cutover without data loss.

**Learn more:** [About replicating from an external server | Cloud SQL for MySQL](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/mysql/replication/external-server) · [Configure Cloud SQL and the external server for replication | Cloud SQL for MySQL](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/mysql/replication/configure-replication-from-external?hl=en)

You have an App Engine application that requires an update. You want to test the update using production traffic before it replaces the current application version.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Deploy the update using the Instance Group Updater to create a partial rollout, which allows for canary testing.
Deploy the update as a new version in the App Engine application, and split traffic between the new and current versions.
Deploy the update in a new VPC, and use Google's global HTTP load balancing to split traffic between the update and current applications.
Deploy the update as a new App Engine application, and use Google's global HTTP load balancing to split traffic between the new and current applications.

questions.explanation:
App Engine can run multiple versions of a service and split a specified percentage of traffic among them. Deploying the update as a new version and splitting traffic with the current version enables a controlled production rollout before the new version becomes the primary version.

**Learn more:** [Splitting traffic | App Engine standard environment](https://docs.cloud.google.com/appengine/docs/standard/splitting-traffic)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You want to configure your running Google Kubernetes Engine cluster to scale as demand for your application varies.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Add additional nodes to your Kubernetes Engine cluster using the following command: gcloud container clusters resize CLUSTER_Name ג€
Add a tag to the instances in the cluster with the following command: gcloud compute instances add-tags INSTANCE - -tags enable- autoscaling max-nodes-10
Update the existing Kubernetes Engine cluster with the following command: gcloud alpha container clusters update mycluster - -enable- autoscaling - -min-nodes=1 - -max-nodes=10
Create a new Kubernetes Engine cluster with the following command: gcloud alpha container clusters create mycluster - -enable- autoscaling - -min-nodes=1 - -max-nodes=10 and redeploy your application

questions.explanation:
GKE cluster autoscaling automatically adjusts node-pool capacity in response to workload demand within configured minimum and maximum node limits. Enabling autoscaling on the existing cluster with `--enable-autoscaling`, `--min-nodes`, and `--max-nodes` provides this behavior without manually resizing nodes or recreating the cluster.

**Learn more:** [Autoscaling a cluster | Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE)](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/cluster-autoscaler) · [gcloud container clusters update | Google Cloud SDK](https://cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/container/clusters/update)

Refer to the KnightMotives Automotive case study. KnightMotives has created a new car configurator application to improve both the dealer and customer experience. The new application will run on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). KnightMotives wants to replicate the application's deployment across multiple locations so this critical application remains available on the internet, even during regional outages. What should you do?

options.text: Create multiple GKE clusters in different regions. Deploy part of the microservices of the app in different clusters. Configure a multi-cluster Cloud Service Mesh.
Create multiple GKE clusters in different regions. Deploy the app on every cluster. Configure a multi-cluster Cloud Service Mesh.
Create a fleet of GKE clusters in different regions Deploy part of the microservices of the app in different clusters Configure a multi-cluster Gateway.
Create a fleet of GKE clusters in different regions. Deploy the app on every cluster. Configure a multi-cluster Gateway.

questions.explanation:
A GKE fleet with the complete application deployed in each regional cluster provides redundant healthy backends if a region fails. Multi-cluster Gateway uses Google Cloud global load-balancing infrastructure to provide one external entry point and route traffic to healthy Pods across the fleet.

**Learn more:** [About multi-cluster Gateways](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/multi-cluster-gateways) · [Migrate to multi-cluster networking with GKE](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/migrate-gke-multi-cluster)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company is migrating 75 TB of data to Google Cloud. You want to use Cloud Storage while following Google-recommended practices. What should you do?

options.text: Move your data onto a Transfer Appliance. Use a Transfer Appliance Rehydrator to decrypt the data into Cloud Storage.
Move your data onto a Transfer Appliance. Use Cloud Dataprep to decrypt the data into Cloud Storage.
Install gsutil on each server that contains data. Use resumable transfers to upload the data into Cloud Storage.
Install gsutil on each server containing data. Use streaming transfers to upload the data into Cloud Storage.

questions.explanation:
For large on-premises data migrations, Transfer Appliance is a Google-recommended option. The Transfer Appliance Rehydrator restores and decrypts the appliance-captured data into Cloud Storage; Cloud Dataprep is not a Transfer Appliance decryption tool.

**Learn more:** [Data transfer options | Google Cloud](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage-transfer/docs/transfer-options) · [Transfer Appliance release notes | Google Cloud](https://docs.cloud.google.com/transfer-appliance/docs/release-notes)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You operate a Python web application with many dependencies that needs **0.1 CPU cores** and **128 MB of memory** in production. You want to monitor and maximize machine utilization, while also reliably deploying new versions of the application. Which set of steps should you take?

options.text: Perform the following: 1. Create a managed instance group with f1-micro type machines. 2. Use a startup script to clone the repository, check out the production branch, install the dependencies, and start the Python app. 3. Restart the instances to automatically deploy new production releases.

Perform the following: 1. Create a managed instance group with n1-standard-1 type machines. 2. Build a Compute Engine image from the production branch that contains all of the dependencies and automatically starts the Python app. 3. Rebuild the Compute Engine image, and update the instance template to deploy new production releases.

Perform the following: 1. Create a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster with n1-standard-1 type machines. 2. Build a Docker image from the production branch with all of the dependencies, and tag it with the version number. 3. Create a Kubernetes Deployment with the imagePullPolicy set to 'IfNotPresent' in the staging namespace, and then promote it to the production namespace after testing.

Perform the following: 1. Create a GKE cluster with n1-standard-4 type machines. 2. Build a Docker image from the master branch with all of the dependencies, and tag it with 'latest'. 3. Create a Kubernetes Deployment in the default namespace with the imagePullPolicy set to 'Always'. Restart the pods to automatically deploy new production releases.

questions.explanation:
GKE improves machine utilization by scheduling containerized workloads onto shared cluster nodes rather than dedicating a VM to this very small application. An immutable, version-tagged image packages the application and all dependencies, and the same tested image can be promoted from staging to production. Google recommends building an image once and promoting it through environments so that the tested artifact is the one deployed to production.

**Learn more:** [Best practices for continuous integration and delivery to GKE](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/best-practices-continuous-integration-delivery-kubernetes) · [Deploying a stateless Linux application to GKE](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/stateless-apps)

questions.question: For this question, refer to the Altostrat Media case study. Altostrat has fluctuating compute demands for its batch processing jobs. The jobs are not time-critical and can tolerate occasional interruptions. You need to optimize cloud costs while meeting the batch-processing requirements. What should you do?

options.text: Configure reserved VM instances
Deploy spot VM instances.
Set up standard VM instances.
Use Cloud Run functions.

questions.explanation:
Spot VMs provide substantially discounted Compute Engine capacity and are designed for fault-tolerant batch workloads that can tolerate preemption. Their possible interruption is acceptable for non-time-critical jobs, while their lower price optimizes compute cost.\
\
**Learn more:** [Spot VMs — Compute Engine documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instances/spot?hl=en)

questions.question: For this question, refer to the Altostrat Media case study. Altostrat has fluctuating compute demands for its batch processing jobs. The jobs are not time-critical and can tolerate occasional interruptions. You need to optimize cloud costs while meeting the batch-processing requirements. What should you do?

options.text: 1. Use Linux shasum to compute a digest of files you want to upload. 2. Use gsutil -m to upload all the files to Cloud Storage. 3. Use gsutil cp to download the uploaded files. 4. Use Linux shasum to compute a digest of the downloaded files. 5. Compare the hashes.

1. Use gsutil -m to upload the files to Cloud Storage. 2. Develop a custom Java application that computes CRC32C hashes. 3. Use gsutil ls -L gs://[YOUR_BUCKET_NAME] to collect CRC32C hashes of the uploaded files. 4. Compare the hashes.
1. Use gsutil -m to upload all the files to Cloud Storage. 2. Use gsutil cp to download the uploaded files. 3. Use Linux diff to compare the content of the files.

1. Use gsutil -m to upload the files to Cloud Storage. 2. Use gsutil hash -c FILE_NAME to generate CRC32C hashes of all on-premises files. 3. Use gsutil ls -L gs://[YOUR_BUCKET_NAME] to collect CRC32C hashes of the uploaded files. 4. Compare the hashes.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Storage maintains a CRC32C checksum for every object. Computing CRC32C hashes for the on-premises files and comparing them with the uploaded objects’ CRC32C metadata verifies data integrity without incurring the time and retrieval cost of downloading the files or developing a custom hashing application.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A recent audit found that a new network was created in your GCP project. A GCE instance in this network has its SSH port exposed to the internet. You want to determine the origin of this network.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Search for Create VM entry in the Stackdriver alerting console
Navigate to the Activity page in the Home section. Set category to Data Access and search for Create VM entry
In the Logging section of the console, specify GCE Network as the logging section. Search for the Create Insert entry
Connect to the GCE instance using project SSH keys. Identify previous logins in system logs, and match these with the project owners list

questions.explanation:
Creating a VPC network generates a Compute Engine Admin Activity audit log for `v1.compute.networks.insert`. The audit entry records the authenticated principal and operation details, so filtering Cloud Logging for the GCE Network creation/insert event identifies who created the network.

**Learn more:** [Virtual Private Cloud audit logging](https://cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/audit-logging) · [Compute Engine audit logging](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/logging/audit-logging)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],The application reliability team at your company has added a debug feature to its backend service that sends all server events to Google Cloud Storage for later analysis. The event records are at least 50 KB and at most 15 MB, and they are expected to peak at 3,000 events per second. You want to minimize data loss.  
  
Which process should you implement?

options.text: ג€¢ Append metadata to file body ג€¢ Compress individual files ג€¢ Name files with serverName ג€
ג€¢ Batch every 10,000 events with a single manifest file for metadata ג€¢ Compress event files and manifest file into a single archive file ג€¢ Name files using serverName ג€
ג€¢ Compress individual files ג€¢ Name files with serverName ג€
ג€¢ Append metadata to file body ג€¢ Compress individual files ג€¢ Name files with a random prefix pattern ג€¢ Save files to one bucket

questions.explanation:
Storing each event as a separate compressed object limits the loss from any individual failed upload. Including metadata in the object body ensures it is persisted with the event in the same write operation. Randomized object-name prefixes distribute high-volume writes more evenly; Cloud Storage recommends avoiding sequential names at high request rates because they can constrain performance.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Storage request rate and access distribution guidelines](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/request-rate) · [Cloud Storage object quotas and limits](https://cloud.google.com/storage/quotas)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A financial-services company is retiring one of its on-premises data centers. As part of this effort, it must perform a one-time migration of 500 ТВ of historical transaction archives to a Cloud Storage bucket for long-term retention.  
  
The data center’s 1 Gbps internet egress is shared with critical business operations. You must complete the secure data transfer within a 60-day window to meet the decommissioning deadline. What should you do?

options.text: Provision a Partner Interconnect connection with a 10 Gbps capacity to accelerate the data transfer, and then use Storage Transfer Service.
Write a script that uses the gcloud storage cp --parallel command to upload the data in chunks over the public internet during off-peak hours.
Use Storage Transfer Service to create an agent-based transfer job that moves the data from the on-premises file servers directly to the Cloud Storage bucket.
Order a Transfer Appliance, copy the data to the appliance using your high-speed local network, and ship it back to Google to upload the data into your Cloud Storage bucket.

questions.explanation:
Transfer Appliance is designed for large on-premises transfers when available network bandwidth is limited or cannot safely meet the required deadline. Copying the archives to the appliance over the high-speed local network and shipping it to Google avoids saturating the shared 1 Gbps internet connection; Google then uploads the data to the Cloud Storage bucket. A 500 ТВ online transfer at 1 Gbps would consume nearly the entire 60-day period even at uninterrupted theoretical throughput.

**Learn more:** [Data transfer options | Storage Transfer Service](https://cloud.google.com/storage-transfer/docs/transfer-options) · [Migrate to Google Cloud: Transfer your large datasets](https://cloud.google.com/architecture/migration-to-google-cloud-transferring-your-large-datasets)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You want your Google Kubernetes Engine cluster to automatically add or remove nodes according to CPU load.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Configure a HorizontalPodAutoscaler with a target CPU usage. Enable the Cluster Autoscaler from the GCP Console.
Configure a HorizontalPodAutoscaler with a target CPU usage. Enable autoscaling on the managed instance group for the cluster using the gcloud command.
Create a deployment and set the maxUnavailable and maxSurge properties. Enable the Cluster Autoscaler using the gcloud command.
Create a deployment and set the maxUnavailable and maxSurge properties. Enable autoscaling on the cluster managed instance group from the GCP Console.

questions.explanation:
A HorizontalPodAutoscaler uses a target CPU utilization to adjust the number of workload Pods. GKE Cluster Autoscaler adjusts node-pool capacity to accommodate Pods that cannot be scheduled and can remove unneeded nodes. Together, they provide workload scaling based on CPU and corresponding automatic node scaling.

**Learn more:** [Horizontal Pod autoscaling | Google Kubernetes Engine](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/horizontalpodautoscaler) · [Autoscaling a cluster | Google Kubernetes Engine](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/cluster-autoscaler)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Refer to the EHR Healthcare case study. You are responsible for ensuring that EHR's Google Cloud usage passes an upcoming privacy compliance audit. What should you do? (Choose two.)

options.text: Verify EHR's product usage against the list of compliant products on the Google Cloud compliance page.
Advise EHR to execute a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) with Google Cloud.
Use Firebase Authentication for EHR's user facing applications.
Implement Prometheus to detect and prevent security breaches on EHR's web-based applications.
Use GKE private clusters for all Kubernetes workloads.

questions.explanation:
For HIPAA-regulated workloads that handle protected health information, the customer must execute a Google Cloud Business Associate Agreement (BAA) and ensure that it uses only Google Cloud products covered by that agreement. Verifying product usage against the covered-products list and executing the BAA directly address these compliance requirements.

**Learn more:** [HIPAA Compliance on Google Cloud](https://cloud.google.com/security/compliance/hipaa) · [HIPAA - Compliance](https://cloud.google.com/security/compliance/hipaa-compliance?hl=en)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You developed a non-critical update for an application running in a managed instance group and created a new instance template containing the update that you want to release. To avoid any possible effect on the application, you do not want to update any running instances. You want all new instances created by the managed instance group to include the new update. What should you do?

options.text: Start a new rolling restart operation.
Start a new rolling replace operation.
Start a new rolling update. Select the Proactive update mode.
Start a new rolling update. Select the Opportunistic update mode.

questions.explanation:
An opportunistic update changes the managed instance group’s desired configuration without proactively updating existing instances. The group applies the new instance template when new instances are created, while proactive updates automatically roll the configuration out to existing VMs.

**Learn more:** [Automatically apply VM configuration updates in a MIG](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instance-groups/rolling-out-updates-to-managed-instance-groups)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Compute Engine application that you want to autoscale when total memory utilization rises above 80%. You installed the Cloud Monitoring agent and configured the autoscaling policy as follows:  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783775678762-ip04grq4.png)  
  
You notice that the application does not scale during high load. You want to fix this. What should you do?

options.text: Change the Target type to DELTA_PER_MINUTE.
Change the Metric identifier to agent.googleapis.com/memory/bytes_used.
Change the filter to metric.label.state = ‘used’.
Change the filter to metric.label.state = ‘free’ and the Target utilization to 20.

questions.explanation:
`agent.googleapis.com/memory/percent_used` reports separate time series for memory states such as `used`, `buffered`, `cached`, and `slab`. A filter joined with `AND` requires one time series to have every listed state simultaneously, which is impossible; therefore, it selects no usable series for autoscaling. Filtering on `metric.label.state = 'used'` selects the memory-in-use percentage, and `GAUGE` correctly compares its recent values with the utilization target of 80.

**Learn more:** [Scale based on Monitoring metrics](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/autoscaler/scaling-cloud-monitoring-metrics) · [Legacy Monitoring and Logging agent metrics](https://cloud.google.com/monitoring/api/metrics_agent)

options.text: Create a project for development and test and another for staging and production
Create a network for development and test and another for staging and production
Create one subnetwork for development and another for staging and production
Create one project for development, a second for staging and a third for production

questions.explanation:
In Google Cloud the project is the primary boundary for IAM and resource isolation. Putting development and test in one project lets developers and testers freely access each other's resources, while a separate project for staging and production denies them access to those environments. Because staging and production share a single project, staging can be granted access to the specific production services it needs. A separate network (B) or subnetwork (C) only isolates at the network layer, not at the IAM/resource level, and three separate projects (D) would needlessly complicate the required staging-to-production access.

**Learn more:** [PCA Case Study Q5](https://www.examtopics.com/discussions/google/view/9191-exam-professional-cloud-architect-topic-5-question-5/) · [Mountkirk Games case study](https://cloud.google.com/certification/guides/cloud-architect/casestudy-mountkirkgames-rev2)

Your company highly values responsiveness and rapidly meeting customer needs. Its primary business objectives are release speed and agility. You want to lower the likelihood that security errors are introduced accidentally.  
  
Which two actions can you take? (Choose two.)

options.text: Ensure every code check-in is peer reviewed by a security SME
Use source code security analyzers as part of the CI/CD pipeline
Ensure you have stubs to unit test all interfaces between components
Enable code signing and a trusted binary repository integrated with your CI/CD pipeline
Run a vulnerability security scanner as part of your continuous-integration /continuous-delivery (CI/CD) pipeline

questions.explanation:
Automated source-code security analysis in CI/CD performs static analysis to identify security vulnerabilities and coding errors early, without adding a manual review gate to every check-in. Automated vulnerability security scanning in the pipeline adds continuous security validation, allowing vulnerabilities to be detected and addressed while maintaining rapid, agile releases.

**Learn more:** [Enhance source code security with static application security testing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/devops-guidance/qa.st.4-enhance-source-code-security-with-static-application-security-testing.html) · [DevOps security considerations overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cloud-adoption-framework/ready/considerations/security-considerations-overview)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],For this question, refer to the TerramEarth case study. To comply with European GDPR regulation, TerramEarth must delete data generated by its European customers after 36 months when it includes personal data. In the new architecture, the data will be stored in both Cloud Storage and BigQuery. What should you do?

options.text: Create a BigQuery table for the European data, and set the table retention period to 36 months. For Cloud Storage, use gsutil to enable lifecycle management using a DELETE action with an Age condition of 36 months.

Create a BigQuery table for the European data, and set the table retention period to 36 months. For Cloud Storage, use gsutil to create a SetStorageClass to NONE action when with an Age condition of 36 months.

Create a BigQuery time-partitioned table for the European data, and set the partition expiration period to 36 months. For Cloud Storage, use gsutil to enable lifecycle management using a DELETE action with an Age condition of 36 months.

Create a BigQuery time-partitioned table for the European data, and set the partition expiration period to 36 months. For Cloud Storage, use gsutil to create a SetStorageClass to NONE action with an Age condition of 36 months.

questions.explanation:
A BigQuery time-partitioned table with a partition-expiration period deletes each partition after its retention period, allowing continuously ingested personal data to expire according to its partition time. Cloud Storage Object Lifecycle Management uses a `Delete` action with an age condition to automatically delete qualifying objects. `SetStorageClass` only changes an object’s storage class and does not delete it.

**Learn more:** [Manage partitioned tables | BigQuery | Google Cloud Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/managing-partitioned-tables) · [Object Lifecycle Management | Cloud Storage | Google Cloud Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/lifecycle)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are moving a large on-premises application to Google Cloud. The application comprises several interconnected virtual machines. You want to develop a detailed migration plan that ensures a smooth migration with minimal effort. You need to understand the current environment, identify dependencies, and estimate the total cost of ownership (TCO) in the cloud. What should you do?

options.text: Write a custom script to query the vSphere API for virtual machine information and then import it into BigQuery for analysis.
Use the Google Cloud Migration Center to perform an automated discovery and assessment of the on-premises environment.
Use Config Connector to declare the desired state of your Google Cloud resources in Kubernetes-style manifests.
Use the Google Cloud pricing calculator to input the specifications of your on-premises servers and receive a TCO estimate.

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud Migration Center performs automated discovery and assessment of on-premises infrastructure. It provides inventory and dependency insights and can generate TCO reports for migration scenarios, supporting detailed migration planning with minimal manual effort.

**Learn more:** [About infrastructure discovery and assessment | Migration Center](https://docs.cloud.google.com/migration-center/docs/discovery-and-assessment-overview) · [Migration Center overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/migration-center/docs/migration-center-overview)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company routes all Google Cloud logs to Cloud Logging. The security team wants to monitor these logs. You need to ensure that the security team can respond quickly when an anomaly—such as an unwanted firewall change or a server breach—is detected. You want to follow Google-recommended practices. What should you do?

options.text: Schedule a cron job with Cloud Scheduler. The scheduled job queries the logs every minute for the relevant events.
Export logs to BigQuery, and trigger a query in BigQuery to process the log data for the relevant events.
Export logs to a Pub/Sub topic, and trigger Cloud Function with the relevant log events.
Export logs to a Cloud Storage bucket, and trigger Cloud Run with the relevant log events.

questions.explanation:
A Cloud Logging sink can route relevant log entries to a Pub/Sub topic in near real time, and a Cloud Function can process the resulting events automatically. This event-driven pattern supports rapid response to security anomalies, whereas scheduled polling and Cloud Storage exports introduce delay.

**Learn more:** [View logs routed to Pub/Sub](https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/export/pubsub?hl=en) · [Route log entries](https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/routing/overview)

",["$","p",null,{"children":"What should you do to isolate development environments from staging and production?"}],"
",["$","$L56",null,{"choices":{"A":"Create a project for development and test and another for staging and production","B":"Create a network for development and test and another for staging and production","C":"Create one subnetwork for development and another for staging and production","D":"Create one project for development, a second for staging and a third for production"},"correctAnswer":"A","explanation":"In Google Cloud the project is the primary boundary for IAM and resource isolation. Putting development and test in one project lets developers and testers freely access each other's resources, while a separate project for staging and production denies them access to those environments. Because staging and production share a single project, staging can be granted access to the specific production services it needs. A separate network (B) or subnetwork (C) only isolates at the network layer, not at the IAM/resource level, and three separate projects (D) would needlessly complicate the required staging-to-production access.

**Learn more:** [PCA Case Study Q5](https://www.examtopics.com/discussions/google/view/9191-exam-professional-cloud-architect-topic-5-question-5/) · [Mountkirk Games case study](https://cloud.google.com/certification/guides/cloud-architect/casestudy-mountkirkgames-rev2)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"cc0d29d8-7888-4a18-9df5-5efd1d9eaf56","examProvider":"google","examName":"professional-cloud-architect","mode":"default"}}]]
52:[["$","p",null,{"children":"Your company highly values responsiveness and rapidly meeting customer needs. Its primary business objectives are release speed and agility. You want to lower the likelihood that security errors are introduced accidentally."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":["Which two actions can you take?"]}],"
",["$","$L56",null,{"choices":{"A":"Ensure every code check-in is peer reviewed by a security SME","B":"Use source code security analyzers as part of the CI/CD pipeline","C":"Ensure you have stubs to unit test all interfaces between components","D":"Enable code signing and a trusted binary repository integrated with your CI/CD pipeline","E":"Run a vulnerability security scanner as part of your continuous-integration /continuous-delivery (CI/CD) pipeline"},"correctAnswer":"BE","explanation":"Automated source-code security analysis in CI/CD performs static analysis to identify security vulnerabilities and coding errors early, without adding a manual review gate to every check-in. Automated vulnerability security scanning in the pipeline adds continuous security validation, allowing vulnerabilities to be detected and addressed while maintaining rapid, agile releases.

**Learn more:** [Enhance source code security with static application security testing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/devops-guidance/qa.st.4-enhance-source-code-security-with-static-application-security-testing.html) · [DevOps security considerations overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cloud-adoption-framework/ready/considerations/security-considerations-overview)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"ad54bd58-3159-4c97-a811-d7d04ec00e1b","examProvider":"google","examName":"professional-cloud-architect","mode":"default"}}]]

",["$","$L56",null,{"choices":{"A":"Create a BigQuery table for the European data, and set the table retention period to 36 months. For Cloud Storage, use gsutil to create a SetStorageClass to NONE action when with an Age condition of 36 months.","C":"Create a BigQuery time-partitioned table for the European data, and set the partition expiration period to 36 months. For Cloud Storage, use gsutil to enable lifecycle management using a DELETE action with an Age condition of 36 months.","D":"Create a BigQuery time-partitioned table for the European data, and set the partition expiration period to 36 months. For Cloud Storage, use gsutil to create a SetStorageClass to NONE action with an Age condition of 36 months."},"correctAnswer":"C","explanation":"A BigQuery time-partitioned table with a partition-expiration period deletes each partition after its retention period, allowing continuously ingested personal data to expire according to its partition time. You have been hired by your client to lead the migration of their application infrastructure to GCP. A current issue is that their on-premises high-performance SAN needs frequent, costly upgrades to keep pace with these identified workloads:  
  
- 20 TB of log archives kept for legal reasons  
- 500 GB of VM boot/data volumes and templates  
- 500 GB of image thumbnails  
- 200 GB of customer session-state data that lets customers restart sessions even after being offline for several days  
  
Which option best represents your recommendations for a cost-effective storage allocation?

options.text: Local SSD for customer session state data. Lifecycle-managed Cloud Storage for log archives, thumbnails, and VM boot/data volumes.
Memcache backed by Cloud Datastore for the customer session state data. Lifecycle-managed Cloud Storage for log archives, thumbnails, and VM boot/data volumes.
Memcache backed by Cloud SQL for customer session state data. Assorted local SSD-backed instances for VM boot/data volumes. Cloud Storage for log archives and thumbnails.
Memcache backed by Persistent Disk SSD storage for customer session state data. Assorted local SSD-backed instances for VM boot/data volumes. Cloud Storage for log archives and thumbnails.

questions.explanation:
Customer session state that must survive customers being offline for several days needs durable storage. Memcache can provide low-latency cached access, while Cloud Datastore persists the session data. Local SSD is temporary storage and may lose data when its VM stops, restarts, crashes, or is terminated; it also cannot be used as a boot device. Cloud Storage lifecycle rules can automatically transition or manage objects to reduce the cost of retained archives and other object data.

**Learn more:** [About Local SSD disks](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/disks/local-ssd) · [Add a Local SSD disk to your compute instance](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/disks/add-local-ssd)

Your agricultural division is testing fully autonomous vehicles and wants its architecture to provide strong security while the vehicles operate.  
  
Which two architectures should you consider? (Choose two.)

options.text: Treat every micro service call between modules on the vehicle as untrusted.
Require IPv6 for connectivity to ensure a secure address space.
Use a trusted platform module (TPM) and verify firmware and binaries on boot.
Use a functional programming language to isolate code execution cycles.
Use multiple connectivity subsystems for redundancy.
Enclose the vehicle's drive electronics in a Faraday cage to isolate chips.

questions.explanation: A zero-trust architecture treats each microservice call between vehicle modules as untrusted and requires authentication and authorization rather than relying on its location inside the vehicle. A TPM supplies a hardware root of trust that can support verification of firmware and boot binaries before they execute, helping prevent compromised software from running.

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company is moving its on-premises data center to the cloud. As part of this migration, you want to incorporate Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) for workload orchestration. Parts of the architecture must also be PCI DSS compliant. Which of the following is most accurate?

options.text: App Engine is the only compute platform on GCP that is certified for PCI DSS hosting.
GKE cannot be used under PCI DSS because it is considered shared hosting.
GKE and GCP provide the tools you need to build a PCI DSS-compliant environment.
All Google Cloud services are usable because Google Cloud Platform is certified PCI-compliant.

questions.explanation:
GKE and Google Cloud provide PCI DSS–compliant infrastructure and guidance for building a compliant environment. PCI compliance follows a shared-responsibility model: Google secures the underlying services, while the customer must implement and operate the required application, access, network, and other security controls.

**Learn more:** [PCI DSS compliance on GKE](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/pci-dss-and-gke-guide) · [PCI DSS compliance on Google Cloud](https://cloud.google.com/security/compliance/pci-dss)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to build an online analytical processing (OLAP) marketing analytics and reporting tool. It requires a relational database capable of operating on hundreds of terabytes of data. Which Google-recommended tool should be used for these applications?

options.text: Cloud Spanner, because it is globally distributed
Cloud SQL, because it is a fully managed relational database
Cloud Firestore, because it offers real-time synchronization across devices
BigQuery, because it is designed for large-scale processing of tabular data

questions.explanation:
BigQuery is a fully managed analytics data warehouse optimized for large-scale analytical queries. Its columnar storage and distributed query engine support querying terabytes in seconds and petabytes in minutes, making it suitable for OLAP reporting and marketing analytics workloads.

**Learn more:** [BigQuery overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/introduction?hl=en) · [Overview of BigQuery analytics](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/query-overview?hl=en)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work in a highly secured environment in which Compute Engine VMs cannot have public Internet access. You do not yet have a VPN connection for accessing an on-premises file server. You need to install specific software on a Compute Engine instance. How should you install the software?

options.text: Upload the required installation files to Cloud Storage. Configure the VM on a subnet with a Private Google Access subnet. Assign only an internal IP address to the VM. Download the installation files to the VM using gsutil.
Upload the required installation files to Cloud Storage and use firewall rules to block all traffic except the IP address range for Cloud Storage. Download the files to the VM using gsutil.

Upload the required installation files to Cloud Source Repositories. Configure the VM on a subnet with a Private Google Access subnet. Assign only an internal IP address to the VM. Download the installation files to the VM using gcloud.

Upload the required installation files to Cloud Source Repositories and use firewall rules to block all traffic except the IP address range for Cloud Source Repositories. Download the files to the VM using gsutil.

questions.explanation:
Private Google Access enables Compute Engine VMs that have only internal IP addresses to reach Google APIs and services, including Cloud Storage, when it is enabled on the VM’s subnet. Uploading the installation files to Cloud Storage and downloading them with gsutil therefore supplies the software without granting the VM public Internet access.

**Learn more:** [Configure Private Google Access](https://cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/configure-private-google-access) · [Private Google Access](https://cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/private-google-access)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are managing an application deployed on Cloud Run for Anthos and need to define a strategy to deploy new versions of the application. You want to assess the new code using a subset of production traffic to determine whether to continue with the rollout. What should you do?

options.text: Deploy a new revision to Cloud Run with the new version. Configure traffic percentage between revisions.
Deploy a new service to Cloud Run with the new version. Add a Cloud Load Balancing instance in front of both services.

In the Google Cloud Console page for Cloud Run, set up continuous deployment using Cloud Build for the development branch. As part of the Cloud Build trigger, configure the substitution variable TRAFFIC_PERCENTAGE with the percentage of traffic you want directed to a new version.

In the Google Cloud Console, configure Traffic Director with a new Service that points to the new version of the application on Cloud Run. Configure Traffic Director to send a small percentage of traffic to the new version of the application.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Run can split incoming traffic across revisions of the same service by percentage. Deploying the updated code as a new revision and directing only part of production traffic to it implements a canary rollout while the existing revision continues serving the remaining traffic.

**Learn more:** [Rollbacks, gradual rollouts, and traffic migration](https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/rollouts-rollbacks-traffic-migration) · [Manage revisions](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/managing/revisions)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has just completed a rapid lift-and-shift migration to Google Compute Engine for its compute requirements. You have another 9 months to design and deploy a more cloud-native solution. In particular, you want a no-ops, auto-scaling system.  
  
Which two compute products should you select? (Choose two.)

options.text: Compute Engine with containers
Google Kubernetes Engine with containers
Google App Engine Standard Environment
Compute Engine with custom instance types
Compute Engine with managed instance groups

questions.explanation:
Google Kubernetes Engine provides managed Kubernetes for containerized workloads and can automatically scale workloads and cluster capacity. App Engine Standard Environment is a fully managed application platform that automatically creates and removes instances in response to traffic. Compute Engine-based choices still require virtual-machine and infrastructure management, even where managed instance groups can scale.

**Learn more:** [Autoscaling a cluster | Google Kubernetes Engine](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/cluster-autoscaler?hl=en) · [How instances are managed | App Engine standard environment](https://docs.cloud.google.com/appengine/docs/standard/how-instances-are-managed?hl=en)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],The TerramEarth development team needs to create an API that satisfies the company’s business requirements. You want the team to concentrate its development effort on business value rather than on building a custom framework.  
  
Which method should they use?

options.text: Use Google App Engine with Google Cloud Endpoints. Focus on an API for dealers and partners
Use Google App Engine with a JAX-RS Jersey Java-based framework. Focus on an API for the public
Use Google App Engine with the Swagger (Open API Specification) framework. Focus on an API for the public
Use Google Container Engine with a Django Python container. Focus on an API for the public
Use Google Container Engine with a Tomcat container with the Swagger (Open API Specification) framework. Focus on an API for dealers and partners

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud Endpoints is a managed API-management system that provides capabilities such as security, monitoring, logging, and quotas. Using it with App Engine lets developers focus on the API’s business functionality instead of implementing and maintaining a custom API framework.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Endpoints documentation](https://cloud.google.com/endpoints/docs)

Your company operates a support-ticketing solution that uses App Engine Standard. The project containing the App Engine application already has a Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) network fully connected to the company's on-premises environment through a Cloud VPN tunnel. You want to allow the App Engine application to communicate with a database running in the company's on-premises environment. What should you do?

options.text: Configure private Google access for on-premises hosts only.
Configure private Google access.
Configure private services access.
Configure serverless VPC access.

questions.explanation:
A Serverless VPC Access connector lets an App Engine Standard service send requests into the connected VPC network. The VPC's existing Cloud VPN connectivity can then route that traffic to the on-premises database. Private Google Access is for reaching Google APIs and services, while Private Services Access establishes private connectivity to supported managed service producers.

**Learn more:** [Connecting to a VPC network | App Engine standard environment](https://cloud.google.com/appengine/docs/standard/connecting-vpc) · [Send serverless traffic to a VPC network | Virtual Private Cloud](https://cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/serverless-vpc-access)

questions.domain: Designing and planning a cloud solution architecture
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to deploy an application on Google Cloud. The application receives traffic over TCP and reads from and writes to the filesystem. It does not support horizontal scaling. Because concurrent access causes corruption, the application process needs exclusive control of the data on the filesystem. The business can accept downtime during an incident, but the application must be available 24/7 to support business operations.  
  
You need to design this application's architecture on Google Cloud. What should you do?

options.text: Use a managed instance group with instances in multiple zones, use Cloud Filestore, and use an HTTP load balancer in front of the instances.
Use a managed instance group with instances in multiple zones, use Cloud Filestore, and use a network load balancer in front of the instances.
Use an unmanaged instance group with an active and standby instance in different zones, use a regional persistent disk, and use an HTTP load balancer in front of the instances.
Use an unmanaged instance group with an active and standby instance in different zones, use a regional persistent disk, and use a network load balancer in front of the instances.

questions.explanation:
An active-passive pair in separate zones prevents concurrent access to the application data while retaining a standby for failover. A regional persistent disk synchronously replicates storage across two zones and can be attached to the standby VM during failover, which suits an application that permits incident downtime. A network load balancer supports TCP traffic; an HTTP load balancer does not provide the required TCP load-balancing architecture.

**Learn more:** [Build HA services using synchronously replicated disks](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/disks/high-availability-regional-persistent-disk) · [External proxy Network Load Balancer overview](https://cloud.google.com/load-balancing/docs/tcp)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],The operations manager requests a list of recommended practices she should consider while migrating a J2EE application to the cloud.  
  
Which three practices should you recommend? (Choose three.)

options.text: Port the application code to run on Google App Engine
Integrate Cloud Dataflow into the application to capture real-time metrics
Instrument the application with a monitoring tool like Stackdriver Debugger
Select an automation framework to reliably provision the cloud infrastructure
Deploy a continuous integration tool with automated testing in a staging environment
Migrate from MySQL to a managed NoSQL database like Google Cloud Datastore or Bigtable

questions.explanation:
Cloud migrations benefit from application observability, repeatable infrastructure automation, and automated validation before release. Instrumentation and debugging/monitoring help diagnose workload behavior; infrastructure automation improves consistency and reliability; and CI with automated tests in a staging environment detects functional and integration issues before production deployment. A specific App Engine port or a MySQL-to-NoSQL redesign is not inherently required, and Cloud Dataflow is not the standard mechanism for collecting application metrics.

**Learn more:** [Migrate to Google Cloud: Best practices for validating a migration plan](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/migration-to-google-cloud-best-practices) · [Automate and manage change](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/framework/operational-excellence/automate-and-manage-change)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You created a pipeline that deploys your source-code changes to infrastructure running in self-healing instance groups. One change adversely affects your key performance indicator. You are unsure how to correct it, and investigating could take up to a week.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Log in to a server, and iterate on the fox locally
Revert the source code change, and rerun the deployment pipeline
Log into the servers with the bad code change, and swap in the previous code
Change the instance group template to the previous one, and delete all instances

questions.explanation:
Restore the last known-good source revision and deploy it through the existing pipeline. This rapidly removes the harmful code while maintaining a consistent, repeatable, version-controlled state across all instances; manual server changes can create drift and may be replaced by the self-healing mechanism. Google Cloud guidance recommends controlled deployments with rollback mechanisms, and Cloud Deploy rollbacks use a prior successful release.

**Learn more:** [Automate and manage change](https://cloud.google.com/architecture/framework/operational-excellence/automate-and-manage-change) · [Roll back a target](https://cloud.google.com/deploy/docs/roll-back)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],For this question, use the Mountkirk Games case study.  
  
You need to analyze and define the technical architecture for Mountkirk Games’ compute workloads. In light of the Mountkirk Games business and technical requirements, what should you do?

options.text: Create network load balancers. Use preemptible Compute Engine instances.
Create network load balancers. Use non-preemptible Compute Engine instances.
Create a global load balancer with managed instance groups and autoscaling policies. Use preemptible Compute Engine instances.
Create a global load balancer with managed instance groups and autoscaling policies. Use non-preemptible Compute Engine instances.

questions.explanation:
A global load balancer routes players to healthy, appropriate regional capacity, while managed instance groups with autoscaling add and remove Compute Engine instances as demand changes. Standard, non-preemptible instances are required for the game-serving tier because preemptible VMs can be terminated by Compute Engine and are intended for workloads that can tolerate interruption.

**Learn more:** [Load balancing and scaling | Compute Engine](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/load-balancing-and-autoscaling) · [Preemptible VM instances | Compute Engine](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instances/preemptible)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A customer is migrating an existing corporate application from an on-premises data center to Google Cloud Platform. Business owners require minimal disruption to users, and the security team has strict password-storage requirements.  
  
Which authentication strategy should they use?

options.text: Use G Suite Password Sync to replicate passwords into Google
Federate authentication via SAML 2.0 to the existing Identity Provider
Provision users in Google using the Google Cloud Directory Sync tool
Ask users to set their Google password to match their corporate password

questions.explanation:
SAML 2.0 federation enables single sign-on through the existing identity provider, so users authenticate with their current corporate credentials. The existing identity provider remains the system that manages passwords and applies its credential policies, avoiding password replication or separate Google passwords. [Google Cloud documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/identity/federating-gcp-with-active-directory-introduction)

**Learn more:** [Federate Google Cloud with Active Directory](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/identity/federating-gcp-with-active-directory-introduction) · [Overview of Google identity management](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/identity/overview-google-authentication)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company’s user-feedback portal consists of a standard LAMP stack replicated across two zones. It is deployed in the `us-central1` region and uses autoscaled managed instance groups at every layer except the database. Currently, only a small, selected group of customers can access the portal. Under these conditions, the portal meets a 99,99% availability SLA.  
  
Next quarter, the company will make the portal available to all users, including unauthenticated users. You need to create a resiliency-testing strategy to ensure that the system continues to meet the SLA when additional user load is introduced.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Capture existing users input, and replay captured user load until autoscale is triggered on all layers. At the same time, terminate all resources in one of the zones
Create synthetic random user input, replay synthetic load until autoscale logic is triggered on at least one layer, and introduce ג€chaosג€ to the system by terminating random resources on both zones
Expose the new system to a larger group of users, and increase group size each day until autoscale logic is triggered on all layers. At the same time, terminate random resources on both zones

Capture existing users input, and replay captured user load until resource utilization crosses 80%. Also, derive estimated number of users based on existing user's usage of the app, and deploy enough resources to handle 200% of expected load

questions.explanation:
A representative load replay validates scaling under actual application behavior, and exercising autoscaling across every scalable layer exposes bottlenecks that could prevent the system from serving the expanded audience. Simulating the loss of an entire zone tests the relevant fault domain for a two-zone regional deployment and verifies that the remaining zone can sustain service during the outage. Google Cloud recommends combining load testing with failure scenarios and regularly simulating failures to validate replication and failover strategies.

**Learn more:** [Perform testing for recovery from failures](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/framework/reliability/perform-testing-for-recovery-from-failures) · [Build highly available systems through resource redundancy](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/framework/reliability/build-highly-available-systems?hl=en)

Your company plans to migrate a 10-TB on-premises database export to Cloud Storage. You need to minimize both the time required to complete this activity and the overall cost. The bandwidth between the on-premises environment and Google Cloud is 1 Gbps. You want to follow Google-recommended practices. What should you do?

options.text: Develop a Dataflow job to read data directly from the database and write it into Cloud Storage.
Use the Data Transfer appliance to perform an offline migration.
Use a commercial partner ETL solution to extract the data from the on-premises database and upload it into Cloud Storage.
Upload the data with gcloud storage cp.

questions.explanation:
At 1 Gbps, transferring 10 TB requires about one day under ideal conditions, so it does not meet Google Cloud’s criterion for using Transfer Appliance, which is appropriate when network upload would take more than one week. Cloud Storage data ingress is free; therefore, directly uploading the export with the Google Cloud CLI avoids appliance and shipping overhead while providing the shortest and lowest-cost option.

**Learn more:** [Transfer Appliance overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/transfer-appliance/docs/4.0/overview) · [Cloud Storage pricing](https://cloud.google.com/storage/pricing)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Refer to the EHR Healthcare case study for this question. You must define the technical architecture for securely deploying workloads to Google Cloud. You must also ensure that only verified containers are deployed by using Google Cloud services. What should you do? (Choose two.)

options.text: Enable Binary Authorization on GKE, and sign containers as part of a CI/CD pipeline.
Configure Jenkins to utilize Kritis to cryptographically sign a container as part of a CI/CD pipeline.
Configure Container Registry to only allow trusted service accounts to create and deploy containers from the registry.
Configure Container Registry to use vulnerability scanning to confirm that there are no vulnerabilities before deploying the workload.

questions.explanation:
Binary Authorization for GKE enforces deployment policy and can require trusted, cryptographically signed image attestations. Container images can be signed as part of a CI/CD process, including with Kritis-compatible attestation tooling, so GKE permits deployment only after the required signature is verified. Registry access controls and vulnerability scanning alone do not provide deploy-time verification of signed container images.

**Learn more:** [Binary Authorization overview](https://cloud.google.com/binary-authorization/docs/overview) · [Get started using the Google Cloud CLI (GKE)](https://cloud.google.com/binary-authorization/docs/getting-started-cli)

questions.domain: Analyzing and optimizing technical and business processes
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are analyzing and defining business processes to support your startup’s trial use of GCP, and you do not yet know the consumer demand for your product. Your manager requires that you minimize GCP service costs and follow Google best practices. What should you do?

options.text: Utilize free tier and sustained use discounts. Provision a staff position for service cost management.
Utilize free tier and sustained use discounts. Provide training to the team about service cost management.
Utilize free tier and committed use discounts. Provision a staff position for service cost management.
Utilize free tier and committed use discounts. Provide training to the team about service cost management.

questions.explanation:
Committed use discounts are intended for predictable, steady resource usage and require a one- or three-year commitment, so they are not appropriate when demand is unknown. Eligible sustained use discounts accrue automatically with continued usage, while the free tier helps reduce trial costs. Google Cloud also recommends fostering cost awareness across the organization so team members can make cost-effective decisions, which supports training the team rather than creating a dedicated cost-management position.

**Learn more:** [Foster a culture of cost awareness](https://cloud.google.com/architecture/framework/cost-optimization/foster-culture-cost-awareness) · [Sustained use discounts](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/sustained-use-discounts)

questions.domain: Analyzing and optimizing technical and business processes
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Which of TerramEarth's legacy enterprise processes will undergo significant change because of increased adoption of Google Cloud Platform?

options.text: Opex/capex allocation, LAN changes, capacity planning
Capacity planning, TCO calculations, opex/capex allocation
Capacity planning, utilization measurement, data center expansion
Data Center expansion, TCO calculations, utilization measurement

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud adoption changes capacity planning from procuring fixed infrastructure to planning and managing elastic cloud capacity. It also requires updated total-cost-of-ownership (TCO) calculations and shifts most resource spending from capital expenditure (CapEx) to consumption-based operational expenditure (OpEx).

**Learn more:** [Well-Architected Framework: Cost optimization pillar](https://cloud.google.com/architecture/framework/cost-optimization) · [Optimize resource usage](https://cloud.google.com/architecture/framework/cost-optimization/optimize-resource-usage)

questions.question: For this question, use the Altostrat Media case study. Altostrat uses Apigee for API management and needs to ensure that its APIs are protected from overuse and abuse. You must implement an Apigee feature that controls the total number of API calls for cost management. What should you do?

options.text: Set up API key validation.
Integrate OAuth 2.0 authorization.
Configure Quota policies.
Activate XML threat protection.

questions.explanation:
An Apigee Quota policy sets the number of requests an API proxy will accept during a defined period, maintains request counters, and rejects subsequent calls when the configured limit is reached. This caps API-call consumption and supports cost management.\
\
**Learn more:** [Apigee Quota policy](https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/api-platform/reference/policies/quota-policy?hl=en)

options.text: Configure Cloud Storage to use server-side encryption with Google-managed encryption keys. Create a bucket policy to restrict access to only authorized Google groups and required service accounts.
Use Cloud Storage default encryption at rest. Implement fine-grained access control using IAM roles and groups to restrict access to sensitive buckets

Implement client-side encryption before uploading it to Cloud Storage. Store the encryption keys in a HashiCorp Vault instance deployed on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). Implement fine-grained access control to sensitive Cloud Storage buckets using IAM roles.

Use customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) for all Cloud Storage buckets storing sensitive media content. Implement fine-grained access control using IAM roles and groups to restrict access to sensitive buckets.

questions.explanation:
Customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) use Cloud KMS with Cloud Storage, giving the organization control over key permissions, rotation, lifecycle, and protection settings while providing key-usage audit logs. Applying CMEK to buckets containing sensitive media and restricting bucket access through IAM roles and groups provides managed encryption with appropriate access control.

**Learn more:** [Customer-managed encryption keys | Cloud Storage](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/encryption/customer-managed-keys) · [Use customer-managed encryption keys | Cloud Storage](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/encryption/using-customer-managed-keys)

The Dress4Win security team has turned off external SSH access to production virtual machines (VMs) on Google Cloud Platform (GCP).  
  
The operations team must remotely administer the VMs, build and push Docker containers, and manage Google Cloud Storage objects. What can they do?

options.text: Grant the operations engineer access to use Google Cloud Shell.
Configure a VPN connection to GCP to allow SSH access to the cloud VMs.
Develop a new access request process that grants temporary SSH access to cloud VMs when an operations engineer needs to perform a task.
Have the development team build an API service that allows the operations team to execute specific remote procedure calls to accomplish their tasks.

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud Shell is a browser-based, authenticated administrative environment with the Google Cloud CLI, Docker, and `gsutil` preinstalled. With appropriately assigned IAM permissions, operations personnel can manage Google Cloud resources, build and push container images, and work with Cloud Storage without reopening external SSH access to production VMs.

**Learn more:** [How Cloud Shell works](https://docs.cloud.google.com/shell/docs/how-cloud-shell-works)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You create a Python script that connects to Google BigQuery from a Google Compute Engine virtual machine. The script prints errors saying that it cannot connect to BigQuery.  
  
What should you do to correct the script?

options.text: Install the latest BigQuery API client library for Python
Run your script on a new virtual machine with the BigQuery access scope enabled
Create a new service account with BigQuery access and execute your script with that user
Install the bq component for gcloud with the command gcloud components install bq.

questions.explanation:
Applications running on a Compute Engine VM use the VM’s attached service-account credentials, and the VM’s access scopes can further restrict calls made by client libraries. A VM configured without a BigQuery-compatible scope cannot use its token to call BigQuery; a VM with the BigQuery access scope enabled can, provided its service account has the required IAM permissions.

**Learn more:** [Authenticate workloads to Google Cloud APIs using service accounts](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/access/authenticate-workloads) · [Service accounts for Compute Engine](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/access/service-accounts)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to decrease the number of unplanned rollbacks caused by erroneous production deployments in your company’s web-hosting platform. Improvements to the QA/Test processes achieved an 80% reduction.  
  
Which additional two approaches can you use to further reduce the rollbacks? (Choose two.)

options.text: Introduce a green-blue deployment model
Replace the QA environment with canary releases
Fragment the monolithic platform into microservices
Reduce the platform's dependency on relational database systems
Replace the platform's relational database systems with a NoSQL database

questions.explanation: Blue-green deployment preserves a known-good production environment, enabling traffic to be switched back promptly when a new release is defective. A microservices architecture limits deployments and rollbacks to individual services, reducing the scope and impact of a faulty change. Database technology changes do not inherently prevent deployment errors or reduce rollback frequency, and canary releases complement rather than replace QA.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Mountkirk Games plans to establish a real-time analytics platform for its new game. The new platform must satisfy their technical requirements.  
  
Which combination of Google technologies meets all of these requirements?

options.text: Kubernetes Engine, Cloud Pub/Sub, and Cloud SQL
Cloud Dataflow, Cloud Storage, Cloud Pub/Sub, and BigQuery
Cloud SQL, Cloud Storage, Cloud Pub/Sub, and Cloud Dataflow
Cloud Dataproc, Cloud Pub/Sub, Cloud SQL, and Cloud Dataflow
Cloud Pub/Sub, Compute Engine, Cloud Storage, and Cloud Dataproc

questions.explanation:
Cloud Pub/Sub ingests game events asynchronously, Cloud Dataflow performs scalable stream processing and transformation, Cloud Storage provides durable object storage, and BigQuery supplies the analytics data warehouse. This is the standard Google Cloud pattern for streaming data from Pub/Sub through Dataflow into BigQuery, with Cloud Storage supporting pipeline storage needs.

**Learn more:** [Dataflow overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/overview) · [Stream from Pub/Sub to BigQuery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/tutorials/dataflow-stream-to-bigquery)

You are assisting the QA team in rolling out a new load-testing tool to test the scalability of your primary cloud services running on Google Compute Engine with Cloud Bigtable.  
  
Which three requirements should they include? (Choose three.)

options.text: Ensure that the load tests validate the performance of Cloud Bigtable
Create a separate Google Cloud project to use for the load-testing environment
Schedule the load-testing tool to regularly run against the production environment
Ensure all third-party systems your services use is capable of handling high load
Instrument the production services to record every transaction for replay by the load-testing tool
Instrument the load-testing tool and the target services with detailed logging and metrics collection

questions.explanation:
Cloud Bigtable capacity planning requires testing representative application workloads against a Bigtable cluster, because throughput and latency depend on workload, schema, and data characteristics. A separate Google Cloud project isolates the load-testing environment from production resources and controls. Detailed logs and metrics from both the load generator and target services are necessary to measure throughput, latency, errors, and bottlenecks. Load testing should normally use an isolated, production-like environment rather than routinely stressing production.

**Learn more:** [Understand performance | Bigtable | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigtable/docs/performance) · [Perform testing for recovery from failures | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/framework/reliability/perform-testing-for-recovery-from-failures)

Your company uses Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) as the platform for all workloads. It has one large GKE cluster containing batch, stateful, and stateless workloads. The GKE cluster is configured with one node pool of 200 nodes. The company needs to lower this cluster’s cost without compromising availability. What should you do?

options.text: Create a second GKE cluster for the batch workloads only. Allocate the 200 original nodes across both clusters.
Configure CPU and memory limits on the namespaces in the cluster. Configure all Pods to have a CPU and memory limits.
Configure a HorizontalPodAutoscaler for all stateless workloads and for all compatible stateful workloads. Configure the cluster to use node auto scaling.
Change the node pool to use preemptible VMs.

questions.explanation:
Horizontal Pod Autoscalers scale compatible workloads’ Pod replicas according to demand, while GKE cluster autoscaling resizes node pools within configured minimum and maximum bounds based on the Pods’ resource requirements. This allows the cluster to retain capacity needed for availability during demand increases and to remove unneeded nodes during lower demand, reducing cost.

**Learn more:** [Horizontal Pod autoscaling | Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE)](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/horizontalpodautoscaler) · [About GKE cluster autoscaling | Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE)](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/cluster-autoscaler)
