questions.question: You need to optimize batch transfers of files into Cloud Storage for Mountkirk Games' new Google Cloud solution. The batch files contain game statistics that must be staged in Cloud Storage and processed by an extract transform load (ETL) tool. What should you do?

options.text: Use gsutil to batch move files in sequence.
Use gsutil to batch copy the files in parallel.
Use gsutil to extract the files as the first part of ETL.
Use gsutil to load the files as the last part of ETL.

questions.explanation:
Batch game-statistics files should be copied into the Cloud Storage staging location concurrently. Parallel copies maximize transfer throughput for many files, while preserving the original source files for a safe staging workflow before ETL processing.\
\
**Learn more:** [gsutil tool | Cloud Storage](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/gsutil) · [Use Cloud Storage with big data](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/working-with-big-data)

questions.question: You need to optimize batch transfers of files into Cloud Storage for Mountkirk Games' new Google Cloud solution. The batch files contain game statistics that must be staged in Cloud Storage and processed by an extract transform load (ETL) tool. What should you do?

options.text: Use a private cluster with a private endpoint with master authorized networks configured.
Use a public cluster with firewall rules and Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) routes.
Use a private cluster with a public endpoint with master authorized networks configured.
Use a public cluster with master authorized networks enabled and firewall rules.

questions.explanation:
A private GKE cluster with its control plane exposed only through a private endpoint prevents internet clients from connecting to the control plane. Configuring master authorized networks additionally limits control-plane access to explicitly trusted IP address ranges, minimizing the exposed attack surface.

**Learn more:** [About network isolation in GKE](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/network-isolation) · [Best practices for GKE networking](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/best-practices/networking)

questions.domain: Designing and planning a cloud solution architecture
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Refer to the Dress4Win case study. Dress4Win is projected to grow to 10 times its current size in 1 year, with related data and traffic growth that follows the existing usage patterns. The CIO has set a target to migrate the production infrastructure to the cloud within the next 6 months. How will you configure the solution to scale for this growth, without major application changes, while still maximizing ROI?

options.text: Migrate the web application layer to App Engine, and MySQL to Cloud Datastore, and NAS to Cloud Storage. Deploy RabbitMQ, and deploy Hadoop servers using Deployment Manager.
Migrate RabbitMQ to Cloud Pub/Sub, Hadoop to BigQuery, and NAS to Compute Engine with Persistent Disk storage. Deploy Tomcat, and deploy Nginx using Deployment Manager.
Implement managed instance groups for Tomcat and Nginx. Migrate MySQL to Cloud SQL, RabbitMQ to Cloud Pub/Sub, Hadoop to Cloud Dataproc, and NAS to Compute Engine with Persistent Disk storage.
Implement managed instance groups for the Tomcat and Nginx. Migrate MySQL to Cloud SQL, RabbitMQ to Cloud Pub/Sub, Hadoop to Cloud Dataproc, and NAS to Cloud Storage.

questions.explanation:
Managed instance groups provide autoscaling for the Tomcat and Nginx application tiers. Cloud SQL preserves MySQL compatibility, Pub/Sub supplies a managed messaging service, and Dataproc is a managed Hadoop service that reduces cluster-administration overhead. Cloud Storage is elastic managed object storage for NAS-hosted content, avoiding the capacity and operational constraints of Compute Engine persistent disks as data grows.

**Learn more:** [Compute Engine managed instance groups](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instance-groups) · [Dataproc documentation](https://cloud.google.com/dataproc/docs)

questions.domain: Designing and planning a cloud solution architecture
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Refer to the KnightMotives Automotive case study. KnightMotives has created a dedicated Google Cloud Interconnect with 99.99% availability between its headquarters and two separate metropolitan areas that correspond to the `us-central1` and `us-east1` Google Cloud regions. To minimize cost and latency between these workloads, you need to ensure that every Google Cloud workload is deployed in these two regions as the VLAN attachment for the Cloud Interconnect. What should you do?

options.text: Schedule an export of all assets via Asset Inventory into BigQuery. Schedule a daily Cloud Run function to query the export and send out an alert if resources are created in regions outside of the allowed list.

Ensure all deployments are done through Infrastructure as Code using standardized Terraform modules. Configure the region variable of all resources with a default value corresponding to one of the allowed regions.
Limit the Google Cloud VPC used by the Cloud Interconnect to only have subnets in the allowed regions.
Configure the Resource Location Restriction constraint organization policy at the organization level, and ensure only the allowed regions are listed.

questions.explanation:
The Resource Location Restriction organization policy (`gcp.resourceLocations`) can enforce an allowlist of supported resource locations across the organization hierarchy, preventing creation of new supported resources outside `us-central1` and `us-east1`. This provides centralized enforcement rather than relying on deployment conventions or detecting violations after resources are created.

**Learn more:** [Restrict resource locations](https://cloud.google.com/organization-policy/restrict-locations) · [Create VLAN attachments](https://cloud.google.com/network-connectivity/docs/interconnect/how-to/dedicated/creating-vlan-attachments)

questions.domain: Designing and planning a cloud solution architecture
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A global media company is releasing a new web application. Its backend runs on Compute Engine in `us-central1` and delivers both static assets (images, CSS, and JavaScript) and dynamic, user-specific content from a Cloud SQL database in the same region. Early feedback from users in Europe and Asia reports substantial page-load delays because static content loads slowly. You need to design a solution that minimizes latency for global users who access the static content. What should you do? (Choose two.)

options.text: Use a regional external Network Load Balancer in us-central1 to better distribute the incoming global traffic.
Enable Cloud CDN for the backend service that serves the static assets, and configure it as part of a global external HTTP(S) Load Balancer.
Vertically scale the Compute Engine instances in us-central1 by increasing their machine size.

Deploy the application frontend service to Compute Engine managed instance groups in regions in Europe and Asia. Use a global external HTTP(S) Load Balancer to route user traffic to the nearest region.
Create Cloud SQL read replicas in regions in Europe and Asia, and direct all database read traffic from those continents to their local replica.

questions.explanation:
Cloud CDN caches cacheable static responses at Google edge locations close to users, reducing round-trip time to an origin in `us-central1`. A global external HTTP(S) Load Balancer supports multi-region backends and directs traffic toward the closest healthy backend with capacity, so frontend managed instance groups in Europe and Asia can serve regional users with lower latency.

**Learn more:** [Cloud CDN overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/cdn/docs/overview?hl=en) · [Application Load Balancer overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/load-balancing/docs/application-load-balancer?hl=en)

questions.domain: Designing and planning a cloud solution architecture
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your ecommerce platform runs a regional Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL database that stores critical order information. The business requires a recovery time objective (RTO) of less than 10 minutes and a recovery point objective (RPO) of 2 minutes to maintain business continuity during a full regional outage. You must design a disaster-recovery strategy for the Cloud SQL database that satisfies the business's strict RTO and RPO requirements while avoiding operational complexity. What should you do?

options.text: Schedule hourly automated backups of the Cloud SQL instance to a multi-regional Cloud Storage bucket. In a disaster, restore the latest backup to a new instance in a different region.
Use Database Migration Service to continuously replicate the database to another instance in a different region. In a disaster, redirect application traffic to the replica.
Configure the Cloud SQL instance with a cross-region read replica. In a disaster, promote the read replica to a standalone, primary instance.
Configure the primary instance for high availability (HA). In the event of a regional outage, trigger a failover to the standby instance.

questions.explanation:
A cross-region Cloud SQL read replica provides a continuously replicated copy in a second region for regional disaster recovery. When the primary region is unavailable, promoting that replica creates a writable standalone primary in the surviving region, providing much faster recovery than backup restoration. Cross-region replication is asynchronous, so replication lag must remain within the 2-minute RPO target. High availability failover operates only between zones in the same region and does not protect against a complete regional outage.

**Learn more:** [About disaster recovery (DR) in Cloud SQL](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres/intro-to-cloud-sql-disaster-recovery) · [Promote replicas for regional migration or disaster recovery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres/replication/cross-region-replicas)

questions.question:
You need to optimize performance for an accurate, real-time weather-charting application. Data arrives from 50,000 sensors, each sending 10 readings per second, formatted as a timestamp and sensor reading.  
  
Where should the data be stored?

options.text: Google BigQuery
Google Cloud SQL
Google Cloud Bigtable
Google Cloud Storage

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud Bigtable is a low-latency, scalable wide-column database built for high-throughput time-series and IoT data. It supports large volumes of timestamped sensor writes and low-latency reads needed to render real-time weather charts.\
\
**Learn more:** [Bigtable overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigtable/docs/overview) · [Schema design for time series data](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigtable/docs/schema-design-time-series)

questions.question:
You are building a large distributed application with 30 microservices. Each distributed microservice must connect to a database back end, and you need to store the credentials securely.  
  
Where should the credentials be stored?

options.text: In the source code
In an environment variable
In a secret management system
In a config file that has restricted access through ACLs

questions.explanation:
A secret management system is designed for secure, centralized storage and controlled retrieval of credentials. It supports least-privilege access, auditing, and secret rotation, which are particularly important when many microservices require database access. CISA notes that secrets managers securely manage passwords, API keys, and other credential material and avoid insecure plaintext storage in files or environment variables.\
\
**Learn more:** [CISA: Cloud Secrets Management Stores](https://www.cisa.gov/eviction-strategies-tool/info-attack/T1555.006)

questions.domain: Analyzing and optimizing technical and business processes
questions.question:
You are building a large distributed application with 30 microservices. Each distributed microservice must connect to a database back end, and you need to store the credentials securely.  
  
Where should the credentials be stored?

options.text: Error rates for requests from Asia
Latency difference between US and Asia
Total visits, error rates, and latency from Asia
Total visits and average latency for users from Asia
The number of character sets present in the database

questions.explanation:
Total visits measures user engagement and traffic volume, while error rates and latency measure the reliability and performance experienced by users in Asia. Monitoring all three provides business and technical indicators for the regional application deployment.

**Learn more:** [Define reliability based on user-experience goals](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/framework/reliability/define-reliability-based-on-user-experience-goals) · [Detect potential failures by using observability](https://cloud.google.com/architecture/framework/reliability/slo-and-alerts)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has a Google Cloud project with three Virtual Private Clouds (VPCs). A Compute Engine instance resides in each VPC. The network subnets do not overlap and must stay separated. The network configuration is shown below.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783767416222-4hppuyr6.jpg)  
  
Instance #1 is an exception and must communicate directly with both Instance #2 and Instance #3 using internal IPs. How should this be accomplished?

options.text: Create a cloud router to advertise subnet #2 and subnet #3 to subnet #1.

Add two additional NICs to Instance #1 with the following configuration: ג€¢ NIC1 ג—‹ VPC: VPC #2 ג—‹ SUBNETWORK: subnet #2 ג€¢ NIC2 ג—‹ VPC: VPC #3 ג—‹ SUBNETWORK: subnet #3 Update firewall rules to enable traffic between instances.
Create two VPN tunnels via CloudVPN: ג€¢ 1 between VPC #1 and VPC #2. ג€¢ 1 between VPC #2 and VPC #3. Update firewall rules to enable traffic between the instances.
Peer all three VPCs: ג€¢ Peer VPC #1 with VPC #2. ג€¢ Peer VPC #2 with VPC #3. Update firewall rules to enable traffic between the instances.

questions.explanation:
A Compute Engine VM can use multiple network interfaces attached to unique subnets in different VPC networks. Attaching additional interfaces for subnet #2 and subnet #3 to Instance #1 gives it direct internal-IP connectivity to both VPCs while the VPC networks remain separate; the applicable firewall rules must allow the required traffic. VPC Network Peering does not provide transitive routing, so the listed chained peering topology would not connect VPC #1 to VPC #3.

**Learn more:** [Multiple network interfaces](https://cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/multiple-interfaces-concepts) · [VPC Network Peering](https://cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/vpc-peering)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to create a copy of a production Linux virtual machine in the US-Central region. You want to manage and replace the copy easily when the production virtual machine changes. You will deploy the copy as a new instance in a different project in the US-East region.  
  
What steps must you take?

options.text: Use the Linux dd and netcat commands to copy and stream the root disk contents to a new virtual machine instance in the US-East region.
Create a snapshot of the root disk and select the snapshot as the root disk when you create a new virtual machine instance in the US-East region.
Create an image file from the root disk with Linux dd command, create a new virtual machine instance in the US-East region
Create a snapshot of the root disk, create an image file in Google Cloud Storage from the snapshot, and create a new virtual machine instance in the US-East region using the image file the root disk.

questions.explanation:
Compute Engine standard snapshots provide a managed, portable copy of a boot disk. A snapshot can be shared across projects and used to create a new disk or VM in another region, so taking a new snapshot enables straightforward replacement when the source VM changes.

**Learn more:** [Manage disk snapshots](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/disks/manage-snapshots) · [About archive and standard disk snapshots](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/disks/snapshots)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization has decided to limit the use of external IP addresses on instances to approved instances only. You want to enforce this requirement across all of your Virtual Private Clouds (VPCs). What should you do?

options.text: Remove the default route on all VPCs. Move all approved instances into a new subnet that has a default route to an internet gateway.
Create a new VPC in custom mode. Create a new subnet for the approved instances, and set a default route to the internet gateway on this new subnet.
Implement a Cloud NAT solution to remove the need for external IP addresses entirely.
Set an Organization Policy with a constraint on constraints/compute.vmExternalIpAccess. List the approved instances in the allowedValues list.

questions.explanation:
The Organization Policy list constraint `constraints/compute.vmExternalIpAccess` defines the Compute Engine VM instances that are permitted to use external IPv4 addresses. Applying it at the organization level and specifying the approved instance resource names in `allowedValues` enforces an allowlist across the organization, including all VPCs.

**Learn more:** [Configure static external IP addresses](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/ip-addresses/configure-static-external-ip-address) · [Organization policy constraints](https://cloud.google.com/organization-policy/reference/org-policy-constraints)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have deployed an application to Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) and are using the Cloud SQL proxy container to make the Cloud SQL database available to services running on Kubernetes. You are notified that the application is reporting database connection issues. Your company policies require a post-mortem. What should you do?

options.text: Use gcloud sql instances restart.
Validate that the Service Account used by the Cloud SQL proxy container still has the Cloud Build Editor role.
In the GCP Console, navigate to Stackdriver Logging. Consult logs for (GKE) and Cloud SQL.
In the GCP Console, navigate to Cloud SQL. Restore the latest backup. Use kubectl to restart all pods.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Logging contains logs from GKE clusters, pods, and containers, and Cloud SQL Auth Proxy output is useful for diagnosing connection failures. Reviewing the GKE and Cloud SQL logs preserves the evidence needed to identify the failure cause and complete a post-mortem. The proxy identity needs the Cloud SQL Client role or equivalent permissions, rather than the Cloud Build Editor role.

**Learn more:** [View GKE logs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/view-logs) · [Connect using the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/mysql/connect-auth-proxy)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to assess your team's readiness for a new GCP project. You must conduct the assessment and create a skills-gap plan that incorporates the business goal of cost optimization. Your team has successfully deployed two GCP projects so far. What should you do?

options.text: Allocate budget for team training. Set a deadline for the new GCP project.
Allocate budget for team training. Create a roadmap for your team to achieve Google Cloud certification based on job role.
Allocate budget to hire skilled external consultants. Set a deadline for the new GCP project.
Allocate budget to hire skilled external consultants. Create a roadmap for your team to achieve Google Cloud certification based on job role.

questions.explanation:
A role-based Google Cloud certification roadmap identifies and develops the specific capabilities needed across the team, while training budget enables the team to close those gaps internally. Building internal skills is a cost-conscious way to support future projects after the team has already demonstrated successful GCP delivery, whereas a deadline does not address a skills gap and external consultants add ongoing delivery cost. Google Cloud's cost-optimization guidance emphasizes aligning cloud spending with business value and fostering cost awareness.

**Learn more:** [Well-Architected Framework: Cost optimization pillar](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/framework/cost-optimization) · [Professional Cloud Architect Certification](https://cloud.google.com/learn/certification/cloud-architect)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an application that uses Vertex AI Feature Store to manage and serve product features for real-time recommendations. You want to monitor the application's performance and health. You need to understand the total duration of a request. What should you do?

options.text: Observe the Request size in your featurestore.
Monitor the Queries per second for your featurestore.
Measure the Latency of your requests.
Track the Online serving throughput of your requests.

questions.explanation:
Latency measures the time required for a request to complete, so it directly represents the overall request duration. Request size, queries per second, and online-serving throughput instead describe payload volume or request/serving rate. Vertex AI Feature Store documentation also identifies latency as a consideration for online feature serving.

**Learn more:** [Serve features from online store | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/machine-learning/featurestore/latest/serve-feature-values?hl=en)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization stores a significant volume of log data in Cloud Logging. The data engineering team is used to SQL for analysis and needs the ability to build insightful dashboards that visualize log trends and patterns. You want to follow the Google Cloud Well-Architected Framework recommendations to deliver a solution for the data engineering team. What should you do?

options.text: Create a log sink, and export the data to BigQuery using Pub/Sub. Run queries and visualize the data with Cloud Monitoring dashboards.
Enable log analytics and run queries in Cloud Monitoring. Visualize the data using Vertex AI workbench.
Enable log analytics and run queries in the linked log dataset in BigQuery. Visualize the data with Looker Studio dashboards.
Create a log sink, and export the data to a storage bucket. Create an external table in BigQuery for the data in the bucket. Run queries and visualize the data with Cloud Monitoring dashboards.

questions.explanation:
Log Analytics provides a SQL-based interface for analyzing Cloud Logging data. A linked BigQuery dataset enables BigQuery services to query the log data in place, and Google Cloud specifically identifies Looker Studio as a service that can query that linked dataset. This avoids an unnecessary log export and supports SQL-driven dashboarding.

**Learn more:** [Query and analyze logs with Observability Analytics](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/analyze/query-and-view) · [Configure log buckets](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/buckets)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A news-feed web service is running the following code on Google App Engine. At peak load, users report seeing news articles that they have already viewed. What is the most likely cause of this issue?  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783765498527-25iw9hqn.png)

options.text: The session variable is local to just a single instance
The session variable is being overwritten in Cloud Datastore
The URL of the API needs to be modified to prevent caching
The HTTP Expires header needs to be set to -1 stop caching

questions.explanation:
The `sessions` dictionary is process memory local to one application instance, rather than shared persistent session storage. App Engine can scale to multiple instances and route consecutive requests from the same user to different instances; an instance that lacks the user’s prior in-memory state treats the viewed list as empty and returns previously viewed articles. [Google Cloud: How requests are handled](https://docs.cloud.google.com/appengine/docs/standard/how-requests-are-handled)

Write a lifecycle management rule in JSON and push it to the bucket with gsutil

Google Cloud Platform resources are organized hierarchically through organizations, folders, and projects. When Cloud Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies are set at these different levels, what is the effective policy at a specific node in the hierarchy?

options.text: The effective policy is determined only by the policy set at the node
The effective policy is the policy set at the node and restricted by the policies of its ancestors
The effective policy is the union of the policy set at the node and policies inherited from its ancestors
The effective policy is the intersection of the policy set at the node and policies inherited from its ancestors

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud IAM allow policies propagate downward through the resource hierarchy. A resource’s effective allow policy is the union of the allow policy set on that resource and the allow policy inherited from its parent resources.

**Learn more:** [Using resource hierarchy for access control](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/resource-hierarchy-access-control)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A customer is receiving reports that their recently updated Google App Engine application takes approximately 30 seconds to load for some users.  
  
This behavior was not reported before the update.  
  
What strategy should you use?

options.text: Work with your ISP to diagnose the problem
Open a support ticket to ask for network capture and flow data to diagnose the problem, then roll back your application
Roll back to an earlier known good release initially, then use Stackdriver Trace and Logging to diagnose the problem in a development/test/staging environment
Roll back to an earlier known good release, then push the release again at a quieter period to investigate. Then use Stackdriver Trace and Logging to diagnose the problem

questions.explanation:
A known-good App Engine version can be returned to service quickly by migrating traffic back to it, reducing the production impact of a release-induced performance regression. Cloud Trace helps identify where request latency occurs, while Cloud Logging provides correlated application and request data; testing the changed release in a development, test, or staging environment prevents further impact on users.

**Learn more:** [App Engine overview: versions and rollback traffic routing](https://cloud.google.com/appengine/docs/an-overview-of-app-engine) · [Test and deploy an App Engine application](https://cloud.google.com/appengine/docs/standard/testing-and-deploying-your-app)

You use Cloud CDN to serve static HTTP(S) website content hosted on a Compute Engine instance group. You want to increase the cache hit ratio.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Customize the cache keys to omit the protocol from the key.
Shorten the expiration time of the cached objects.
Make sure the HTTP(S) header ג€Cache-Regionג€ points to the closest region of your users.
Replicate the static content in a Cloud Storage bucket. Point CloudCDN toward a load balancer on that bucket.

questions.explanation: For identical static content served through both HTTP and HTTPS, excluding the protocol from the Cloud CDN cache key allows requests using either protocol to use the same cached object. This avoids separate cache entries for the same resource and can raise the cache hit ratio.

You use Cloud CDN to serve static HTTP(S) website content hosted on a Compute Engine instance group. You want to increase the cache hit ratio.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create a Cloud Storage lifecycle rule with Age: ג€30ג€, Storage Class: ג€Standardג€, and Action: ג€Set to Coldlineג€, and create a second GCS life-cycle rule with Age: ג€365ג€, Storage Class: ג€Coldlineג€, and Action: ג€Deleteג€.

Create a Cloud Storage lifecycle rule with Age: ג€30ג€, Storage Class: ג€Coldlineג€, and Action: ג€Set to Nearlineג€, and create a second GCS life-cycle rule with Age: ג€91ג€, Storage Class: ג€Coldlineג€, and Action: ג€Set to Nearlineג€.

Create a Cloud Storage lifecycle rule with Age: ג€90ג€, Storage Class: ג€Standardג€, and Action: ג€Set to Nearlineג€, and create a second GCS life-cycle rule with Age: ג€91ג€, Storage Class: ג€Nearlineג€, and Action: ג€Set to Coldlineג€.

Create a Cloud Storage lifecycle rule with Age: ג€30ג€, Storage Class: ג€Standardג€, and Action: ג€Set to Coldlineג€, and create a second GCS life-cycle rule with Age: ג€365ג€, Storage Class: ג€Nearlineג€, and Action: ג€Deleteג€.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Storage lifecycle management can change Standard objects to Coldline storage, and it can delete objects when they meet an age and storage-class condition. Moving objects to Coldline at 30 days minimizes ongoing storage cost; deleting Coldline objects at 365 days retains them for one year and exceeds Coldline's 90-day minimum storage duration.

**Learn more:** [Object Lifecycle Management | Cloud Storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/lifecycle) · [Storage classes | Cloud Storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/storage-classes)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has a networking team and a development team. The development team operates applications on Compute Engine instances containing sensitive data. The development team needs administrative permissions for Compute Engine. The company requires that the networking team manage all network resources. The development team does not want the networking team to access the sensitive data on the instances. What should you do?

options.text: 1. Create a project with a standalone VPC and assign the Network Admin role to the networking team. 2. Create a second project with a standalone VPC and assign the Compute Admin role to the development team. 3. Use Cloud VPN to join the two VPCs.
1. Create a project with a standalone Virtual Private Cloud (VPC), assign the Network Admin role to the networking team, and assign the Compute Admin role to the development team.

1. Create a project with a Shared VPC and assign the Network Admin role to the networking team. 2. Create a second project without a VPC, configure it as a Shared VPC service project, and assign the Compute Admin role to the development team.

1. Create a project with a standalone VPC and assign the Network Admin role to the networking team. 2. Create a second project with a standalone VPC and assign the Compute Admin role to the development team. 3. Use VPC Peering to join the two VPCs.

questions.explanation:
Shared VPC centralizes VPC network resources in a host project while allowing application resources, including Compute Engine instances, to reside in attached service projects. The Network Admin role on the host project manages network resources but does not grant administration of instances and disks in the service project, preserving separation from sensitive workload data. The development team can receive Compute Admin in the service project to manage its Compute Engine resources.

**Learn more:** [Shared VPC](https://cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/shared-vpc) · [Compute Engine IAM roles and permissions](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/access/iam)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company runs an application on Google Cloud that gathers data from thousands of globally distributed physical devices. Data is published to Pub/Sub and streamed in real time to an SSD Cloud Bigtable cluster through a Dataflow pipeline.  
  
The operations team reports that the Cloud Bigtable cluster has a hotspot and that queries are taking longer than expected. You need to fix the issue and stop it from recurring. What action should you take?

options.text: Advise your clients to use HBase APIs instead of NodeJS APIs.
Delete records older than 30 days.
Review your RowKey strategy and ensure that keys are evenly spread across the alphabet.
Double the number of nodes you currently have.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Bigtable row keys are lexicographically sorted, so a sequential or otherwise concentrated key pattern directs disproportionate reads or writes to a small key range and creates a hotspot. A row-key design that distributes keys evenly across the key space spreads workload across nodes and prevents the hotspot. Adding nodes does not fix a schema-driven hotspot when traffic remains concentrated on the same row or tablet range.

**Learn more:** [Schema design best practices | Bigtable](https://cloud.google.com/bigtable/docs/schema-design) · [Scaling | Bigtable](https://cloud.google.com/bigtable/docs/scaling)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],At Dress4Win, an operations engineer needs to create a low-cost solution for remotely archiving copies of database backup files.  
  
The database files are compressed tar files stored in the existing data center. How should the engineer proceed?

options.text: Create a cron script using gsutil to copy the files to a Coldline Storage bucket.
Create a cron script using gsutil to copy the files to a Regional Storage bucket.
Create a Cloud Storage Transfer Service Job to copy the files to a Coldline Storage bucket.
Create a Cloud Storage Transfer Service job to copy the files to a Regional Storage bucket.

questions.explanation:
Storage Transfer Service supports scheduled, agent-based transfers from an on-premises file system to Cloud Storage, providing managed and reliable copying of the backup files. Coldline Storage is designed for infrequently accessed data and has lower at-rest storage costs than Regional (Standard) Storage, making it the economical destination among the available choices.

**Learn more:** [Transfer from a file system to Cloud Storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage-transfer/docs/create-transfers/agent-based/file-system-to-cloud-storage) · [Cloud Storage storage classes](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/storage-classes)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have deployed several instances on Compute Engine. As a security requirement, the instances must not have public IP addresses. There is no VPN connection between Google Cloud and your office, and you need to connect by SSH to a specific machine without breaching the security requirements. What should you do?

options.text: Configure Cloud NAT on the subnet where the instance is hosted. Create an SSH connection to the Cloud NAT IP address to reach the instance.
Add all instances to an unmanaged instance group. Configure TCP Proxy Load Balancing with the instance group as a backend. Connect to the instance using the TCP Proxy IP.
Configure Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) for the instance and ensure that you have the role of IAP-secured Tunnel User. Use the gcloud command line tool to ssh into the instance.
Create a bastion host in the network to SSH into the bastion host from your office location. From the bastion host, SSH into the desired instance.

questions.explanation:
Identity-Aware Proxy TCP forwarding provides authenticated, authorized SSH access to a Compute Engine VM through an encrypted tunnel without requiring the VM to have a public, routable IP address. The IAP-Secured Tunnel User role grants the required IAP tunnel access, and `gcloud compute ssh` can use IAP TCP tunneling to reach the specified instance.

**Learn more:** [Use IAP for TCP forwarding](https://cloud.google.com/iap/docs/using-tcp-forwarding) · [TCP forwarding overview](https://cloud.google.com/iap/docs/tcp-forwarding-overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization uses distinct Google Cloud projects for shared services, development, testing, and production.  
  
- The shared services project contains private CI/CD runners and a centralized Artifact Registry.  
- The development, testing, and production projects contain the GKE clusters on which applications are deployed.  
  
You must design an architecture that lets the CI/CD runners connect to the GKE clusters and lets the clusters pull images from Artifact Registry, all through private IP addresses. Direct network traffic among the development, testing, and production environments must, however, be strictly prohibited. What should you do?

options.text: Create a separate VPC in each of the four projects. Connect each environment's VPC to the shared services VPC through VPC Network Peering.
Expose the resources in the shared services project using an external load balancer. Implement a firewall rule to limit access.
Create a separate VPC in each project. Use VPC Network Peering to create a full mesh, connecting every VPC directly to every other VPC.
Configure the shared services project as a Shared VPC host. Create a single VPC in this host project and attach the environment projects as service projects.

questions.explanation:
A hub-and-spoke VPC Network Peering design gives each environment private internal connectivity to the shared-services VPC, allowing access to shared CI/CD and GKE-related resources. VPC Network Peering is not transitive, so environments peered only with shared services cannot communicate with one another through that VPC. Private GKE access to Artifact Registry can use private Google API access, including the restricted VIP configuration where required.

**Learn more:** [VPC Network Peering](https://cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/vpc-peering) · [Configure restricted access for GKE private clusters](https://cloud.google.com/artifact-registry/docs/gke-private-clusters)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You must build and deploy a containerized web application on Google Cloud. The application is highly write-intensive and needs a relational database for its data store. It must be highly available across multiple cloud regions. You want to reduce operational overhead while following Google-recommended practices. What should you do?

options.text: Deploy the application to GKE clusters in multiple regions and expose the application endpoint with a regional load balancer. Use Cloud SQL as the database.
Deploy the application to Cloud Run in multiple regions behind a global HTTPS load balancer. Use Spanner as the database.
Deploy the application to a GKE standard cluster behind a global HTTPS load balancer. Use Firestore as the database with multi-region locations enabled.
Deploy the application to a GKE standard cluster with a global ingress to expose the application endpoint. Use Bigtable as the database.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Run minimizes infrastructure operations for containerized workloads and can be deployed in multiple regions behind a global external HTTPS load balancer. Spanner is a fully managed relational database whose multi-region configurations automatically replicate data across regions with strong consistency, support high availability during regional failures, and are designed for scalable transactional workloads.

**Learn more:** [Serve traffic from multiple regions | Cloud Run](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/multiple-regions?hl=en) · [Regional, dual-region, and multi-region configurations | Spanner](https://docs.cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/instance-configurations)

You are designing the network architecture for a public-facing, containerized web application running on Cloud Run. All inbound traffic must be inspected by a Cloud Armor web application firewall (WAF) before it reaches the application. You plan to use an Application Load Balancer with the Cloud Armor policy attached. You must ensure that every public request passes through the load balancer and that attempts to directly access the Cloud Run service through its default `*.run.app` URL are blocked. What should you do?

options.text: Enable Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) directly on the Cloud Run service to intercept and validate all incoming requests
Create a DNS entry to route traffic to Cloud Armor. Configure Cloud Armor to deny traffic from unknown IP addresses
Set the Cloud Run ingress to Allow internal traffic and Cloud Load Balancing, and use a serverless NEG backend on the load balancer
Configure a VPC firewall rule with a high priority to deny all traffic that does not originate from the load balancer

questions.explanation:
The Cloud Run **Internal and Cloud Load Balancing** ingress setting permits internet traffic only through an external Application Load Balancer and rejects direct internet access to the service’s default `run.app` URL. A serverless NEG is the supported backend that connects the Application Load Balancer to Cloud Run, ensuring Cloud Armor is evaluated on the public request path.

**Learn more:** [Restrict network endpoint ingress for Cloud Run services](https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/securing/ingress) · [Integrate Cloud Armor with other Google Cloud products](https://cloud.google.com/armor/docs/integrating-cloud-armor)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your web application must meet the requirements of the European Union's General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). You are responsible for its technical architecture. What should you do?

options.text: Ensure that your web application only uses native features and services of Google Cloud Platform, because Google already has various certifications and provides ג€pass-onג€ compliance when you use native features.
Enable the relevant GDPR compliance setting within the GCPConsole for each of the services in use within your application.
Ensure that Cloud Security Scanner is part of your test planning strategy in order to pick up any compliance gaps.
Define a design for the security of data in your web application that meets GDPR requirements.

questions.explanation:
GDPR compliance requires workload-specific security and privacy controls. Cloud providers supply infrastructure controls and compliance resources, but the customer remains responsible for securing its application, data, access, configurations, and regulatory use case. The data-security design must therefore meet the applicable GDPR requirements.

**Learn more:** [Shared responsibilities and shared fate on Google Cloud](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/framework/security/shared-responsibility-shared-fate) · [Privacy Resource Center](https://cloud.google.com/privacy)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company operates a critical, revenue-producing ecommerce application served by a regional managed instance group (MIG) behind an external HTTP(S) Load Balancer. The operations team is currently overloaded with low-priority notifications and is beginning to ignore alerts. Your team's service level objective (SLO) is to maintain 99.9% availability, measured as the ratio of successful requests (2xx status codes) to total requests. You want to reduce noise from non-critical events and ensure that the team is notified only about actionable issues that threaten the SLO. What should you do?

options.text: Focus on cause-based alerts, creating alerting policies with thresholds for the Compute Engine instances, including CPU utilization, memory usage, disk I/O, and network traffic.
Create log-based alerts for only the WARN and ERROR log entries generated by the application to ensure that no potential issue is missed.
Implement an error budget policy based on the availability of the SLO. Create a
Configure alerts based on predictive metrics. Use the instance count of the MIG as the primary metric to trigger an alert.

questions.explanation:
An error-budget burn-rate alert directly monitors the availability SLO and identifies when the allowed 0.1% failure budget is being consumed rapidly enough that the SLO is likely to be violated. Paging on projected exhaustion within 24 hours prioritizes incidents affecting user-observed service health, while avoiding noisy alerts for individual resource metrics, log entries, or instance-count changes that may not endanger availability.

**Learn more:** [Alerting on your burn rate | Google Cloud Observability](https://docs.cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/solutions/slo-monitoring/alerting-on-budget-burn-rate?hl=en) · [Concepts in service monitoring | Google Cloud Observability](https://docs.cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/solutions/slo-monitoring)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is developing a web-based application. You need to ensure that production deployments are linked to source-code commits and are completely auditable. What should you do?

options.text: Make sure a developer is tagging the code commit with the date and time of commit.
Make sure a developer is adding a comment to the commit that links to the deployment.
Make the container tag match the source code commit hash.
Make sure the developer is tagging the commits with latest.

questions.explanation:
Tagging each container image with the source-code commit hash creates a unique, durable association between the deployed artifact and the exact revision that produced it. Commit-hash image tags support version tracking, rollback, and traceability, whereas `latest` is mutable and manual commit annotations do not establish artifact identity.

**Learn more:** [Automate your builds with GitHub Actions](https://docs.docker.com/guides/angular/configure-github-actions/)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work at a financial institution that stores mortgage-loan approval documents in Cloud Storage. Every change to an approval document must be uploaded as a separate approval file, and you need to ensure these documents cannot be deleted or overwritten for the next 5 years. What should you do?

options.text: Create a retention policy on the bucket for the duration of 5 years. Create a lock on the retention policy.
Create the bucket with uniform bucket-level access, and grant a service account the role of Object Writer. Use the service account to upload new files.
Use a customer-managed key for the encryption of the bucket. Rotate the key after 5 years.
Create the bucket with fine-grained access control, and grant a service account the role of Object Writer. Use the service account to upload new files.

questions.explanation:
A Cloud Storage bucket retention policy enforces a minimum retention period for every object in the bucket, preventing deletion or replacement before the period expires. Locking the policy permanently prevents its removal or reduction, preserving the required five-year immutability period.

**Learn more:** [Bucket Lock | Cloud Storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/bucket-lock) · [Use and lock retention policies | Cloud Storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/using-bucket-lock)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company runs an enterprise application on Compute Engine that needs high availability and high performance. The application is deployed on two instances across two zones in the same region in active-passive mode. It writes data to a persistent disk. If a single zone fails, that data must be immediately available to the instance in the other zone. You want to maximize performance while minimizing downtime and data loss.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: 1. Attach a persistent SSD disk to the first instance. 2. Create a snapshot every hour. 3. In case of a zone outage, recreate a persistent SSD disk in the second instance where data is coming from the created snapshot.
1. Create a Cloud Storage bucket. 2. Mount the bucket into the first instance with gcs-fuse. 3. In case of a zone outage, mount the Cloud Storage bucket to the second instance with gcs-fuse.
1. Attach a regional SSD persistent disk to the first instance. 2. In case of a zone outage, force-attach the disk to the other instance.

1. Attach a local SSD to the first instance disk. 2. Execute an rsync command every hour where the target is a persistent SSD disk attached to the second instance. 3. In case of a zone outage, use the second instance.

questions.explanation:
Regional SSD Persistent Disk synchronously replicates every write between two zones in the same region, protecting against a single-zonal failure with minimal recovery point objective. During a zonal outage, force-attaching the regional disk to the standby instance in the surviving replica zone makes the replicated data available without waiting for snapshots or periodic file synchronization.

**Learn more:** [About synchronous disk replication](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/disks/about-regional-persistent-disk?hl=en) · [Manage failures for regional disks](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/disks/repd-failover)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are designing the architecture for a stateless, public-facing containerized web application. The marketing department uses this web application to run unpredictable flash sales that create sudden, massive spikes in user traffic. The application is a critical revenue driver and must remain available and responsive to users at all times. Your design must automatically accommodate large traffic fluctuations and enable new application versions to be deployed with zero downtime, along with safe and rapid rollback capability. What should you do?

options.text: Deploy the application to a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster. Use the Recreate deployment strategy to roll out new application versions.
Deploy the application to a single, large Compute Engine instance and use a startup script to pull and run the latest container image on boot.
Deploy the application as a Cloud Run service. Configure request-based auto-scaling and use gradual rollouts by splitting traffic between revisions.
Deploy the application to a regional Managed Instance Group (MIG). Configure a CPU-based autoscaling policy and use the MIG's rolling update feature for deployments.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Run is designed to run stateless containers and automatically scales revisions to serve incoming requests. Its immutable revisions support percentage-based traffic splitting, allowing gradual deployments without interrupting in-flight requests, and traffic can be shifted back to a prior revision for a fast rollback.

**Learn more:** [About instance autoscaling in Cloud Run services](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/about-instance-autoscaling) · [Rollbacks, gradual rollouts, and traffic migration](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/rollouts-rollbacks-traffic-migration)

questions.domain: Designing and planning a cloud solution architecture
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company needs you to build a highly reliable web application with several public APIs as its backend. You do not anticipate high user traffic, but traffic might occasionally spike. You want to use Cloud Load Balancing, and the solution must be cost-effective for users. What should you do?

options.text: Store static content such as HTML and images in Cloud CDN. Host the APIs on App Engine and store the user data in Cloud SQL.

Store static content such as HTML and images in a Cloud Storage bucket. Host the APIs on a zonal Google Kubernetes Engine cluster with worker nodes in multiple zones, and save the user data in Cloud Spanner.
Store static content such as HTML and images in Cloud CDN. Use Cloud Run to host the APIs and save the user data in Cloud SQL.
Store static content such as HTML and images in a Cloud Storage bucket. Use Cloud Functions to host the APIs and save the user data in Firestore.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Run provides on-demand, automatically scaling capacity without requiring infrastructure to be pre-provisioned for peak demand, which suits low baseline traffic with occasional spikes. An external Application Load Balancer supports Cloud Run backends and Cloud CDN can serve static content. Cloud SQL supports regional high-availability configurations for resilient relational data storage.

**Learn more:** [What is Cloud Run](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/overview/what-is-cloud-run) · [Cloud Run pricing](https://cloud.google.com/run/pricing)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A development team at your company has built a dockerized HTTPS web application. You need to deploy the application to Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) and ensure that it scales automatically.  
  
How should you deploy it to GKE?

options.text: Use the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler and enable cluster autoscaling. Use an Ingress resource to load-balance the HTTPS traffic.
Use the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler and enable cluster autoscaling on the Kubernetes cluster. Use a Service resource of type LoadBalancer to load-balance the HTTPS traffic.
Enable autoscaling on the Compute Engine instance group. Use an Ingress resource to load-balance the HTTPS traffic.
Enable autoscaling on the Compute Engine instance group. Use a Service resource of type LoadBalancer to load-balance the HTTPS traffic.

questions.explanation:
Horizontal Pod Autoscaler automatically adjusts the number of workload Pods based on configured metrics, while GKE cluster autoscaling adjusts node capacity to accommodate changing Pod demand. A GKE Ingress resource configures an HTTP(S) Application Load Balancer for HTTPS traffic to Services and Pods.

**Learn more:** [Horizontal Pod autoscaling | Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE)](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/horizontalpodautoscaler?hl=en) · [Autoscaling a cluster | Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE)](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/cluster-autoscaler?hl=en)

questions.domain: Designing and planning a cloud solution architecture
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],The team must create a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster to host a newly developed application that needs access to third-party services on the internet.  
  
The company prohibits any Compute Engine instance in Google Cloud from having a public IP address. You need to create a deployment strategy that complies with these guidelines. What should you do?

options.text: Configure the GKE cluster as a private cluster, and configure Cloud NAT Gateway for the cluster subnet.
Configure the GKE cluster as a private cluster. Configure Private Google Access on the Virtual Private Cloud (VPC).
Configure the GKE cluster as a route-based cluster. Configure Private Google Access on the Virtual Private Cloud (VPC).
Create a Compute Engine instance, and install a NAT Proxy on the instance. Configure all workloads on GKE to pass through this proxy to access third-party services on the Internet.

questions.explanation:
A private GKE cluster creates nodes without external IP addresses, satisfying the requirement that Compute Engine instances have no public IPs. Cloud NAT supplies outbound internet connectivity for those private nodes and Pods, allowing workloads to call third-party internet services without accepting inbound connections or assigning public IP addresses. Private Google Access is intended for Google APIs and services rather than general internet egress.

**Learn more:** [About network isolation in GKE](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/network-isolation) · [Learn GKE networking architecture](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/learn/learn-gke-net-architecture)

questions.question: For this question, use the Mountkirk Games case study. Which managed storage option satisfies Mountkirk's technical requirement to store game activity in a time-series database service?

options.text: Cloud Bigtable
Cloud Spanner
BigQuery
Cloud Datastore

questions.explanation:
Cloud Bigtable is a fully managed, highly scalable NoSQL database designed for high-throughput workloads and supports storing and querying time-series data, making it appropriate for game-activity events recorded over time.\
\
**Learn more:** [Bigtable overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigtable/docs/overview) · [Schema design for time series data](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigtable/docs/schema-design-time-series)

questions.domain: Designing and planning a cloud solution architecture
questions.question: For this question, use the Mountkirk Games case study. Which managed storage option satisfies Mountkirk's technical requirement to store game activity in a time-series database service?

options.text: Use Service Directory to register the monolith's endpoint, allowing dependent applications to look up its address and connect directly.
Implement a managed API facade with Apigee to handle all requests from dependent applications on behalf of the monolith’s backend.
Use an internal load balancer to provide a stable IP for dependent applications to connect directly to the monolith's native API.
Provide dependent applications with direct database access by creating secured SQL VIEWs on Cloud SQL for them to query.

questions.explanation:
Apigee API proxies act as a managed facade between client applications and backend services. They decouple the consumer-facing API from backend implementation, so the monolith can later be replaced or decomposed and request/response mediation or routing can change without requiring dependent applications to call the native backend API directly.

**Learn more:** [Understanding APIs and API proxies | Apigee](https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/api-platform/fundamentals/understanding-apis-and-api-proxies)

options.text: Ensure that a firewall rules exists to allow source traffic on HTTP/HTTPS to reach the load balancer.
Assign a public IP to each instance and configure a firewall rule to allow the load balancer to reach the instance public IP.
Ensure that a firewall rule exists to allow load balancer health checks to reach the instances in the instance group.
Create a tag on each instance with the name of the load balancer. Configure a firewall rule with the name of the load balancer as the source and the instance tag as the destination.

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud load-balancer backends require an ingress firewall rule that allows health-check probes to reach the backend VMs on the health-check protocol and port. If the probes are blocked, the default implied ingress-deny rule causes the backends to be considered unhealthy, which can trigger replacement of instances in a managed instance group. Public IP addresses are not required for backend VMs.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Load Balancing firewall rules](https://cloud.google.com/load-balancing/docs/firewall-rules) · [Cloud Load Balancing health checks](https://cloud.google.com/load-balancing/docs/health-checks)

Your company is expanding its AI-powered operations across the country and has selected accelerator-based compute for its AI workloads. The batch image-processing workloads are not time-sensitive and can tolerate interruptions. You need to quickly deploy cost-effective accelerator nodes for these batch tasks, while ensuring rapid deployment and data persistence when needed. What should you do?

options.text: Deploy standard VMs with configured accelerators and attached persistent disks.
Deploy spot VMs with attached persistent disks and implement checkpoint mechanisms.
Deploy spot VMs with local SSD to reduce time for bursty workloads
Deploy Cloud Run functions with ephemeral local SSD.

questions.explanation:
Spot VMs provide substantially discounted accelerator compute for fault-tolerant batch workloads, but they can be preempted at any time. Checkpointing preserves job progress, and attached persistent disks keep recoverable data after the Spot VM is stopped or preempted. Local SSD storage is temporary and is unsuitable where persistence is required.

**Learn more:** [Spot VMs | Compute Engine](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instances/spot) · [About GPU instances | Compute Engine](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/gpus/about-gpus)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],To accelerate data retrieval, more vehicles will be upgraded with cellular connections and will be able to send data to the ETL process. The existing FTP process is error-prone and restarts transfer from the beginning of a file whenever a connection fails, which occurs frequently. You want to improve solution reliability and minimize data-transfer time over the cellular connections.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Use one Google Container Engine cluster of FTP servers. Save the data to a Multi-Regional bucket. Run the ETL process using data in the bucket

Use multiple Google Container Engine clusters running FTP servers located in different regions. Save the data to Multi-Regional buckets in US, EU, and Asia. Run the ETL process using the data in the bucket
Directly transfer the files to different Google Cloud Multi-Regional Storage bucket locations in US, EU, and Asia using Google APIs over HTTP(S). Run the ETL process using the data in the bucket

Directly transfer the files to a different Google Cloud Regional Storage bucket location in US, EU, and Asia using Google APIs over HTTP(S). Run the ETL process to retrieve the data from each Regional bucket

questions.explanation:
Cloud Storage resumable uploads over HTTP(S) can resume after a communication failure from the byte offset already persisted, avoiding retransmission of the entire file. Placing uploads into regional buckets in the US, EU, and Asia keeps data transfer close to the vehicles’ geographic regions, minimizing latency and transfer time.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Storage resumable uploads](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/resumable-uploads?hl=en) · [Cloud Storage bucket locations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/bucket-locations)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing an App Engine application that uses Cloud Datastore as its persistence layer. You must retrieve several root entities whose identifiers you have. You want to minimize the overhead of Cloud Datastore operations. What should you do?

options.text: Create the Key object for each Entity and run a batch get operation
Create the Key object for each Entity and run multiple get operations, one operation for each entity
Use the identifiers to create a query filter and run a batch query operation
Use the identifiers to create a query filter and run multiple query operations, one operation for each entity

questions.explanation:
Cloud Datastore can retrieve multiple entities directly from their keys in a single batch lookup. Batch reads have the same operational overhead as a single operation, making them more efficient than separate get operations; queries are unnecessary when the entity identifiers are already known.

**Learn more:** [Datastore best practices](https://docs.cloud.google.com/datastore/docs/best-practices) · [Batch lookup | Datastore](https://docs.cloud.google.com/datastore/docs/samples/datastore-batch-lookup)

questions.domain: Analyzing and optimizing technical and business processes
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are migrating third-party applications from optimized on-premises virtual machines to Google Cloud. You are uncertain about the optimal CPU and memory settings. The applications show a consistent usage pattern over multiple weeks. You want to optimize resource use at the lowest cost. What should you do?

options.text: Create an instance template with the smallest available machine type, and use an image of the third-party application taken from a current on-premises virtual machine. Create a managed instance group that uses average CPU utilization to autoscale the number of instances in the group. Modify the average CPU utilization threshold to optimize the number of instances running.

Create an App Engine flexible environment, and deploy the third-party application using a Dockerfile and a custom runtime. Set CPU and memory options similar to your application's current on-premises virtual machine in the app.yaml file.

Create multiple Compute Engine instances with varying CPU and memory options. Install the Cloud Monitoring agent, and deploy the third-party application on each of them. Run a load test with high traffic levels on the application, and use the results to determine the optimal settings.

Create a Compute Engine instance with CPU and memory options similar to your application's current on-premises virtual machine. Install the Cloud Monitoring agent, and deploy the third-party application. Run a load test with normal traffic levels on the application, and follow the Rightsizing Recommendations in the Cloud Console.

questions.explanation:
Compute Engine Rightsizing Recommendations analyze CPU and memory utilization from running VMs over time and recommend an appropriate machine type, including smaller configurations when resources are underused. Deploying the workload with settings comparable to the existing VM, observing it under representative normal traffic, and applying those recommendations supports cost-efficient CPU and memory sizing.

**Learn more:** [Apply machine type recommendations to VM instances](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instances/apply-machine-type-recommendations-for-instances)

For this question, refer to the Dress4Win case study. Which compute service can be migrated as-is while still providing an architecture optimized for cloud performance?

options.text: Web applications deployed using App Engine standard environment
RabbitMQ deployed using an unmanaged instance group
Hadoop/Spark deployed using Cloud Dataproc Regional in High Availability mode
Jenkins, monitoring, bastion hosts, security scanners services deployed on custom machine types

questions.explanation:
Cloud Dataproc is a managed Hadoop and Spark platform, so it can host the existing analytics and real-time trending workloads without replacing their processing framework. Configuring Dataproc in Hadoop high-availability mode provides three master instances and keeps HDFS and YARN operating through a single master-node failure or reboot, supporting a performant, resilient deployment.

**Learn more:** [High availability mode | Dataproc | Google Cloud Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/dataproc/docs/concepts/configuring-clusters/high-availability) · [Dataproc FAQ | Google Cloud Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/dataproc/docs/resources/faq)

Your company runs an application composed of multiple microservices on Anthos clusters (formerly Anthos GKE). The cluster has both Anthos Service Mesh and Anthos Config Management configured. End users report that the application is responding very slowly. You want to determine which microservice is causing the delay. What should you do?

options.text: Use the Service Mesh visualization in the Cloud Console to inspect the telemetry between the microservices.

Use Anthos Config Management to create a ClusterSelector selecting the relevant cluster. On the Google Cloud Console page for Google Kubernetes Engine, view the Workloads and filter on the cluster. Inspect the configurations of the filtered workloads.

Use Anthos Config Management to create a namespaceSelector selecting the relevant cluster namespace. On the Google Cloud Console page for Google Kubernetes Engine, visit the workloads and filter on the namespace. Inspect the configurations of the filtered workloads.
Reinstall istio using the default istio profile in order to collect request latency. Evaluate the telemetry between the microservices in the Cloud Console.

questions.explanation:
Anthos Service Mesh telemetry in the Google Cloud console provides service-level latency metrics, service-to-service traffic details, and a topology visualization. Inspecting that visualization and its communication-edge performance reveals the microservice responsible for elevated latency. Anthos Config Management is for managing configuration, not analyzing runtime service latency.

**Learn more:** [Observability overview | Cloud Service Mesh](https://docs.cloud.google.com/service-mesh/docs/observability-overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A lead software engineer says that a new application design uses WebSockets and HTTP sessions that are not shared across the web servers. You want to help ensure that the application will operate properly on Google Cloud Platform.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Help the engineer to convert his websocket code to use HTTP streaming
Review the encryption requirements for websocket connections with the security team
Meet with the cloud operations team and the engineer to discuss load balancer options
Help the engineer redesign the application to use a distributed user session service that does not rely on websockets and HTTP sessions.

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud HTTP(S)-based Application Load Balancers support WebSockets and can use session affinity to direct related requests from a client to the same backend. Load-balancer options and their affinity behavior should therefore be reviewed with the cloud operations team to accommodate server-local HTTP session state.

**Learn more:** [External Application Load Balancer overview](https://cloud.google.com/load-balancing/docs/https) · [Request distribution for external Application Load Balancers](https://cloud.google.com/load-balancing/docs/https/request-distribution)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],To lower costs, the Director of Engineering has directed all developers to migrate their development infrastructure resources from on-premises virtual machines (VMs) to Google Cloud Platform. These resources undergo several start/stop events each day and need state to be retained. You have been asked to design how to run a development environment in Google Cloud while giving the finance department cost visibility.  
  
Which two steps should you take? (Choose two.)

options.text: Use the - -no-auto-delete flag on all persistent disks and stop the VM
Use the - -auto-delete flag on all persistent disks and terminate the VM
Apply VM CPU utilization label and include it in the BigQuery billing export
Use Google BigQuery billing export and labels to associate cost to groups
Store all state into local SSD, snapshot the persistent disks, and terminate the VM
Store all state in Google Cloud Storage, snapshot the persistent disks, and terminate the VM

questions.explanation:
Persistent Disk provides durable storage that is retained with a stopped VM, and disabling automatic disk deletion protects the disks from deletion with the VM. Cloud Billing export to BigQuery includes resource and project label information, so labels can associate and analyze costs by groups for finance reporting.

**Learn more:** [Stop or restart a Compute Engine instance](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instances/stop-start-instance) · [Modify a Persistent Disk or Google Cloud Hyperdisk's settings](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/disks/modify-persistent-disk)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],As part of its disaster-recovery plan, your company is attempting to replicate its production MySQL database from its private data center to its GCP project over a Google Cloud VPN connection. It is encountering latency issues and a small degree of packet loss that is interrupting replication.  
  
What should it do?

options.text: Configure their replication to use UDP.
Configure a Google Cloud Dedicated Interconnect.
Restore their database daily using Google Cloud SQL.
Add additional VPN connections and load balance them.
Send the replicated transaction to Google Cloud Pub/Sub.

questions.explanation:
Dedicated Interconnect creates a direct physical connection between an on-premises network and Google’s network. Cloud Interconnect is intended to provide low-latency, highly available connectivity, which avoids the unreliable VPN path that is causing replication disruption.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Interconnect overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/network-connectivity/docs/interconnect/concepts/overview?hl=en) · [Dedicated Interconnect overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/network-connectivity/docs/interconnect/concepts/dedicated-overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You must develop procedures to validate disaster-recovery resilience for remote recovery using GCP. Your production environment runs on-premises, and you need to create a secure, redundant connection between the on-premises network and the GCP network.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Verify that Dedicated Interconnect can replicate files to GCP. Verify that direct peering can establish a secure connection between your networks if Dedicated Interconnect fails.
Verify that Dedicated Interconnect can replicate files to GCP. Verify that Cloud VPN can establish a secure connection between your networks if Dedicated Interconnect fails.
Verify that the Transfer Appliance can replicate files to GCP. Verify that direct peering can establish a secure connection between your networks if the Transfer Appliance fails.
Verify that the Transfer Appliance can replicate files to GCP. Verify that Cloud VPN can establish a secure connection between your networks if the Transfer Appliance fails.

questions.explanation:
Dedicated Interconnect provides direct connectivity between an on-premises network and Google’s network for the primary replication path. Cloud VPN securely extends a peer network to a VPC through encrypted IPsec tunnels, making it an appropriate secure failover connection. Transfer Appliance is intended for bulk data transfer, typically by shipping a physical appliance, rather than continuous remote recovery replication.

**Learn more:** [Dedicated Interconnect overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/network-connectivity/docs/interconnect/concepts/dedicated-overview) · [Cloud VPN overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/network-connectivity/docs/vpn/concepts/overview)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],For this question, refer to the Mountkirk Games case study. Mountkirk Games asks you to design a method to test the analytics platform’s resilience to variations in mobile network latency. What should you do?

options.text: Deploy failure injection software to the game analytics platform that can inject additional latency to mobile client analytics traffic.

Build a test client that can be run from a mobile phone emulator on a Compute Engine virtual machine, and run multiple copies in Google Cloud Platform regions all over the world to generate realistic traffic.
Add the ability to introduce a random amount of delay before beginning to process analytics files uploaded from mobile devices.
Create an opt-in beta of the game that runs on players' mobile devices and collects response times from analytics endpoints running in Google Cloud Platform regions all over the world.

questions.explanation:
Controlled fault injection can introduce delays that simulate network latency, allowing the platform’s behavior under the specified failure condition to be measured safely and repeatably. Injecting added latency into mobile-client analytics traffic directly tests tolerance of changing mobile network latency.

**Learn more:** [Patterns for scalable and resilient apps](https://cloud.google.com/architecture/scalable-and-resilient-apps) · [Fault Injection Testing overview](https://cloud.google.com/fault-injection-testing/overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company offers a recommendation engine to retail customers. You provide those retail customers an API through which they can submit a user ID, and the API returns a list of recommendations for that user.  
  
You are responsible for the API lifecycle and want to ensure stability for your customers if the API undergoes backward-incompatible changes. You want to follow Google-recommended practices. What should you do?

options.text: Create a distribution list of all customers to inform them of an upcoming backward-incompatible change at least one month before replacing the old API with the new API.
Create an automated process to generate API documentation, and update the public API documentation as part of the CI/CD process when deploying an update to the API.
Use a versioning strategy for the APIs that increases the version number on every backward-incompatible change.
Use a versioning strategy for the APIs that adds the suffix ג€DEPRECATEDג€ to the current API version number on every backward-incompatible change. Use the current version number for the new API.

questions.explanation:
Backward-incompatible changes require a new major API version so existing clients can continue using the version they were built against. Google Cloud recommends incrementing the major version when a change breaks customers' client code, and supports running multiple major API versions concurrently.

**Learn more:** [Versioning an API | Cloud Endpoints with OpenAPI](https://docs.cloud.google.com/endpoints/docs/openapi/versioning-an-api?hl=en)
