Refer to the EHR Healthcare case study. You must define the technical architecture for hybrid connectivity between EHR's on-premises systems and Google Cloud. You want to follow Google's recommended practices for production-level applications. Given the EHR Healthcare business and technical requirements, what should you do?

options.text: Configure two Partner Interconnect connections in one metro (City), and make sure the Interconnect connections are placed in different metro zones.
Configure two VPN connections from on-premises to Google Cloud, and make sure the VPN devices on-premises are in separate racks.
Configure Direct Peering between EHR Healthcare and Google Cloud, and make sure you are peering at least two Google locations.
Configure two Dedicated Interconnect connections in one metro (City) and two connections in another metro, and make sure the Interconnect connections are placed in different metro zones.

questions.explanation:
Google’s production-level, 99.99% availability topology requires four Cloud Interconnect connections across two metropolitan areas: two Dedicated Interconnect connections in each metro, with the connections in a given metro placed in separate edge availability domains. This design protects connectivity from individual connection failures and avoids coordinated maintenance risk within a metro.

**Learn more:** [Topology for production-level applications overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/network-connectivity/docs/interconnect/tutorials/production-level-overview) · [Dedicated Interconnect overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/network-connectivity/docs/interconnect/concepts/dedicated-overview)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are implementing Firestore for Mountkirk Games. Mountkirk Games wants to provide a new game with programmatic access to a legacy game's Firestore database.  
  
Access must be as restricted as possible. What should you do?

options.text: Create a service account (SA) in the legacy game's Google Cloud project, add a second SA in the new game's IAM page, and then give the Organization Admin role to both SAs.
Create a service account (SA) in the legacy game's Google Cloud project, give the SA the Organization Admin role, and then give it the Firebase Admin role in both projects.
Create a service account (SA) in the legacy game's Google Cloud project, add this SA in the new game's IAM page, and then give it the Firebase Admin role in both projects.
Create a service account (SA) in the legacy game's Google Cloud project, give it the Firebase Admin role, and then migrate the new game to the legacy game's project.

questions.explanation:
Service accounts are IAM principals that can be granted roles on project resources, including projects other than the project in which the service account was created. Granting the service account the Firebase Admin role in each relevant project provides Firebase-level administrative access without the organization-wide privileges of the Organization Admin role or a project migration.

**Learn more:** [Manage project access with Firebase IAM](https://firebase.google.com/docs/projects/iam/overview) · [Service accounts overview](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/service-account-overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company is developing containerized applications as part of its CI/CD pipeline. To enhance the security and maintainability of the build process, you need to:  
  
- Identify potential vulnerabilities in your container images.  
- Generate verifiable metadata about builds for auditing and compliance.  
- Create a comprehensive inventory of your application’s dependencies.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Use Cloud Build to build container images, and then trigger Artifact Analysis on images pushed to Artifact Registry.
Use Cloud Build to build container images, trigger Binary Authorization, and use Cloud Asset Inventory for tracking and analysis.
Use Cloud Build to build container images, push the images to Artifact Registry, and use Security Command Center for tracking and analysis.
Use Cloud Build to build container images, trigger Binary Authorization, and use Security Command Center for tracking and analysis.

questions.explanation:
Artifact Analysis scans container images in Artifact Registry for vulnerabilities and detects dependency and license metadata. It can generate an SBOM, which is a machine-readable inventory of an application’s packages and dependencies. Cloud Build can generate verifiable SLSA build provenance for container images stored in Artifact Registry, and Artifact Analysis stores the associated build metadata for audit and compliance use.

**Learn more:** [Generate and validate build provenance | Cloud Build](https://docs.cloud.google.com/build/docs/securing-builds/generate-validate-build-provenance) · [Container scanning overview | Artifact Analysis](https://docs.cloud.google.com/artifact-analysis/docs/container-scanning-overview)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company runs its application workloads on Compute Engine. The applications are deployed in production, acceptance, and development environments. The production environment is business-critical and operates 24/7, whereas the acceptance and development environments are critical only during office hours. Your CFO has asked you to optimize these environments for cost savings during idle periods. What should you do?

options.text: Create a shell script that uses the gcloud command to change the machine type of the development and acceptance instances to a smaller machine type outside of office hours. Schedule the shell script on one of the production instances to automate the task.
Use Cloud Scheduler to trigger a Cloud Function that will stop the development and acceptance environments after office hours and start them just before office hours.
Deploy the development and acceptance applications on a managed instance group and enable autoscaling.
Use regular Compute Engine instances for the production environment, and use preemptible VMs for the acceptance and development environments.

questions.explanation:
Stopping Compute Engine instances outside required hours removes VM CPU usage charges while they are stopped, although attached resources can still incur charges. Scheduling the acceptance and development environments to stop after office hours and start before office hours provides the required availability while reducing idle-time costs; production remains continuously available.

**Learn more:** [Schedule a Compute Engine VM to start or stop](https://cloud.google.com/scheduler/docs/start-and-stop-compute-engine-instances-on-a-schedule) · [Suspend, stop, or reset Compute Engine instances](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instances/suspend-stop-reset-instances-overview)

questions.question:
Your web application uses Google Kubernetes Engine to manage several workloads. One workload needs a consistent set of hostnames even after pods scale and relaunch.  
  
Which Kubernetes feature should you use to achieve this?

options.text: StatefulSets
Role-based access control
Container environment variables
Persistent Volumes

questions.explanation:
A StatefulSet manages Pods with persistent, unique identities. Its Pods receive stable ordinal-based names and network identities that are retained across rescheduling, scaling, and replacement, supporting consistent hostnames.\
\
**Learn more:** [StatefulSets | Kubernetes](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/statefulset/)

questions.question:
Your web application uses Google Kubernetes Engine to manage several workloads. One workload needs a consistent set of hostnames even after pods scale and relaunch.  
  
Which Kubernetes feature should you use to achieve this?

options.text: Use Dataprep to ingest the transactions.
Use Dataflow to process the streaming data.
Use a Dataproc cluster for both the streaming and batch workloads.
Use BigQuery for the batch analytics reports.
Use Firestore to store and analyze the transaction data.

questions.explanation:
Dataflow is a fully managed, scalable service for streaming data processing, making it appropriate for real-time fraud-detection processing. BigQuery is a fully managed serverless data warehouse for running complex analytical SQL queries and reporting on the transaction data. Together, they meet the real-time and daily batch-reporting requirements without managing processing clusters.

**Learn more:** [Dataflow overview](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/overview) · [BigQuery overview](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/introduction)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have created several preemptible Linux virtual machine instances with Google Compute Engine. You want to shut down your application properly before the virtual machines are preempted.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create a shutdown script named k99.shutdown in the /etc/rc.6.d/ directory
Create a shutdown script registered as a xinetd service in Linux and configure a Stackdriver endpoint check to call the service
Create a shutdown script and use it as the value for a new metadata entry with the key shutdown-script in the Cloud Platform Console when you create the new virtual machine instance

Create a shutdown script, registered as a xinetd service in Linux, and use the gcloud compute instances add-metadata command to specify the service URL as the value for a new metadata entry with the key shutdown-script-url

questions.explanation:
Compute Engine runs a Linux shutdown script specified in instance metadata with the `shutdown-script` key when a preemptible VM receives a preemption notice, providing a best-effort period of up to 30 seconds for cleanup. Supplying the script as the value of that metadata key during VM creation configures this behavior.

**Learn more:** [Create and use preemptible VMs](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instances/create-use-preemptible) · [Run shutdown scripts](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/shutdownscript)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has announced that it will outsource operations functions. You want to enable developers to easily stage new versions of a cloud-based application in the production environment, while allowing the outsourced operations team to independently promote staged versions to production. You also want to minimize the solution's operational overhead. Which Google Cloud product should you migrate to?

options.text: App Engine
GKE On-Prem
Compute Engine
Google Kubernetes Engine

questions.explanation:
App Engine is a fully managed application platform that supports deploying a new version with traffic promotion disabled, so it can be staged in the production environment. Authorized operators can subsequently migrate traffic to that version independently. This version-and-traffic model requires substantially less infrastructure and cluster administration than Compute Engine or Google Kubernetes Engine.

**Learn more:** [Test and deploy your application — App Engine standard environment](https://cloud.google.com/appengine/docs/standard/testing-and-deploying-your-app) · [Migrating traffic — App Engine standard environment](https://cloud.google.com/appengine/docs/standard/migrating-traffic)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has a Google Cloud project that uses BigQuery for data warehousing. The VPN tunnel between the on-premises environment and Google Cloud is configured with Cloud VPN. Your security team wants to prevent data exfiltration by malicious insiders, compromised code, and accidental oversharing. What should you do?

options.text: Configure Private Service Connect.
Configure VPC Service Controls and configure Private Google Access for on-promises hosts.
Create a service account, grant the BigQuery JobUser role and Storage Object Viewer role to the service account, and remove all other Identity and Access Management (IAM) access from the project.
Configure Private Google Access.

questions.explanation:
VPC Service Controls creates a security perimeter around BigQuery and other supported Google Cloud services, limiting unauthorized data access and egress even when an identity otherwise has IAM permissions. Private Google Access for on-premises hosts lets hosts connected through Cloud VPN access protected Google APIs through the VPC; using it with the service perimeter supports secure private access from the on-premises environment.

**Learn more:** [Overview of VPC Service Controls](https://cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/overview) · [Private Google Access with VPC Service Controls](https://cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/private-connectivity)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are monitoring Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) clusters in a Cloud Monitoring workspace. As a Site Reliability Engineer (SRE), you must triage incidents quickly. What should you do?

options.text: Navigate the predefined dashboards in the Cloud Monitoring workspace, and then add metrics and create alert policies.
Navigate the predefined dashboards in the Cloud Monitoring workspace, create custom metrics, and install alerting software on a Compute Engine instance.
Write a shell script that gathers metrics from GKE nodes, publish these metrics to a Pub/Sub topic, export the data to BigQuery, and make a Data Studio dashboard.
Create a custom dashboard in the Cloud Monitoring workspace for each incident, and then add metrics and create alert policies.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Monitoring provides predefined GKE dashboards with relevant cluster and workload metrics, and GKE supports alert policies based on Cloud Monitoring metrics. Using these dashboards and configuring appropriate metrics and alert policies provides the built-in workflow for rapid incident detection and triage.

**Learn more:** [View observability metrics | Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE)](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/view-observability-metrics) · [Observability for GKE | Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE)](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/observability)

questions.question:
You deploy a custom Java application to Google App Engine. The deployment fails and produces the following stack trace.  
  
What should you do?  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783765525454-rpylm1ve.png)

options.text: Upload missing JAR files and redeploy your application.
Digitally sign all of your JAR files and redeploy your application
Recompile the CLoakedServlet class using and MD5 hash instead of SHA1

questions.explanation: A SHA1 digest error from Java’s JAR verifier means a class file does not match the integrity digest stored in its signed JAR’s manifest. Re-signing the JAR files regenerates signature metadata that matches the deployed contents; missing JARs and changing the class compilation to MD5 do not correct that manifest-digest mismatch.

questions.question: Your web application runs several VM instances in a VPC. You need to limit communication between instances to only the authorized paths and ports, without depending on static IP addresses or subnets because the application can autoscale. How should you restrict communication?

options.text: Use separate VPCs to restrict traffic
Use firewall rules based on network tags attached to the compute instances
Use Cloud DNS and only allow connections from authorized hostnames
Use service accounts and configure the web application to authorize particular service accounts to have access

questions.explanation: VPC firewall rules can use network tags as source and target selectors, so authorized traffic can be limited by protocol and port between appropriately tagged VM instances. Instances created through autoscaling receive the relevant tags without requiring static IP-address or subnet-based rules.

For this question, refer to the TerramEarth case study.  
  
You are developing a microservice-based application for TerramEarth that uses Docker containers. You want to follow Google-recommended practices to continuously build the application and store its build artifacts. What should you do?

options.text: Configure a trigger in Cloud Build for new source changes. Invoke Cloud Build to build container images for each microservice, and tag them using the code commit hash. Push the images to the Container Registry.

Configure a trigger in Cloud Build for new source changes. The trigger invokes build jobs and build container images for the microservices. Tag the images with a version number, and push them to Cloud Storage.

Create a Scheduler job to check the repo every minute. For any new change, invoke Cloud Build to build container images for the microservices. Tag the images using the current timestamp, and push them to the Container Registry.
Configure a trigger in Cloud Build for new source changes. Invoke Cloud Build to build one container image, and tag the image with the label 'latest.' Push the image to the Container Registry.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Build triggers can automatically start builds when source changes are pushed. Building a distinct container image for each microservice preserves independent deployability, while tagging each image with its source commit hash provides an immutable, traceable association between the artifact and the code revision. Container images should be stored in a container registry rather than Cloud Storage; current Google Cloud guidance uses Artifact Registry as the successor to Container Registry.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Build triggers](https://docs.cloud.google.com/build/docs/triggers) · [Substituting variable values in Cloud Build](https://docs.cloud.google.com/build/docs/configuring-builds/substitute-variable-values)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company plans to begin using Google Cloud resources but wants to keep its on-premises Active Directory domain controller for identity management.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Use the Admin Directory API to authenticate against the Active Directory domain controller.
Use Google Cloud Directory Sync to synchronize Active Directory usernames with cloud identities and configure SAML SSO.
Use Cloud Identity-Aware Proxy configured to use the on-premises Active Directory domain controller as an identity provider.
Use Compute Engine to create an Active Directory (AD) domain controller that is a replica of the on-premises AD domain controller using Google Cloud Directory Sync.

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud Directory Sync synchronizes Active Directory users and groups into Cloud Identity, while SAML single sign-on delegates authentication to the external identity provider backed by Active Directory. This keeps the on-premises Active Directory environment as the authoritative identity system and avoids synchronizing passwords.

**Learn more:** [Federate Google Cloud with Active Directory](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/identity/federating-gcp-with-active-directory-introduction) · [Active Directory single sign-on](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/identity/federating-gcp-with-active-directory-configuring-single-sign-on?hl=en)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A lead engineer created a custom tool to deploy virtual machines in the legacy data center. He wants to migrate this custom tool to the new cloud environment.  
  
You want to advocate adopting Google Cloud Deployment Manager.  
  
What are two business risks of migrating to Cloud Deployment Manager? (Choose two.)

options.text: Cloud Deployment Manager uses Python
Cloud Deployment Manager APIs could be deprecated in the future
Cloud Deployment Manager is unfamiliar to the company's engineers
Cloud Deployment Manager requires a Google APIs service account to run
Cloud Deployment Manager can be used to permanently delete cloud resources
Cloud Deployment Manager only supports automation of Google Cloud resources

questions.explanation: A managed deployment service can be deprecated or retired, creating lifecycle, migration, and continuity risk. Adopting an unfamiliar deployment system also requires engineers to acquire new skills and operational experience, which creates training, productivity, and delivery risk.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has engaged an external auditing firm for a compliance audit. Company governance requires that external auditors be managed through one Google Group, which receives temporary, read-only access to a Cloud Storage bucket named `audit-evidence-bucket`.  
  
Access must be traceable to each individual auditor’s identity and remain active only for the audit engagement, which lasts the full month of October. You need a secure access-control approach that avoids administrative overhead and meets the company’s governance policy. What should you do?

options.text: Apply an IAM policy binding that grants the roles/storage.objectViewer role to the Google Group. Configure this binding with a time-based IAM Condition that automatically grants access from October 1 to November 1.
Create a service account, and grant it the roles/storage.objectViewer role on the bucket. Generate and share Signed URLs for each object in the bucket with an expiration date of November 1.

Use Cloud Scheduler to run a Cloud Run functions script that adds the IAM binding of roles/storage.objectViewer to the Google Group on October 1 and another that removes the IAM binding on November 1.
Use Workforce Identity Federation to map the auditors’ group to the Google Group. Bind the roles/storage.objectViewer role to this Google Group. Configure a 1-month session duration on the provider.

questions.explanation:
A conditional IAM role binding can grant `roles/storage.objectViewer` to the required Google Group while a date/time condition limits authorization to the October audit window, such as `request.time >= timestamp('YYYY-10-01T00:00:00Z') && request.time < timestamp('YYYY-11-01T00:00:00Z')`. Auditors access Cloud Storage using their individual identities as group members, preserving per-user audit attribution. Cloud Storage supports date/time IAM Conditions on bucket policy bindings; uniform bucket-level access must be enabled for conditions set directly on a bucket.

**Learn more:** [Identity and Access Management for Cloud Storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/access-control/iam) · [Set and manage IAM policies on buckets](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/access-control/using-iam-permissions)

What should they do?

Configure their load balancer to pass through the User-Agent HTTP header when the value matches GoogleStackdriverMonitoring-UptimeChecks (https:// cloud.google.com/monitoring)
Configure their legacy web servers to allow requests that contain user-Agent HTTP header when the value matches GoogleStackdriverMonitoring- UptimeChecks (https://cloud.google.com/monitoring)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Refer to the TerramEarth case study for this question. You have decomposed a legacy monolithic application into several containerized RESTful microservices.  
  
You want to run these microservices on Cloud Run and ensure that the services are highly available with low latency for your customers. What should you do?

options.text: Deploy Cloud Run services to multiple availability zones. Create Cloud Endpoints that point to the services. Create a global HTTP(S) Load Balancing instance and attach the Cloud Endpoints to its backend.

Deploy Cloud Run services to multiple regions. Create serverless network endpoint groups pointing to the services. Add the serverless NEGs to a backend service that is used by a global HTTP(S) Load Balancing instance.
Deploy Cloud Run services to multiple regions. In Cloud DNS, create a latency-based DNS name that points to the services.
Deploy Cloud Run services to multiple availability zones. Create a TCP/IP global load balancer. Add the Cloud Run Endpoints to its backend service.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Run services are regional resources, so high availability across regional failures requires deployments in multiple regions. A global external HTTP(S) load balancer uses serverless network endpoint groups (NEGs) as Cloud Run backends and routes users toward the closest available regional backend, reducing latency while providing a multi-region architecture.

**Learn more:** [Serve traffic from multiple regions](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/multiple-regions?hl=en) · [Serverless network endpoint groups overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/load-balancing/docs/negs/serverless-neg-concepts?authuser=108)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are designing the storage setup for a critical Cloud Storage bucket. The bucket will store trade-confirmation documents for a financial services company. These documents are immutable and function as a legal record. Your design must meet two primary data-protection requirements:  
  
- The system must support rapid recovery of any document accidentally deleted or maliciously overwritten.  
- After a document is written, it must be impossible for anyone, including administrators, to delete or modify it for seven years.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Grant only the roles/storage.objectCreator IAM role to the application's service account. Remove all other admin permissions from the bucket.
Use Storage Transfer Service to create a daily replication job that synchronizes the bucket to a separate archive bucket in another region.
Configure an Object Lifecycle Management rule on the bucket to ensure all objects are retained for at least seven years before they can be deleted.
Enable Object Versioning on the bucket. Additionally, configure the bucket with a Bucket Lock and a retention policy of seven years.

questions.explanation:
Object Versioning preserves prior object generations as noncurrent versions when a live object is deleted or replaced, allowing recovery. A Bucket Lock with a seven-year retention policy prevents objects from being deleted or replaced before the retention period expires; locking the policy prevents it from being removed or shortened, including by administrators.

**Learn more:** [Object Versioning | Cloud Storage](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/object-versioning) · [Bucket Lock | Cloud Storage](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/bucket-lock)

You want to deploy a Compute Engine application in one VPC spanning two regions. The application must communicate with an on-premises network over VPN.  
  
How should the VPN be deployed?

options.text: Use VPC Network Peering between the VPC and the on-premises network.
Expose the VPC to the on-premises network using IAM and VPC Sharing.
Create a global Cloud VPN Gateway with VPN tunnels from each region to the on-premises peer gateway.
Deploy Cloud VPN Gateway in each region. Ensure that each region has at least one VPN tunnel to the on-premises peer gateway.

questions.explanation:
Each Cloud VPN gateway is a regional resource. A multi-region deployment therefore uses a Cloud VPN gateway in each region, with at least one VPN tunnel from each regional gateway to the on-premises peer gateway.\
\
**Learn more:** [Cloud VPN overview](https://cloud.google.com/network-connectivity/docs/vpn/concepts/overview)

questions.question:

How should the VPN be deployed?

options.text: 1. Mount the Cloud Storage bucket using gcsfuse on all backend Compute Engine instances. 2. Serve music files directly from the backend Compute Engine instance.

1. Create a Cloud Filestore NFS volume and attach it to the backend Compute Engine instances. 2. Download popular songs in Cloud Filestore. 3. Serve music files directly from the backend Compute Engine instance.
1. Copy popular songs into CloudSQL as a blob. 2. Update application code to retrieve data from CloudSQL when Cloud Storage is overloaded.

1. Create a managed instance group with Compute Engine instances. 2. Create a global load balancer and configure it with two backends: ג—‹ Managed instance group ג—‹ Cloud Storage bucket 3. Enable Cloud CDN on the bucket backend.

A global external Application Load Balancer can route application traffic to a managed instance group and static media requests to a Cloud Storage backend bucket. Cloud CDN on the backend bucket caches popular music at Google's edge, reducing load on the Cloud Storage origin and improving delivery performance during demand spikes. A managed instance group also allows the Compute Engine application tier to scale beyond the fixed instance count.

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are monitoring Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) clusters in a Cloud Monitoring workspace. As a Site Reliability Engineer (SRE), you must triage incidents rapidly. What should you do?

options.text: 1. Navigate the predefined dashboards in the Cloud Monitoring workspace.2. Add metrics and create alert policies.
1. Write a shell script that gathers metrics from GKE nodes, and publish these metrics to a Pub/Sub topic.2. Export the data to BigQuery. and make a Data Studio dashboard.
1. Create a custom dashboard in the Cloud Monitoring workspace for each incident.2. Add metrics and create alert policies.
1. Navigate the predefined dashboards in the Cloud Monitoring workspace.2. Create custom metrics and install alerting software on a Compute Engine instance.

Cloud Monitoring provides predefined GKE dashboards for viewing cluster and workload observability metrics, so they support rapid incident investigation without building a new dashboard or data-collection pipeline. Alert policies on the relevant metrics provide proactive notification when monitored conditions are met.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],TerramEarth's 20 million vehicles are distributed worldwide. Based on each vehicle's location, its telemetry data is stored in a Google Cloud Storage (GCS) regional bucket (US, Europe, or Asia). The CTO has asked you to run a report on the raw telemetry data to identify why vehicles are breaking down after 100 K miles. You want to run this job across all the data.  
  
What is the most cost-effective way to run this job?

options.text: Move all the data into 1 zone, then launch a Cloud Dataproc cluster to run the job
Move all the data into 1 region, then launch a Google Cloud Dataproc cluster to run the job
Launch a cluster in each region to preprocess and compress the raw data, then move the data into a multi-region bucket and use a Dataproc cluster to finish the job
Launch a cluster in each region to preprocess and compress the raw data, then move the data into a region bucket and use a Cloud Dataproc cluster to finish the job

questions.explanation:
Preprocessing and compressing telemetry in its source regions minimizes the volume of chargeable inter-region data transfer. Consolidating the reduced output in a single regional bucket and running the final Dataproc workload in that same region avoids unnecessary multi-region replication and keeps storage colocated with compute, which reduces latency and transfer costs.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Storage pricing](https://cloud.google.com/storage/pricing) · [Dataproc best practices guide](https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/developers-practitioners/dataproc-best-practices-guide)

questions.question:
Your organization needs to manage IAM policies independently for different departments while retaining central control.  
  
Which approach should you use?

options.text: Multiple Organizations with multiple Folders
Multiple Organizations, one for each department
A single Organization with Folders for each department
A single Organization with multiple projects, each with a central owner

questions.explanation:
A single Google Cloud Organization provides centralized ownership and governance. Folders can map to departments and act as IAM policy inheritance boundaries, allowing department-level IAM administration over the projects and resources within each folder.\
\
**Learn more:** [Resource Manager overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/resource-manager-overview) · [Access control for folders with IAM](https://cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/access-control-folders)

questions.question:
Your organization needs to manage IAM policies independently for different departments while retaining central control.  
  
Which approach should you use?

options.text: Use an external Application Load Balancer to serve your application APIs.
Use Cloud CDN to serve static assets of your application.
Use Media CDN to serve static assets of your application
Use Memorystore to serve your web application.
Use a multi-region Cloud Storage bucket to serve your entire web application.

questions.explanation:
A global external Application Load Balancer provides a global anycast front end and routes HTTP(S) application API traffic to appropriate backends. Cloud CDN is optimized to cache static web assets such as CSS, JavaScript, and images at Google’s edge locations. Google Cloud specifically recommends this combination for social-media workloads; Media CDN is optimized for streaming video and high-throughput downloads, not for serving static web assets.

**Learn more:** [Choose a CDN product](https://docs.cloud.google.com/cdn/docs/choose-cdn-product) · [Cloud Load Balancing overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/load-balancing/docs/load-balancing-overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building a globally scaled frontend for a legacy streaming-backend data API. The API requires events in strict chronological order and without repeated data for correct processing.  
  
Which products should you deploy to guarantee once-only FIFO (first-in, first-out) data delivery?

options.text: Cloud Pub/Sub alone
Cloud Pub/Sub to Cloud Dataflow
Cloud Pub/Sub to Stackdriver
Cloud Pub/Sub to Cloud SQL

questions.explanation:
Pub/Sub alone only guarantees ordering and exactly-once delivery within a single region via ordering keys, so it cannot alone satisfy strict chronological, duplicate-free processing for a globally scaled frontend whose publishers/subscribers span regions. Cloud Dataflow adds the windowing, buffering, and stateful deduplication needed to reorder and dedupe a global stream before it reaches the legacy API, which is why Pub/Sub feeding into Dataflow is required.

**Learn more:** [Pub/Sub to Dataflow streaming](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/concepts/streaming-with-cloud-pubsub) · [Pub/Sub message ordering](https://cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/ordering)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are designing an observability strategy for a new microservices application running on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). The application contains multiple services (for example, frontend, orders, and payments). During load testing, you see an error in the frontend service logs, but cannot locate the corresponding logs in downstream services to investigate the root cause because the logs are not correlated. You need to implement a solution that lets you follow one user request across every microservice involved in the transaction. The solution must not require developers to manually add correlation logic to application code. What should you do?

options.text: Implement Cloud Trace by ensuring the traceparent header is propagated between microservice calls to link logs to a single trace.
Configure all containers to write logs to STDOUT/STDERR, and then filter logs by pod name and timestamp in the Logs Explorer.
Require developers to generate a unique correlation-id at the frontend, and manually add it as a field to every log message in all services.
Create custom metrics in Cloud Monitoring for error counts in each service and correlate incident spikes using a shared dashboard.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Trace uses trace context propagation, including the W3C `traceparent` header, to associate spans generated by calls across microservices with one trace ID. Cloud Logging can use that trace association to view all logs for the trace, providing request-level troubleshooting without implementing a custom correlation ID in every service.

**Learn more:** [Trace context | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/trace/docs/trace-context?hl=en) · [Correlate log entries | Cloud Logging | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/view/correlate-logs)

questions.domain: Analyzing and optimizing technical and business processes
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has built a monolithic, three-tier application that lets external users upload and share files. The solution is difficult to enhance and is not reliable. The development team wants to rearchitect the application to use microservices and a fully managed service approach, but must persuade leadership that the effort is valuable. Which advantage(s) should they emphasize to leadership?

options.text: The new approach will be significantly less costly, make it easier to manage the underlying infrastructure, and automatically manage the CI/CD pipelines.
The monolithic solution can be converted to a container with Docker. The generated container can then be deployed into a Kubernetes cluster.

The new approach will make it easier to decouple infrastructure from application, develop and release new features, manage the underlying infrastructure, manage CI/CD pipelines and perform A/B testing, and scale the solution if necessary.
The process can be automated with Migrate for Compute Engine.

questions.explanation:
Microservices create loosely coupled components that can be developed, deployed, released, and scaled independently, improving change velocity and resilience compared with a tightly coupled monolith. Fully managed services reduce the operational burden of underlying infrastructure, and managed delivery tooling can provide CI/CD and traffic-splitting capabilities for controlled releases and A/B testing. Google Cloud documents independent deployment and scaling for modular services, managed infrastructure benefits, and deployment traffic splitting.

**Learn more:** [Patterns for scalable and resilient apps](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/scalable-and-resilient-apps) · [Automate and manage change](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/framework/operational-excellence/automate-and-manage-change)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization must retain metrics from every application for 5 years so they can be analyzed in potential future legal proceedings.  
  
Which approach should you use?

options.text: Grant the security team access to the logs in each Project
Configure Stackdriver Monitoring for all Projects, and export to BigQuery
Configure Stackdriver Monitoring for all Projects with the default retention policies
Configure Stackdriver Monitoring for all Projects, and export to Google Cloud Storage

questions.explanation:
Cloud Monitoring deletes metric data after its applicable retention period, so its default retention cannot satisfy a five-year requirement. Exporting metrics to BigQuery supports long-term retention and SQL-based analysis of historical metric data; the retention configuration must ensure the exported data is not expired before five years.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Monitoring metric export](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/monitoring-metric-export?hl=en) · [Retention and latency of metric data](https://docs.cloud.google.com/monitoring/api/v3/latency-n-retention)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],For this question, refer to the TerramEarth case study. You begin building a new application that uses a few Cloud Functions for the backend. One use case requires Cloud Function `func_display` to invoke another Cloud Function, `func_query`. You want `func_query` to accept invocations only from `func_display`. You also want to follow Google's recommended best practices. What should you do?

options.text: Create a token and pass it in as an environment variable to func_display. When invoking func_query, include the token in the request. Pass the same token to func_query and reject the invocation if the tokens are different.

Make func_query 'Require authentication.' Create a unique service account and associate it to func_display. Grant the service account invoker role for func_query. Create an id token in func_display and include the token to the request when invoking func_query.

Make func_query 'Require authentication' and only accept internal traffic. Create those two functions in the same VPC. Create an ingress firewall rule for func_query to only allow traffic from func_display.

Create those two functions in the same project and VPC. Make func_query only accept internal traffic. Create an ingress firewall for func_query to only allow traffic from func_display. Also, make sure both functions use the same service account.

questions.explanation:
Restricting the target function to authenticated invocations, using a dedicated service account for the calling function, and granting that account only the target function’s invoker IAM role implements least-privilege service-to-service authorization. The caller presents an OIDC ID token, allowing the target to authenticate the service account and enforce its IAM permission.

**Learn more:** [Authenticate for invocation | Cloud Run functions](https://docs.cloud.google.com/functions/docs/securing/authenticating) · [Get an ID token | Google Cloud Authentication](https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/get-id-token)

questions.domain: Managing and provisioning a cloud solution infrastructure
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],The development team has supplied a Kubernetes Deployment file. You do not yet have any infrastructure and must deploy the application. What should you do?

options.text: Use gcloud to create a Kubernetes cluster. Use Deployment Manager to create the deployment.
Use gcloud to create a Kubernetes cluster. Use kubectl to create the deployment.
Use kubectl to create a Kubernetes cluster. Use Deployment Manager to create the deployment.
Use kubectl to create a Kubernetes cluster. Use kubectl to create the deployment.

questions.explanation:
Use `gcloud` to create the Google Kubernetes Engine cluster, then use `kubectl` to submit and manage the Kubernetes Deployment. Google Cloud documentation identifies `gcloud container clusters create-auto` for cluster creation and `kubectl` as the Kubernetes command-line interface for creating Deployments.

**Learn more:** [Deploy an app to a GKE cluster](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/deploy-app-cluster)

questions.domain: Analyzing and optimizing technical and business processes
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783765371112-f0jy29w4.png)  
  
JencoMart’s application migration to Google Cloud Platform (GCP) is moving too slowly. The infrastructure is shown in the diagram. You want to maximize throughput.  
  
What are three possible bottlenecks? (Choose three.)

options.text: A single VPN tunnel, which limits throughput
A tier of Google Cloud Storage that is not suited for this task
A copy command that is not suited to operate over long distances
Fewer virtual machines (VMs) in GCP than on-premises machines
A separate storage layer outside the VMs, which is not suited for this task
Complicated internet connectivity between the on-premises infrastructure and GCP

questions.explanation:
A single Cloud VPN tunnel has a finite bandwidth limit, so it can cap aggregate transfer throughput. A copy operation that does not use parallelism can perform poorly across a high-latency, long-distance connection; parallel composite uploads are available to improve throughput for large Cloud Storage uploads. Routing migration data through a separate storage layer outside the VMs adds an extra write/read transfer stage, which can become an end-to-end throughput constraint.

**Learn more:** [Cloud VPN overview](https://cloud.google.com/network-connectivity/docs/vpn/concepts/overview) · [Parallel composite uploads](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/parallel-composite-uploads)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You created a Cloud Monitoring dashboard for your development environment to view real-time application metrics. The Ops team needs a similar dashboard to monitor the production environment. You want to minimize the time and effort required to help the Ops team with their dashboard request. What should you do?

options.text: Export your dashboard to a JSON file and share it with the Ops team.
Grant viewer permission to the Ops team in your project so they can recreate the charts in their dashboard from the console.
Create a shared document and list every step you performed to create the dashboard. The Ops team can use the document to build their own dashboard.
Share your dashboard and send the shared dashboard URL to the Ops team.

questions.explanation:
A Cloud Monitoring custom dashboard can be saved as a JSON-formatted template and installed in another Google Cloud project. The template carries the dashboard configuration, not its time-series data, allowing the Ops team to create an equivalent production dashboard without manually rebuilding its charts.

**Learn more:** [Create and manage custom dashboards](https://cloud.google.com/monitoring/charts/dashboards)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You manage several internal applications deployed on Compute Engine. Business users report that an application has become very slow during the last few days. You want to identify the root cause so that you can resolve the issue. What should you do first?

options.text: Inspect the logs and metrics from the instances in Cloud Logging and Cloud Monitoring.
Change the Compute Engine Instances behind the application to a machine type with more CPU and memory.
Restore a backup of the application database from a time before the application became slow.
Deploy the applications on a managed instance group with autoscaling enabled. Add a load balancer in front of the managed instance group, and have the users connect to the IP of the load balancer.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Logging and Cloud Monitoring provide the diagnostic evidence needed to identify whether the slowdown is caused by application errors or resource constraints such as CPU, memory, disk, or network utilization. Compute Engine guidance recommends reviewing performance metrics to diagnose performance issues; scaling resources is warranted only when the metrics show sustained resource pressure.

**Learn more:** [Troubleshooting compute instance performance issues](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/troubleshooting/troubleshooting-performance)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A customer wants to perform resilience testing on their authentication layer. It consists of a regional managed instance group that serves a public REST API and reads from and writes to a Cloud SQL instance.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Engage with a security company to run web scrapers that look your for users' authentication data om malicious websites and notify you if any is found.
Deploy intrusion detection software to your virtual machines to detect and log unauthorized access.
Schedule a disaster simulation exercise during which you can shut off all VMs in a zone to see how your application behaves.
Configure a read replica for your Cloud SQL instance in a different zone than the master, and then manually trigger a failover while monitoring KPIs for our REST API.

questions.explanation:
A zonal-failure simulation validates that a regional managed instance group can continue serving the REST API from its remaining zones when all VMs in one zone become unavailable. Cloud SQL read replicas do not provide primary-instance failover; manual failover is for a high-availability primary instance and its standby.

**Learn more:** [Cloud SQL replication overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/mysql/replication) · [Cloud SQL failover API method](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/mysql/admin-api/rest/v1/instances/failover)

questions.domain: Designing and planning a cloud solution architecture

options.text: Request Transfer Appliances from Google Cloud, export the data to appliances, and return the appliances to Google Cloud.
Configure the Storage Transfer service from Google Cloud to send the data from your data center to Cloud Storage.
Make sure there are no other users consuming the 1Gbps link, and use multi-thread transfer to upload the data to Cloud Storage.
Export files to an encrypted USB device, send the device to Google Cloud, and request an import of the data to Cloud Storage.

questions.explanation:
A 1-Gbps connection cannot transfer 1 PB within one month; its theoretical transfer time is about 93 days before accounting for protocol overhead or other use. Transfer Appliance is intended for large on-premises migrations when a network upload would take more than a week, and multiple appliances can scale the transfer. Data is copied locally to the appliances and the appliances are returned to Google for ingestion into Cloud Storage.

**Learn more:** [Transfer Appliance overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/transfer-appliance/docs/4.0/overview) · [Storage Transfer Service transfer options](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage-transfer/docs/transfer-options)

You are designing a centralized, automated infrastructure-deployment process for your organization with Terraform and Cloud Build. The security team forbids using long-lived, static service account keys in any CI/CD pipeline. In addition, although developers can propose infrastructure changes for peer review, they must not be permitted to directly apply changes in the production project.  
  
You need to design a secure, automated workflow for applying Terraform changes that satisfies the security team's requirements and provides appropriate governance. What should you do?

options.text: Configure the Cloud Build pipeline to use service account impersonation. Set up a trigger that automatically runs terraform apply when a pull request is merged.
Use service account impersonation in Cloud Build. Configure the pipeline to run terraform plan on pull requests, and require manual approval before running terraform apply.
Configure the pipeline to only run terraform plan. After a pull request is approved, have an authorized developer run terraform apply from a secured workstation.
Create a privileged service account and store its JSON key in Secret Manager. Configure the Cloud Build pipeline to fetch this key during execution to authenticate Terraform.

questions.explanation:
Service account impersonation supplies short-lived credentials and avoids generating or distributing long-lived service account keys. A pull-request Terraform plan enables review before changes are made, while Cloud Build manual approval gates a pending build so only a principal with approval permission can allow the Terraform apply stage to run. This keeps production apply authority in the controlled pipeline rather than with developers.

**Learn more:** [Authentication for Terraform](https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/terraform/authentication) · [Gate builds on approval](https://docs.cloud.google.com/build/docs/securing-builds/gate-builds-on-approval)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are preparing to migrate your on-premises compute and SAP workloads to Google Cloud. You want to use Google-recommended practices to rapidly create a cost estimate for operating these workloads in Google Cloud. What should you do?

options.text: Leverage Cloud Asset Inventory to gather data and generate a cost estimate.
Use the Google Cloud pricing calculator, and input the estimated resource to generate a cost estimate.
Engage with a Google Cloud partner to perform a comprehensive assessment and provide a customized cost estimate.
Gather data about your current environment, and leverage Google Cloud Migration Center to generate a cost estimate.

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud Migration Center generates rapid cost estimates based on data from the current environment and applies default assumptions for optimized configurations based on Google Cloud best practices. It includes calculators for both on-premises infrastructure and SAP workloads.

**Learn more:** [Cost estimation overview | Migration Center | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/migration-center/docs/estimate/overview?authuser=0) · [Start a cost estimation | Migration Center | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/migration-center/docs/estimate/start-estimation)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],The current Dress4Win system architecture has high latency for some customers because it is hosted in one data center.  
  
During a future evaluation and while optimizing cloud performance, Dresss4Win wants to distribute its system architecture across multiple locations on Google Cloud Platform.  
  
Which approach should it use?

options.text: Use regional managed instance groups and a global load balancer to increase performance because the regional managed instance group can grow instances in each region separately based on traffic.
Use a global load balancer with a set of virtual machines that forward the requests to a closer group of virtual machines managed by your operations team.
Use regional managed instance groups and a global load balancer to increase reliability by providing automatic failover between zones in different regions.
Use a global load balancer with a set of virtual machines that forward the requests to a closer group of virtual machines as part of a separate managed instance groups.

questions.explanation:
Regional managed instance groups can run and scale application instances independently in multiple regions. A global external load balancer can route user traffic to the closest healthy backend with capacity, reducing latency for geographically distributed customers.

**Learn more:** [External Application Load Balancer overview](https://cloud.google.com/load-balancing/docs/https) · [External Application Load Balancer performance best practices](https://cloud.google.com/load-balancing/docs/https/http-load-balancing-best-practices)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],JencoMart has chosen to migrate user-profile storage to Google Cloud Datastore and its application servers to Google Compute Engine (GCE). During the migration, the existing infrastructure will require access to Datastore to upload the data.  
  
Which service-account key-management strategy should you recommend?

options.text: Provision service account keys for the on-premises infrastructure and for the GCE virtual machines (VMs)
Authenticate the on-premises infrastructure with a user account and provision service account keys for the VMs
Provision service account keys for the on-premises infrastructure and use Google Cloud Platform (GCP) managed keys for the VMs
Deploy a custom authentication service on GCE/Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) for the on-premises infrastructure and use GCP managed keys for the VMs

questions.explanation:
Infrastructure running outside Google Cloud requires a service account credential to authenticate to Google Cloud APIs; in this set of options, that is a user-managed service account key. Applications on Compute Engine VMs should use an attached service account, whose credentials are generated with Google-managed keys rather than embedding exported private keys in the VM. Google recommends attached service accounts for VM workloads and documents that Compute Engine uses Google-owned and managed key pairs to generate short-lived service account credentials.

**Learn more:** [Service accounts | Compute Engine | Google Cloud Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/access/service-accounts) · [Service account credentials | IAM | Google Cloud Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/service-account-creds)

You work for a sports association whose members are aged 8 to 30. The association collects a large volume of health data, such as injuries sustained, and stores it in BigQuery. Current legislation requires this information to be deleted at the subject's request. You want to design a solution that can support such a request. What should you do?

options.text: Use a unique identifier for each individual. Upon a deletion request, delete all rows from BigQuery with this identifier.

When ingesting new data in BigQuery, run the data through the Data Loss Prevention (DLP) API to identify any personal information. As part of the DLP scan, save the result to Data Catalog. Upon a deletion request, query Data Catalog to find the column with personal information.

Create a BigQuery view over the table that contains all data. Upon a deletion request, exclude the rows that affect the subject's data from this view. Use this view instead of the source table for all analysis tasks.
Use a unique identifier for each individual. Upon a deletion request, overwrite the column with the unique identifier with a salted SHA256 of its value.

questions.explanation:
A unique identifier provides a reliable way to find every row belonging to a particular subject. BigQuery DML supports deleting rows by using a `DELETE` statement with a `WHERE` condition, allowing the subject's health-data records to be removed. [BigQuery DML statements](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/dml-syntax)

**Learn more:** [BigQuery DML statements in GoogleSQL](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/dml-syntax)

An operations team currently has 10 TB of data stored in an object storage service provided by a third party. They need to transfer this data to a Cloud Storage bucket as quickly as possible while following Google-recommended practices. They also want to minimize the migration cost. Which approach should they use?

options.text: Use the gsutil mv command to move the data.
Use the Storage Transfer Service to move the data.
Download the data to a Transfer Appliance, and ship it to Google.
Download the data to the on-premises data center, and upload it to the Cloud Storage bucket.

questions.explanation:
Storage Transfer Service is Google Cloud’s recommended service for moving data from another cloud storage provider to Cloud Storage. It is designed for large-scale transfers, including data sets larger than 1 TiB, and performs supported cloud-provider-to-Cloud-Storage transfers as a managed service without routing the data through on-premises infrastructure or a Transfer Appliance.

**Learn more:** [Data transfer options | Storage Transfer Service](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage-transfer/docs/transfer-options) · [Storage Transfer Service overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage-transfer/docs/overview)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],For this item, refer to the Dress4Win case study.  
  
To remain legally compliant during an audit, Dress4Win must be able to obtain insight into all administrative actions that change the configuration or metadata of resources on Google Cloud.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Use Stackdriver Trace to create a Trace list analysis.
Use Stackdriver Monitoring to create a dashboard on the project's activity.
Enable Cloud Identity-Aware Proxy in all projects, and add the group of Administrators as a member.
Use the Activity page in the GCP Console and Stackdriver Logging to provide the required insight.

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud Admin Activity audit logs record user-driven API calls and other actions that modify resource configuration or metadata. These logs are always written and can be reviewed through the Google Cloud console’s activity/logging interfaces, providing the administrative audit trail required for compliance.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Audit Logs overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/audit?hl=en)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],For this question, refer to the EHR Healthcare case study. Previously, configuration errors assigned public IP addresses to backend servers that should not have been Internet-accessible. You must ensure that no one can assign external IP addresses to backend Compute Engine instances and that external IP addresses can be configured only on frontend Compute Engine instances. What should you do?

options.text: Create an Organizational Policy with a constraint to allow external IP addresses only on the frontend Compute Engine instances.
Revoke the compute.networkAdmin role from all users in the project with front end instances.
Create an Identity and Access Management (IAM) policy that maps the IT staff to the compute.networkAdmin role for the organization.
Create a custom Identity and Access Management (IAM) role named GCE_FRONTEND with the compute.addresses.create permission.

questions.explanation:
An Organization Policy using the `constraints/compute.vmExternalIpAccess` constraint can allowlist the frontend Compute Engine instances that may use external IP addresses. Once enforced, instances not explicitly listed are prohibited from receiving either ephemeral or static external IP addresses, which prevents backend instances from being exposed to the Internet.

**Learn more:** [Restrict external IP addresses to specific instances](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/ip-addresses/configure-static-external-ip-address)

questions.domain: Designing and planning a cloud solution architecture
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are setting up the cloud network architecture for a newly created Google Cloud project that will host applications on Compute Engine. Compute Engine virtual machine instances will be created in two separate subnets (sub-a and sub-b) in one region:  
  
- Instances in sub-a will have public IP addresses.  
- Instances in sub-b will have private IP addresses only.  
  
To download updated packages, the instances must connect to a public repository outside Google Cloud boundaries. You need to enable sub-b to access the external repository. What should you do?

options.text: Enable Private Google Access on sub-b.
Configure Cloud NAT and select sub-b in the NAT mapping section.
Configure a bastion host instance in sub-a to connect to instances in sub-b.
Enable Identity-Aware Proxy for TCP forwarding for instances in sub-b.

questions.explanation:
Public Cloud NAT lets Compute Engine VMs without external IP addresses initiate outbound connections to internet destinations while receiving only response traffic for those established connections. Configuring the NAT gateway to apply to sub-b provides the required package-repository access without assigning public IP addresses to its instances.

**Learn more:** [Cloud NAT overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/nat/docs/overview) · [Cloud NAT IP addresses and ports](https://docs.cloud.google.com/nat/docs/ports-and-addresses?hl=en)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You use Cloud SQL as the database backend for a large CRM deployment. As usage grows, you need to scale while ensuring that storage does not run out, CPU utilization stays at 75%, and replication lag remains below 60 seconds. What steps should you take to meet these requirements?

options.text: 1. Enable automatic storage increase for the instance. 2. Create a Stackdriver alert when CPU usage exceeds 75%, and change the instance type to reduce CPU usage. 3. Create a Stackdriver alert for replication lag, and shard the database to reduce replication time.

1. Enable automatic storage increase for the instance. 2. Change the instance type to a 32-core machine type to keep CPU usage below 75%. 3. Create a Stackdriver alert for replication lag, and deploy memcache to reduce load on the master.

1. Create a Stackdriver alert when storage exceeds 75%, and increase the available storage on the instance to create more space. 2. Deploy memcached to reduce CPU load. 3. Change the instance type to a 32-core machine type to reduce replication lag.

1. Create a Stackdriver alert when storage exceeds 75%, and increase the available storage on the instance to create more space. 2. Deploy memcached to reduce CPU load. 3. Create a Stackdriver alert for replication lag, and change the instance type to a 32-core machine type to reduce replication lag.

questions.explanation:
Cloud SQL automatic storage increase adds capacity when available storage falls below its threshold, helping prevent an instance from running out of disk space. Increasing the machine type to 32 cores provides additional CPU capacity to keep utilization below the target. Monitoring replication lag with an alert and using a cache to reduce load on the primary database helps keep replicas from falling behind.

**Learn more:** [Cloud SQL instance settings](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres/instance-settings) · [Cloud SQL for MySQL replication lag](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/mysql/replication/replication-lag)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company runs an application as a Deployment in a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster. You maintain separate clusters for development, staging, and production. You discovered that the team can deploy a Docker image to the production cluster without first testing that deployment in development and then staging. You want to preserve the team’s autonomy while preventing this. You need a Google Cloud solution that can be implemented quickly with minimal effort. What should you do?

options.text: Configure a Kubernetes lifecycle hook to prevent the container from starting if it is not approved for usage in the given environment.
Implement a corporate policy to prevent teams from deploying Docker images to an environment unless the Docker image was tested in an earlier environment.
Configure binary authorization policies for the development, staging, and production clusters. Create attestations as part of the continuous integration pipeline.
Create a Kubernetes admissions controller to prevent the container from starting if it is not approved for usage in the given environment.

questions.explanation:
Binary Authorization enforces deploy-time policies for container images on GKE. Policies can require trusted attestations, and the CI pipeline can create those attestations after the required development and staging checks. A production policy can therefore block an image unless it carries the required verifiable approval evidence, without building and operating a custom Kubernetes admission controller.

**Learn more:** [Attestations overview | Binary Authorization](https://cloud.google.com/binary-authorization/docs/attestations) · [Binary Authorization concepts](https://cloud.google.com/binary-authorization/docs/key-concepts)

questions.question:
Your company has completed a successful migration to the cloud and wants to analyze its data stream to optimize operations. It has no existing code for this analysis, so it is evaluating all available options. The options include a combination of batch and stream processing, because it runs some hourly jobs while processing some data live as it arrives.  
  
Which technology should it use?

options.text: Google Cloud Dataproc
Google Cloud Dataflow
Google Container Engine with Bigtable
Google Compute Engine with Google BigQuery

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud Dataflow is a fully managed service for unified batch and stream data processing at scale. It supports both scheduled batch pipelines and continuously processed live data through the Apache Beam programming model.\
\
**Learn more:** [Dataflow overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/overview) · [Dataflow: streaming analytics](https://cloud.google.com/products/dataflow)

Which technology should it use?

options.text: Create a request form where engineers can request a sandbox environment for a specific technology. Automate the creation of a project with only the relevant APIs enabled and lower the default API quota. Grant IAM roles related to this scope to the requesting team. Ensure the project is automatically deleted after a predefined amount of time.

Create a request form where engineers can request a sandbox environment and automate the creation of a project in which the requesting engineer obtains full permissions. Within the details of the request form, highlight the expectation of keeping costs under control and the scope limited to the requested services.

Create a separate billing account for all sandbox projects. Grant all engineers the role of Billing Account User on this billing account. Create a folder called Sandboxes in the Organization's Resource Manager. Grant all users the Project Creator role on this folder.

Create a secondary Google Cloud organization which is to be used for R&D, separate from the production organization. Create a folder for each team under this organization. Create a project for each team member in the relevant folder. Grant each team member full access to their dedicated project. Grant each team manager the permission of Security Admin on the respective folder. Have them enable the relevant APIs in each team member's project.

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud projects provide isolated trust boundaries and are the level at which APIs are enabled, IAM permissions are granted, and quotas are applied. A temporary, centrally automated project that enables only the requested APIs, grants only scope-appropriate roles, applies reduced quotas, and is deleted after a defined period enforces least privilege and limits both resource use and the lifetime of experimental workloads. This prevents sandbox experiments from persisting as unmanaged production-like projects.

**Learn more:** [Create projects | Resource Manager](https://cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/creating-managing-projects) · [Cloud Quotas overview](https://cloud.google.com/docs/quotas/overview)

A large healthcare provider’s main electronic health record (EHR) application runs on Compute Engine instances and uses a Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL database, all in the `us-west1` region.  
  
A new regulatory mandate requires implementation and documentation of a business continuity plan (BCP). The plan must ensure that the EHR application can be completely recovered and operating in another geographical region, with a recovery time objective (RTO) of two hours and a recovery point objective (RPO) of 15 minutes.  
  
You need to design a disaster recovery strategy that fulfills these strict BCP requirements. What should you do?

options.text: Deploy active managed instance groups (MIGs) in both us-west1 and us-east1, fronted by a global external HTTP(S) Load Balancer. For the database, use a cross-region read replica in us-east1, and rely on load balancer health checks to automatically fail over all traffic during an outage.

Use Terraform to define the application’s compute infrastructure. During a disaster, configure the Cloud SQL database in us-west1 to use a cross-region read replica in us-east1, build the environment in us-east1, and promote the replica.

Take daily snapshots of the Compute Engine disks and Cloud SQL database. Copy these snapshots to a Cloud Storage bucket in us-east1. During a disaster, manually restore the virtual machines (VMs) and database from the latest snapshots
Deploy a regional MIG in us-west1 for high availability, and rely on the Google Cloud SLA to ensure the region remains online.

questions.explanation:
A pre-established cross-region Cloud SQL read replica provides continuously replicated data in the secondary region and can be promoted to a writable primary during a regional outage. Defining the Compute Engine application infrastructure with Terraform enables the secondary environment to be recreated consistently within the two-hour recovery window. The replica’s replication lag must be monitored and kept within 15 minutes to meet the RPO. Google Cloud documents cross-region replicas and promotion as the Cloud SQL regional-disaster-recovery mechanism; backup/restore takes longer, and replica promotion is required before the secondary database can accept writes.

**Learn more:** [Promote replicas for regional migration or disaster recovery](https://cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres/replication/cross-region-replicas) · [About disaster recovery in Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL](https://cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres/intro-to-cloud-sql-disaster-recovery)

You are deploying a PHP App Engine Standard service that uses Cloud SQL as its backend. You want to minimize the number of database queries.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Set the memcache service level to dedicated. Create a key from the hash of the query, and return database values from memcache before issuing a query to Cloud SQL.
Set the memcache service level to dedicated. Create a cron task that runs every minute to populate the cache with keys containing query results.
Set the memcache service level to shared. Create a cron task that runs every minute to save all expected queries to a key called ג€cached_queriesג€.
Set the memcache service level to shared. Create a key called ג€cached_queriesג€, and return database values from the key before using a query to Cloud SQL.

questions.explanation:
A cache-aside implementation uses a distinct key, such as a hash of the query, to look up a cached result before accessing Cloud SQL. A cache hit avoids the database query; on a cache miss, the application can query Cloud SQL and cache the result for later requests. Dedicated memcache provides cache capacity exclusively assigned to the application, while shared memcache is best-effort.

**Learn more:** [Memcache Examples — App Engine standard environment](https://docs.cloud.google.com/appengine/docs/standard/services/memcache/examples?hl=en) · [Using Memcache — App Engine standard environment](https://docs.cloud.google.com/appengine/docs/standard/services/memcache/using)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You must choose a storage system for click data from your company’s large portfolio of websites. The data is streamed by a custom website-analytics package at a typical rate of 6,000 clicks per minute, with bursts reaching 8,500 clicks per second. It must be retained for later analysis by the data science and user-experience teams.  
  
Which storage infrastructure should you select?

options.text: Google Cloud SQL
Google Cloud Bigtable
Google Cloud Storage
Google Cloud Datastore

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud Bigtable provides horizontally scalable, low-latency, high-throughput storage for large single-keyed datasets. It is explicitly suited to clickstream workloads and stream-processing or analytics use cases, making it appropriate for sustained ingestion with very high write bursts and subsequent analysis.

questions.question: You are using Cloud Shell and must install a custom utility to use in a few weeks. Where can you store the file so that it is on the default execution path and persists between sessions?

options.text: ~/bin
Cloud Storage
/google/scripts
/usr/local/bin

questions.explanation:
Cloud Shell provides persistent storage mounted at `$HOME`, and files in that home directory survive across sessions. The `~/bin` directory is a user-level executable location in the login `PATH`, allowing an executable stored there to be invoked directly while remaining persistent. Directories such as `/usr/local/bin` are on the ephemeral Cloud Shell instance filesystem and are not retained after the instance is replaced.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure Cloud Shell](https://cloud.google.com/shell/docs/configuring-cloud-shell) · [How Cloud Shell works](https://cloud.google.com/shell/docs/how-cloud-shell-works)

options.text: Replace the existing data warehouse with BigQuery. Use table partitioning.
Replace the existing data warehouse with a Compute Engine instance with 96 CPUs.
Replace the existing data warehouse with BigQuery. Use federated data sources.
Replace the existing data warehouse with a Compute Engine instance with 96 CPUs. Add an additional Compute Engine preemptible instance with 32 CPUs.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery is a managed, serverless data warehouse designed for scalable analytics. Partitioned BigQuery tables divide large datasets into partitions; queries that filter on the partitioning column can prune irrelevant partitions, which improves performance and reduces the amount of data processed and associated query cost.

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are deploying an application on App Engine that must integrate with an on-premises database. For security reasons, the on-premises database must not be reachable through the public internet. What should you do?

options.text: Deploy your application on App Engine standard environment and use App Engine firewall rules to limit access to the open on-premises database.
Deploy your application on App Engine standard environment and use Cloud VPN to limit access to the on-premises database.
Deploy your application on App Engine flexible environment and use App Engine firewall rules to limit access to the on-premises database.
Deploy your application on App Engine flexible environment and use Cloud VPN to limit access to the on-premises database.

questions.explanation:
Cloud VPN provides private connectivity between the Google Cloud VPC network and the on-premises network, allowing the application to reach the database by its internal IP address without exposing the database to the public internet. App Engine flexible environment instances use the Compute Engine networking model, enabling this VPC-based connectivity.

**Learn more:** [Understanding data and file storage — App Engine flexible environment](https://docs.cloud.google.com/appengine/docs/flexible/storage-options) · [App Engine flexible environment app.yaml reference](https://cloud.google.com/appengine/docs/flexible/reference/app-yaml)
