questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You use a single Cloud SQL instance to serve your application from a particular zone. You want to add high availability. What should you do?

options.text: Create a read replica instance in a different region
Create a failover replica instance in a different region
Create a read replica instance in the same region, but in a different zone
Create a failover replica instance in the same region, but in a different zone

questions.explanation:
Cloud SQL high availability uses a primary instance and a synchronized standby instance in different zones within the same region. If the primary instance or its zone fails, Cloud SQL fails over to the standby automatically. Read replicas do not provide automatic failover, and cross-region replicas address regional disaster recovery rather than zonal high availability.

**Learn more:** [Availability in Cloud SQL](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/availability) · [Cloud SQL key terms](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/key-terms)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You discovered an error in your App Engine application that is due to missing Cloud Datastore indexes. Upload the configuration file to App Engine's default Cloud Storage bucket, and have App Engine detect the new indexes
In the GCP Console, use Datastore Admin to delete the current indexes and upload the new configuration file
Create an HTTP request to the built-in python module to send the index configuration file to your application

questions.explanation:
Composite Cloud Datastore indexes are deployed from the local index configuration file by using the gcloud Datastore index-creation command. In current gcloud syntax, this is `gcloud datastore indexes create INDEX_FILE`; the older command form in the option is the equivalent intended action.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],For this item, refer to the KnightMotives Automotive case study. As part of developing fully autonomous driving vehicles, KnightMotives wants to analyze all vehicle-sensor data captured during test drives. This analysis will allow KnightMotives to improve its software using insights from the data.  
  
- Different event types, including parking, overtaking, and navigating, must be analyzed. Each test vehicle and event type has an ID.  
- Different sensor categories, including cameras, radars, and ultrasonic beams, must also be analyzed. During every autonomously initiated event, data from multiple sensors will be captured and sent to Google Cloud, where it will be stored in Bigtable.  
  
During analysis, you need to retrieve all sensor data for occurrences of the same event type, for a particular vehicle, within a specified time interval. You need to design a Bigtable schema optimized for read performance. What should you do?

options.text: Use the sensor category, event ID, and timestamp (in that order) as the row key. Create a column family for each individual sensor and a column qualifier for each vehicle.

Use the timestamp, vehicle ID, and event ID (in that order) as the row key. Create a column family per sensor category, and use a column qualifier for each individual sensor within its respective category.

Use the vehicle ID, event ID, and timestamp (in that order) as the row key. Create a column family per sensor category, and use a column qualifier for each individual sensor within its respective category.

Use the vehicle ID and event ID (in that order) as the row key. Create a column family per sensor category, and use a column qualifier for each individual sensor within its respective category. Utilize the timestamped versions of a cell to distinguish between different moments in time of similar events.

questions.explanation:
Bigtable sorts row keys lexicographically. A row key ordered as vehicle ID, event ID, and timestamp places all records for a vehicle-event pair in one contiguous range and permits an efficient timestamp-bounded scan. Sensor categories are appropriate column families, and individual sensors within a category are appropriate column qualifiers. A timestamp should not be the leading key component for this access pattern.

**Learn more:** [Schema design best practices | Bigtable](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigtable/docs/schema-design?hl=en) · [Schema design for time series data | Bigtable](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigtable/docs/schema-design-time-series)

options.text: Add all users to a group. Grant the group the role of BigQuery user on the billing project and BigQuery dataViewer on the projects that contain the data.
Add all users to a group. Grant the group the roles of BigQuery dataViewer on the billing project and BigQuery user on the projects that contain the data.
Add all users to a group. Grant the group the roles of BigQuery jobUser on the billing project and BigQuery dataViewer on the projects that contain the data.
Add all users to a group. Grant the group the roles of BigQuery dataViewer on the billing project and BigQuery jobUser on the projects that contain the data.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery requires `bigquery.jobs.create` on the project from which a query is run, irrespective of where the queried data resides. Granting BigQuery Job User on the centralized billing project causes query jobs, and therefore their charges, to be associated with that project. BigQuery Data Viewer on the data projects provides read/query access to the datasets without data-editing permissions.

**Learn more:** [Run a query | BigQuery | Google Cloud Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/running-queries) · [BigQuery IAM roles and permissions | Google Cloud Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/access-control)

You need to upload files from your on-premises environment to Cloud Storage. You want the files stored in Cloud Storage to be encrypted with customer-supplied encryption keys. What should you do?

options.text: Supply the encryption key in a .boto configuration file. Use gsutil to upload the files.
Supply the encryption key using gcloud config. Use gsutil to upload the files to that bucket.
Use gsutil to upload the files, and use the flag --encryption-key to supply the encryption key.
Use gsutil to create a bucket, and use the flag --encryption-key to supply the encryption key. Use gsutil to upload the files to that bucket.

questions.explanation:
For the legacy gsutil workflow, configure the customer-supplied encryption key in the `.boto` configuration file and upload the objects with `gsutil`. Customer-supplied encryption keys are applied to individual objects, not configured as a bucket default.

**Learn more:** [Boto configuration file | Cloud Storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/boto-gsutil) · [Customer-supplied encryption keys | Cloud Storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/encryption/customer-supplied-keys)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company uses Salesforce for customer relationship management (CRM), ServiceNow for IT service management, and a Cloud SQL database for storing customer transaction data.  
  
You must seamlessly connect, map, and transform data across these systems to maintain data consistency and support real-time reporting. You want to follow Google-recommended practices. What should you do?

options.text: Leverage Workflows to connect the services and transform the data.
Leverage Application Integration to connect the services and transform the data.
Leverage Pub/Sub and BigQuery to connect the services and transform the data.
Leverage Pub/Sub and Datastream to connect the services and transform the data.

questions.explanation:
Application Integration is Google Cloud’s recommended service for integrating business systems with differing data structures, including Salesforce, ServiceNow, and Cloud SQL. Its connectors and data-mapping and transformation capabilities support consistent data exchange and event-driven integrations across those systems.

**Learn more:** [Choose Application Integration or Workflows](https://docs.cloud.google.com/application-integration/docs/choose-application-integration-or-workflows) · [Data mapping | Application Integration](https://docs.cloud.google.com/application-integration/docs/data-mapping-overview)

questions.domain: Designing and planning a cloud solution architecture
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are leading a large-scale Google Cloud implementation project. Your development teams must deploy applications, but they do not have deep expertise in cloud-native patterns. This results in inconsistent and insecure deployments, including GKE clusters without appropriate logging and IAM roles that are overly permissive. You need to implement a system that enables these teams to deploy complete, pre-approved architectural patterns through self-service. The system must provide security and consistency by default while preserving high developer velocity and avoiding manual approval bottlenecks. What should you do?

options.text: Create a central Cloud Monitoring dashboard and a set of custom alerts that fire whenever a non-compliant resource is detected.
Use Service Catalog to define, govern, and offer a portfolio of approved products. Include Terraform scripts into Service Catalog items.
Enforce a mandatory CI/CD pipeline using Cloud Build that requires every Terraform deployment to be reviewed and approved before the Terraform apply step can run.
Use a combination of organization policies to restrict resource configurations and IAM recommender to periodically suggest improvements.

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud Service Catalog lets administrators curate and share approved solutions for internal users to discover and deploy. A catalog solution can use a Terraform configuration, so platform teams can package complete, validated infrastructure patterns that enforce secure defaults while allowing self-service deployment without a separate manual approval for each deployment.

**Learn more:** [Creating a Terraform configuration — Service Catalog](https://docs.cloud.google.com/service-catalog/docs/terraform-configuration) · [Service Catalog documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/service-catalog/docs)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building a deep learning model that needs high-performance access to large volumes of media data currently held in Cloud Storage. Model training will run on multiple VM instances with attached GPUs, but the application must access the data as though it were on the local file system. You need to minimize cost and complexity. What should you do?

options.text: Copy the data from Cloud Storage to Filestore, and then mount the Filestore volume as a local file system on your VM instances.
Create a shared persistent disk, attach the disk to your VM instances, and load data from the Cloud Storage bucket.
Use the gcsfuse command line tool to mount the Cloud Storage bucket as a local file system, and perform read/write operations in your bucket using standard file system semantics.
Use the gsutil command line tool to download the data to your VM instances.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Storage FUSE mounts a Cloud Storage bucket as a local file system, allowing applications to read and write bucket objects through standard file-system semantics. This avoids copying the dataset into Filestore, persistent disks, or each VM, reducing extra storage cost and operational complexity.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Storage FUSE overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/cloud-storage-fuse/overview)

Your organization runs a 3-tier web application in the same Google Cloud Platform network. Each tier—web, API, and database—scales independently of the other tiers. Network traffic must pass from the web tier to the API tier and then to the database tier. Traffic must not pass directly between the web and database tiers.  
  
How should you configure the network?

options.text: Add each tier to a different subnetwork
Set up software based firewalls on individual VMs
Add tags to each tier and set up routes to allow the desired traffic flow
Add tags to each tier and set up firewall rules to allow the desired traffic flow

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud VPC firewall rules control whether traffic is allowed or denied, and network tags let those rules apply to all instances in each scalable tier. Assign distinct tags to the web, API, and database tiers; allow web-to-API and API-to-database traffic with targeted firewall rules, and do not allow web-to-database traffic. Routes determine packet paths and do not provide this tier-to-tier access control.

**Learn more:** [Use VPC firewall rules](https://cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/using-firewalls) · [Add network tags](https://cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/add-remove-network-tags)

options.text: 1. From the dataset where you have the source data, create views of tables that you want to share, excluding PII. 2. Assign an appropriate project-level IAM role to the members of the data science team. 3. Assign access controls to the dataset that contains the view.

questions.explanation:

Your company wants to migrate its 10-TB on-premises database export to Cloud Storage. You want to minimize the time required to complete this activity, the total cost, and database load. Bandwidth between the on-premises environment and Google Cloud is 1 Gbps. You want to follow Google-recommended practices. What should you do?

options.text: Develop a Dataflow job to read data directly from the database and write it into Cloud Storage.
Use the Data Transfer appliance to perform an offline migration.
Use a commercial partner ETL solution to extract the data from the on-premises database and upload it into Cloud Storage.
Compress the data and upload it with gsutil -m to enable multi-threaded copy.

questions.explanation:
With a 1-Gbps connection, an online upload of a 10-TB export is practical; Google describes Transfer Appliance as especially suitable when network bandwidth is limited or unavailable, and notes that reasonable connectivity such as 1 Gbps can make online transfer appropriate. Compressing the existing export reduces the transfer volume without rereading the database, while `gsutil -m` performs operations in parallel to improve upload throughput. This avoids the shipping delay and added appliance cost, as well as the database load of extracting data through Dataflow or an ETL tool.

**Learn more:** [Migrate to Google Cloud: Transfer your large datasets](https://cloud.google.com/architecture/migration-to-google-cloud-transferring-your-large-datasets) · [Data transfer options](https://cloud.google.com/storage-transfer/docs/transfer-options)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company runs AI/ML workloads on graphics processing units (GPUs) in Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). These workloads are deployed across production and development projects, and the production environment is business-critical and runs 24/7. You must ensure GPU capacity is always available during scaling events without being constrained by overall GPU availability. You also need to be able to shift unused GPU capacity from the production project to development projects as necessary. You want to follow Google-recommended practices. What should you do?

options.text: Create a reservation in the production project, and then transfer the reservation to the development project when needed.
Create a shared reservation in the production project, and then add the development project as a consumer project to move capacity when needed.
Create an owner project with shared reservations, and then configure the production project and development project as consumer projects to consume capacity.
Create a reservation in the production project, and then create a separate reservation in the development project to secure capacity.

questions.explanation:
Shared reservations guarantee capacity for matching GPU VM resources and can be consumed by multiple designated projects. Google recommends an owner project that creates and manages the shared reservations but does not consume them, with workload projects configured as consumer projects. This lets production and development draw from the same reserved capacity, maximizing use of capacity that production is not currently consuming.

**Learn more:** [Best practices for shared reservations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instances/best-practices-shared-reservations) · [Consuming reserved zonal resources in GKE](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/consuming-reservations?hl=en)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are moving a critical, on-premises, three-tier ecommerce application to Google Cloud. The application has tightly coupled dependencies across its web, application, and database tiers. The business has stringent performance and availability requirements and is concerned about the risks of an "all-at-once" migration. You want to follow Google-recommended practices to build a migration plan that systematically handles application dependencies and validates post-migration performance before the final production cutover. What should you do?

options.text: Prioritize the establishment of a high-bandwidth, low-latency Cloud Interconnect connection, and then plan to migrate the database servers first.
Plan a
Redesign the application to be cloud-native using microservices before migration to eliminate dependencies and simplify workload testing.
Use dependency mapping to group application components into waves, create a phased migration plan, and incorporate performance testing for each wave.

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud recommends mapping workload dependencies during discovery and assessment, then grouping interdependent workloads into migration waves and move groups. Phased waves enable risk reduction and feedback between deployments, while testing and validation of non-functional requirements—including performance and availability—helps confirm that each migrated wave meets operational requirements before production cutover.

**Learn more:** [About migration planning | Migration Center | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/migration-center/docs/migration-planning-overview) · [Plan your migration waves | Migration Center | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/migration-center/docs/plan-migration-waves)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],TerramEarth intends to connect all 20 million vehicles in the field to the cloud. This raises the volume to 20 million 600-byte records per second, totaling 40 TB per hour.  
  
How should the data ingestion be designed?

options.text: Vehicles write data directly to GCS
Vehicles write data directly to Google Cloud Pub/Sub
Vehicles stream data directly to Google BigQuery
Vehicles continue to write data using the existing system (FTP)

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud Pub/Sub is an asynchronous, scalable messaging service designed to ingest and distribute streaming data from many producers, including IoT devices. It decouples vehicle publishers from downstream processing and storage, which can subsequently deliver the data to services such as BigQuery or Cloud Storage. Google documents Pub/Sub as supporting data-streaming use cases and workloads reaching millions of messages per second.

**Learn more:** [What is Pub/Sub?](https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/overview) · [Architectural overview of Pub/Sub](https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/architecture)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are designing the storage architecture for a financial analytics platform. The platform ingests and retains terabytes of transactional data each day, which supports both real-time fraud detection and long-term historical analysis.  
  
Transaction data from the most recent 30 days must be available with very low latency to the fraud-detection engine. Data more than 30 days old is accessed infrequently for quarterly reports, for which retrieval times of a few seconds are acceptable. All data must be retained for five years to satisfy compliance regulations.  
  
You need to design the most cost-effective solution possible. What should you do?

options.text: Store all transaction data in a Cloud Storage bucket using the Standard storage class for the entire five-year retention period.
Ingest all data into BigQuery using time-partitioned tables, and rely on BigQuery’s automatic long-term storage pricing for data older than 90 days.
Configure a Cloud Storage bucket with an Object Lifecycle Management policy to transition data from the Standard class to the Archive class after 30 days.
Configure a Cloud Storage bucket with an Object Lifecycle Management policy to transition data from the Standard class to the Coldline class after 30 days.

questions.explanation:
Coldline storage is designed for data read or modified at most once per quarter and provides low-latency online access at a lower storage cost than Standard storage. Keeping the most recent 30 days in Standard storage satisfies the fraud-detection latency requirement, while an Object Lifecycle Management policy can automatically transition older objects to Coldline for the five-year retention period. Archive storage is better suited to data accessed less than once per year and has higher access costs.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Storage storage classes](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/storage-classes) · [Object Lifecycle Management](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/lifecycle)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],For this question, refer to the Altostrat Media case study. Altostrat is worried about sophisticated, multi-vector Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks aimed at multiple layers of its infrastructure. DDoS attacks could disrupt video streaming and result in financial losses. You must mitigate this risk. What should you do?

options.text: Set up VPC Service Controls to restrict access to sensitive resources and prevent data exfiltration.
Configure Cloud Next Generation Firewall (NGFW) with custom rules to filter malicious traffic at the network level.
Deploy Google Cloud Armor with pre-configured and custom rules for L3/L4 and L7 protection
Activate Security Command Center to monitor security posture and detect potential threats.

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud Armor provides always-on protection against Layer 3 and Layer 4 volumetric and network-protocol DDoS attacks, while Cloud Armor security policies provide configurable Layer 7 protection. This combination mitigates multi-vector attacks before malicious traffic reaches streaming workloads.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Armor overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/armor/docs/cloud-armor-overview)

Your team is beginning development of a new application that uses a microservices architecture on Kubernetes Engine. As part of the development lifecycle, every code change pushed to the remote `develop` branch in your GitHub repository must be built and tested automatically. After the build and tests succeed, the applicable microservice must be deployed automatically to the development environment. You need to ensure that all code deployed to the development environment follows this process. What should you do?

options.text: Have each developer install a pre-commit hook on their workstation that tests the code and builds the container when committing on the development branch. After a successful commit, have the developer deploy the newly built container image on the development cluster.

Install a post-commit hook on the remote git repository that tests the code and builds the container when code is pushed to the development branch. After a successful commit, have the developer deploy the newly built container image on the development cluster.

Create a Cloud Build trigger based on the development branch that tests the code, builds the container, and stores it in Container Registry. Create a deployment pipeline that watches for new images and deploys the new image on the development cluster. Ensure only the deployment tool has access to deploy new versions.

Create a Cloud Build trigger based on the development branch to build a new container image and store it in Container Registry. Rely on Vulnerability Scanning to ensure the code tests succeed. As the final step of the Cloud Build process, deploy the new container image on the development cluster. Ensure only Cloud Build has access to deploy new versions.

questions.explanation:
A branch-based Cloud Build trigger centrally runs the required tests and creates the container image whenever code is pushed to the remote `develop` branch. A deployment pipeline that consumes the resulting image can deploy only artifacts that have passed that build, and exclusive deployment access for that tool prevents developers from bypassing the process. Vulnerability scanning evaluates container-image vulnerabilities and does not replace application build and test steps.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Build triggers](https://docs.cloud.google.com/build/docs/triggers) · [Create and manage build triggers](https://docs.cloud.google.com/build/docs/automating-builds/create-manage-triggers)

A primary business objective is to be able to trust the data stored in your application. You want to record every change to the application data.  
  
How can you design the logging system to verify the authenticity of its logs?

options.text: Write the log concurrently in the cloud and on premises
Use a SQL database and limit who can modify the log table
Digitally sign each timestamp and log entry and store the signature
Create a JSON dump of each log entry and store it in Google Cloud Storage

questions.explanation: Digital signatures cryptographically bind each timestamp and log entry to the signer. A valid signature can be verified later, and any modification to the signed content invalidates it, providing evidence of log integrity and authenticity.

options.text: Engage an independent auditor to conduct an ISO/IEC 27001 audit of your organization's Google Cloud implementation.

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your operations team has asked for help diagnosing a performance problem in a production application running on Compute Engine. The application drops requests that reach it under heavy load. The process list on affected instances shows one application process consuming all available CPU, and autoscaling has reached the instance upper limit. No other related systems, including the database, are experiencing abnormal load. You want production traffic to be served again as quickly as possible. Which action should you recommend?

options.text: Change the autoscaling metric to agent.googleapis.com/memory/percent_used.
Restart the affected instances on a staggered schedule.
SSH to each instance and restart the application process.
Increase the maximum number of instances in the autoscaling group.

questions.explanation:
A CPU-saturated managed instance group that has reached its autoscaling maximum cannot add capacity despite continued demand. Raising the autoscaler's maximum number of instances permits scale-out and distributes requests across additional application instances. Compute Engine autoscaling adds VMs when CPU utilization exceeds the configured target, subject to the configured maximum. 

**Learn more:** [Scaling based on CPU utilization](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/autoscaler/scaling-cpu) · [Autoscaling groups of instances](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/autoscaler)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],For this question, refer to the TerramEarth case study. You are moving a Linux-based application from your private data center to Google Cloud. The TerramEarth security team has sent you several recently published Linux vulnerabilities from Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE). You need help understanding how these vulnerabilities might affect your migration. What should you do? (Choose two.)

options.text: Open a support case regarding the CVE and chat with the support engineer.
Read the CVEs from the Google Cloud Status Dashboard to understand the impact.
Read the CVEs from the Google Cloud Platform Security Bulletins to understand the impact.
Post a question regarding the CVE in Stack Overflow to get an explanation.
Post a question regarding the CVE in a Google Cloud discussion group to get an explanation.

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud Security Bulletins provide official information about security vulnerabilities affecting Google Cloud products, including CVE impact and mitigation guidance. A Google Cloud support case provides access to a support engineer for assistance applying that information to a specific environment and migration.

**Learn more:** [Google Cloud Security Bulletins](https://docs.cloud.google.com/support/bulletins)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],For this question, use the EHR Healthcare case study. Because infrastructure administration costs are increasing, you want to migrate the legacy relational database systems to Google Cloud. You must maintain the strict uptime requirements with limited in-house expertise. What should you do?

options.text: Use the Database Migration Service (DMS) to migrate the MySQL databases to Cloud SQL.
Backup and restore the databases to Cloud SQL instances with minimal changes.
Leverage AlloyDB to migrate the on-premises databases.
Set up database replication to Cloud SQL instances using native database tools, and incrementally switch applications to use the replicas.

questions.explanation:
Database Migration Service provides a managed migration path from MySQL to Cloud SQL, including an initial data load and continuous replication for a low-downtime cutover. Cloud SQL reduces database-administration effort and supports regional high availability, making it appropriate for stringent availability requirements with limited operational expertise.

**Learn more:** [Migrate a database to Cloud SQL for MySQL by using Database Migration Service](https://docs.cloud.google.com/database-migration/docs/mysql/quickstart) · [Types of migration — Database Migration Service for MySQL](https://docs.cloud.google.com/database-migration/docs/mysql/migration-types)

questions.domain: Analyzing and optimizing technical and business processes
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your product team is developing a critical, customer-facing application on Google Cloud. The development team wants to use Spanner for its database to benefit from its horizontal scalability and low operational overhead. However, the FinOps team is concerned about Spanner's direct monthly cost and has proposed using a self-managed PostgreSQL database on Compute Engine VMs instead.  
  
You need to resolve this conflict and ensure the project proceeds with an architecturally sound database selection that balances technical requirements and financial constraints. What should you do?

options.text: Provide the development team with a reference architecture for deploying a highly available PostgreSQL cluster on a regional managed instance group (MIG).
Suggest using Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL as a compromise to get a managed service at a lower cost than Spanner.
Develop a total cost of ownership (TCO) analysis that includes operational overhead, and present it in a workshop to facilitate a decision.
Cite the reliability and performance optimization pillars of the Google Cloud Well-Architected Framework to formally justify the use of Spanner.

questions.explanation:
A total cost of ownership analysis compares more than direct database charges: it accounts for compute, storage, network, one-time costs, and continuing operational expenses. This enables a fact-based workshop decision that weighs Spanner's managed scalability and operational benefits against the cost and operational burden of a self-managed PostgreSQL deployment.

**Learn more:** [Assess your migration | Spanner | Google Cloud Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/assess-migration) · [Spanner operational guidelines | Google Cloud Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/operational-guidelines)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Dress4Win has end-to-end tests that cover 100% of its endpoints. They want to ensure that moving to the cloud does not introduce any new bugs.  
  
Which additional testing method should the developers use to prevent an outage?

options.text: They should enable Google Stackdriver Debugger on the application code to show errors in the code.
They should add additional unit tests and production scale load tests on their cloud staging environment.
They should run the end-to-end tests in the cloud staging environment to determine if the code is working as intended.
They should add canary tests so developers can measure how much of an impact the new release causes to latency.

questions.explanation:
Running the existing end-to-end suite in a cloud staging environment validates the complete application behavior in the actual target environment before production release. This exposes migration-specific defects in cloud configuration, service interactions, and deployment behavior while a rollback or correction can still occur safely. Google Cloud guidance describes staging as the final validation step before production and recommends end-to-end testing alongside other test types.

**Learn more:** [Automate and manage change](https://cloud.google.com/architecture/framework/operational-excellence/automate-and-manage-change) · [Environment hybrid pattern](https://cloud.google.com/architecture/hybrid-multicloud-patterns-and-practices/environment-hybrid-pattern)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Every 12 months, auditors visit your teams and ask to review all Google Cloud Identity and Access Management (Cloud IAM) policy changes made during the preceding 12 months. You want to simplify and speed up the analysis and audit process.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create custom Google Stackdriver alerts and send them to the auditor
Enable Logging export to Google BigQuery and use ACLs and views to scope the data shared with the auditor
Use cloud functions to transfer log entries to Google Cloud SQL and use ACLs and views to limit an auditor's view
Enable Google Cloud Storage (GCS) log export to audit logs into a GCS bucket and delegate access to the bucket

questions.explanation:
Cloud Audit Logs can be routed to a BigQuery dataset for analysis. BigQuery provides SQL querying across the retained audit data, and IAM controls together with views can limit an auditor to the appropriate subset of records without granting unrestricted access to all log data.

**Learn more:** [Route log entries](https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/routing/overview) · [Cloud Audit Logs overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/audit)

questions.domain: Analyzing and optimizing technical and business processes
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company needs to optimize Google Cloud costs for its development and staging environments. These environments are workstations used by developers Monday through Friday, from 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM local time. Currently, the environments run on a fleet of nl-standard-4 Compute Engine instances that operate 24/7, resulting in a high monthly cost for resources that are idle more than 70% of the time. You must implement a solution that significantly lowers the monthly cost of these non-production environments without affecting the development team’s productivity during work hours. What should you do?

options.text: Schedule the virtual machines to start and stop to match your team’s work schedule.
Purchase three-year committed use discounts (CUDs) for the existing nl-standard-4 instances.
Upgrade all instances to the N2 machine series.
Re-architect the environments to run on a regional managed instance group (MIG) with autoscaling enabled.

questions.explanation:
Compute Engine instance schedules can automatically start and stop VM instances on a recurring timetable, including a local time zone. Stopping the non-production workstations outside Monday–Friday working hours eliminates most idle compute runtime while keeping them available when developers need them.

**Learn more:** [Schedule a VM instance to start and stop](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instances/schedule-instance-start-stop)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A large multinational company is migrating to Google Cloud. It has distinct business units: Finance, Marketing, and Research and Development (R&D). The central security team has established the following governance requirements for each unit:  
  
- **Finance:** Must be limited to deploying resources only in the specific compliant regions `us-central1` and `europe-west2`. Access to its projects must be strictly controlled by a dedicated `finance-admins` group.  
- **Marketing:** Requires separate production and development environments, with different teams responsible for managing each environment.  
- **R&D:** Needs maximum flexibility to test new services, but must be fully isolated so it cannot affect production systems.  
- **Global Auditing:** A central compliance team needs read-only access to view every resource across the entire company for auditing.  
  
You must design a resource hierarchy that enforces these security policies at scale, follows the Google Cloud Well-Architected Framework, and provides each business unit with the appropriate level of autonomy. What should you do?

options.text: Create a folder for each department under the root Organization node. Apply the resource location Organization Policy on the Finance folder. Within the Marketing folder, create separate projects for mktg-prod and mktg-dev. Grant the compliance team the roles/viewer role at the Organization level.

Place all projects directly under the Organization node. Use network tags and service accounts to enforce security boundaries between the different department workloads. Apply the resource location Organization Policy on the Finance project.
Create separate Google Cloud Organizations for each department (Finance, Marketing, and R&D). Grant the compliance team the roles/viewer role for each organization.
Create a single project for each department. Apply the resource location policy directly to the Finance project. Grant the compliance team the roles/browser role on each project individually.

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud folders are policy and IAM inheritance boundaries that support delegated administration, security isolation, and scalable governance. Applying the resource-location Organization Policy to the Finance folder constrains all descendant projects to the approved locations, while department folders allow separate administrative control and isolation. Separate Marketing production and development projects create distinct environment boundaries. Granting `roles/viewer` at the Organization level gives the compliance team inherited read-only access throughout the organization hierarchy.

**Learn more:** [About the Google Cloud resource hierarchy](https://cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/cloud-platform-resource-hierarchy) · [Manage projects within folders](https://cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/manage-projects-within-folder)

options.text: Grant all department members the required IAM permissions for their respective projects.

Create a Google Group per department and add all department members to their respective groups. Create a folder per department and grant the respective group the required IAM permissions at the folder level. Add the projects under the respective folders.

Create a folder per department and grant the respective members of the department the required IAM permissions at the folder level. Structure all projects for each department under the respective folders.
Create a Google Group per department and add all department members to their respective groups. Grant each group the required IAM permissions for their respective projects.

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud recommends using groups when multiple principals need the same access, instead of assigning roles to individual users. Roles granted at a folder are inherited by projects under that folder; therefore, a department group with IAM roles assigned at its department folder receives consistent access across that department’s projects while membership and permissions are managed centrally.

**Learn more:** [Using resource hierarchy for access control](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/resource-hierarchy-access-control) · [Understanding allow policies](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/allow-policies)

To strengthen governance and security, your organization has organized its Google Cloud environment with folders for separate business units. Every business-unit folder contains development, staging, and production subfolders that must meet internal security controls:  
  
- Production workloads must, by default, be protected from direct internet ingress unless they are explicitly tagged.  
- The application must be reachable by customers over HTTPS.  
  
You need to create a scalable, enforceable model that blocks internet ingress traffic to production folders while selectively permitting direct HTTPS traffic to the required virtual machines. You must also make sure individual project teams cannot override these controls after they are deployed for all existing and future production projects. What should you do?

options.text: At each production folder, apply a hierarchical firewall policy to deny all ingress except for HTTPS to tagged VMs.
Mandate the application teams to deploy a Terraform module to create VPC firewall rules in each project that deny ingress and allow HTTPS.
At the organization root, apply a hierarchical firewall policy to deny all ingress except for HTTPS to tagged VMs.
At each production folder, use an organization policy to block all external IPs and require teams to use external HTTPS load balancers.

questions.explanation:
A hierarchical firewall policy associated with each production folder applies to every descendant project and its VPC resources, including projects created later. It can use a higher-priority HTTPS allow rule targeted to the approved VM group, followed by a lower-priority deny rule for other internet ingress. Hierarchical firewall rules inherited from a higher resource level cannot be overridden by lower-level project or VPC firewall rules, providing centrally enforced protection. Secure tags can target the approved VM group in hierarchical firewall rules.

**Learn more:** [Hierarchical firewall policies](https://cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/firewall-policies) · [Create hierarchical firewall policies and rules](https://cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/using-firewall-policies)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],For this question, use the Helicopter Racing League (HRL) case study.  
  
A recent finance audit of cloud infrastructure found an exceptionally high number of Compute Engine instances allocated for video encoding and transcoding. You suspect these Virtual Machines are zombie machines that were not deleted after their workloads completed. You need to quickly obtain a list of idle VM instances. What should you do?

options.text: Log into each Compute Engine instance and collect disk, CPU, memory, and network usage statistics for analysis.
Use the gcloud compute instances list to list the virtual machine instances that have the idle: true label set.
Use the gcloud recommender command to list the idle virtual machine instances.
From the Google Console, identify which Compute Engine instances in the managed instance groups are no longer responding to health check probes.

questions.explanation:
Compute Engine’s Idle VM Recommender uses Cloud Monitoring system metrics to identify idle VM instances and exposes those recommendations through `gcloud recommender recommendations list` with the `google.compute.instance.IdleResourceRecommender` recommender. This provides a direct list of VMs that are candidates for removal.

**Learn more:** [View and apply idle VM recommendations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instances/viewing-and-applying-idle-vm-recommendations?hl=en) · [Idle VM recommendations overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instances/idle-vm-recommendations-overview?hl=en)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],For this question, refer to the TerramEarth case study. Taking the technical requirements into account, how should you reduce unplanned vehicle downtime in GCP?

options.text: Use BigQuery as the data warehouse. Connect all vehicles to the network and stream data into BigQuery using Cloud Pub/Sub and Cloud Dataflow. Use Google Data Studio for analysis and reporting.
Use BigQuery as the data warehouse. Connect all vehicles to the network and upload gzip files to a Multi-Regional Cloud Storage bucket using gcloud. Use Google Data Studio for analysis and reporting.

Use Cloud Dataproc Hive as the data warehouse. Upload gzip files to a Multi-Regional Cloud Storage bucket. Upload this data into BigQuery using gcloud. Use Google Data Studio for analysis and reporting.
Use Cloud Dataproc Hive as the data warehouse. Directly stream data into partitioned Hive tables. Use Pig scripts to analyze data.

questions.explanation:
Reducing vehicle downtime requires current telemetry for timely predictive maintenance and replacement-parts planning. Pub/Sub can ingest events from connected vehicles, and Dataflow can process the streaming data and write it to BigQuery for low-latency analytics and reporting. Periodic gzip-file uploads leave the data stale, while a Dataproc/Hive solution adds operational complexity without improving the real-time ingestion path.

**Learn more:** [Dataflow overview](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/overview) · [Stream from Pub/Sub to BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/tutorials/dataflow-stream-to-bigquery)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You must deploy a stateful workload on Google Cloud. The workload can scale horizontally, but every instance must read from and write to the same POSIX filesystem. Under high load, the stateful workload must support up to 100 MB/s of writes. What should you do?

options.text: Use a persistent disk for each instance.
Use a regional persistent disk for each instance.
Create a Cloud Filestore instance and mount it in each instance.
Create a Cloud Storage bucket and mount it in each instance using gcsfuse.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Filestore supplies a shared, POSIX-compliant NFS filesystem that multiple instances can mount concurrently. Its performance can be provisioned to meet the required write throughput. Persistent Disk options are per-instance block storage rather than a shared filesystem, and Cloud Storage FUSE is not POSIX compliant.

**Learn more:** [Filestore overview](https://cloud.google.com/filestore/docs/overview) · [About instance performance](https://cloud.google.com/filestore/docs/performance)

You are designing a new application feature for a healthcare provider located in Qatar. The feature must summarize sensitive patient notes submitted by clinicians. A critical requirement is that the contents of these patient notes must never be processed outside Qatar's borders. You want to use a powerful, pretrained generative model for the summarization task while strictly complying with the data-residency constraint. What should you do?

options.text: Write application code that sends the patient notes explicitly to the Gemini API endpoint in Qatar for summarization. Protect the API by VPC-Service Controls.
Use Vertex AI Model Garden to select a Gemma model. Deploy this model to a Vertex AI Endpoint within a Google Cloud region located in Qatar.
Use the Cloud Natural Language API to analyze the text and configure it to generate a summary of the patient notes.
Gather a large, anonymized dataset of medical notes. Use Vertex AI Training to train a custom summarization model from scratch, deploying it in a Qatar region.

questions.explanation:
Deploying a Gemma model from Vertex AI Model Garden to a Vertex AI Endpoint in Doha, Qatar (`me-central1`) keeps online inference within the selected regional deployment while using a pretrained generative model. Doha supports Vertex AI custom-model online inference, and Model Garden supports deploying Gemma models to Vertex AI endpoints. VPC Service Controls helps mitigate data-exfiltration risks but does not itself establish the geographic location in which a Gemini API request is processed.

**Learn more:** [Vertex AI locations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/machine-learning/general/locations) · [Deploy Gemma using Model Garden and Vertex AI endpoints](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/model-garden/deploy-and-inference-tutorial)

A customer needs to capture multiple GBs of aggregate, real-time key performance indicators (KPIs) from game servers running on Google Cloud Platform and monitor those KPIs with low latency. How should they capture the KPIs?

options.text: Store time-series data from the game servers in Google Bigtable, and view it using Google Data Studio.
Output custom metrics to Stackdriver from the game servers, and create a Dashboard in Stackdriver Monitoring Console to view them.
Schedule BigQuery load jobs to ingest analytics files uploaded to Cloud Storage every ten minutes, and visualize the results in Google Data Studio.
Insert the KPIs into Cloud Datastore entities, and run ad hoc analysis and visualizations of them in Cloud Datalab.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Monitoring supports user-defined (custom) metrics for application-specific data sent by instrumented applications. Those metric time series can be displayed on custom dashboards, providing the appropriate real-time operational monitoring workflow. Stackdriver Monitoring is the former name of Cloud Monitoring.

**Learn more:** [User-defined metrics overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/monitoring/custom-metrics) · [Display metric data on a custom dashboard](https://docs.cloud.google.com/monitoring/charts)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an application running in Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). During the past 2 weeks, customers have reported that a particular part of the application returns errors very frequently. No logging or monitoring solution is currently enabled on the GKE cluster. You want to diagnose the issue, but have been unable to reproduce it. You want to minimize disruption to the application. What should you do?

options.text: 1. Update your GKE cluster to use Cloud Operations for GKE. 2. Use the GKE Monitoring dashboard to investigate logs from affected Pods.

1. Create a new GKE cluster with Cloud Operations for GKE enabled. 2. Migrate the affected Pods to the new cluster, and redirect traffic for those Pods to the new cluster. 3. Use the GKE Monitoring dashboard to investigate logs from affected Pods.
1. Update your GKE cluster to use Cloud Operations for GKE, and deploy Prometheus. 2. Set an alert to trigger whenever the application returns an error.

1. Create a new GKE cluster with Cloud Operations for GKE enabled, and deploy Prometheus. 2. Migrate the affected Pods to the new cluster, and redirect traffic for those Pods to the new cluster. 3. Set an alert to trigger whenever the application returns an error.

questions.explanation:
Enabling Cloud Operations for the existing GKE cluster provides workload logging and monitoring without migrating Pods or redirecting production traffic. Workload logs can be examined for the affected Pods to diagnose intermittent customer-facing errors. Creating a replacement cluster is unnecessary disruption, while deploying Prometheus and setting an alert primarily supports future detection rather than investigating the observed errors.

**Learn more:** [About GKE logs](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/about-logs) · [View GKE logs](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/view-logs)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a custom-built application on a Compute Engine virtual machine (VM). The application processes real-time sales data and writes it to a zonal Persistent Disk. A recent internal audit requires a backup and recovery plan that protects against zonal failures. The company has a strict policy requiring all backup data to be retained for at least 90 days and stored in a separate project with restricted access. You need a fully automated backup solution that satisfies these requirements with minimal operational overhead. What should you do?

options.text: Write a script to create daily backups of the Persistent Disk. Copy the backups to a different zone and apply a label to each snapshot to indicate the deletion date.
Use gcloud commands to create snapshots of the Persistent Disk. Store the snapshots in a regional Cloud Storage bucket and configure a lifecycle rule to delete objects older than 90 days.
Create a snapshot schedule to automatically create Persistent Disk snapshots and use a script to move and store them in a multi-regional Cloud Storage bucket.
Use the Backup and Disaster Recovery (DR) service to create a backup plan. Configure the backup plan to take daily snapshots and store them in a backup vault with a 90-day retention policy.

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud Backup and DR backup plans can automatically create scheduled backups for Compute Engine disks and retain them in a backup vault. Backup vaults provide isolated storage with enforced retention, and a centralized model can place backup vaults and backup plans in an administrator project while protecting resources in separate service projects. A 90-day vault retention policy therefore meets the required retention period and supports restricted access with minimal operational management.

**Learn more:** [Backup vaults for immutable and indelible backups](https://docs.cloud.google.com/backup-disaster-recovery/docs/concepts/backup-vault?hl=en) · [Back up disks to a backup vault](https://docs.cloud.google.com/backup-disaster-recovery/docs/cloud-console/compute/disk-backup)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Mountkirk Games has deployed its new backend on Google Cloud Platform (GCP). You want to establish a thorough testing process for new backend versions before they are released publicly. You want the testing environment to scale cost-effectively. How should you design the process?

options.text: Create a scalable environment in GCP for simulating production load
Use the existing infrastructure to test the GCP-based backend at scale
Build stress tests into each component of your application using resources internal to GCP to simulate load
Create a set of static environments in GCP to test different levels of load ג€

questions.explanation:
A scalable, production-like GCP environment enables end-to-end load testing of the backend under simulated production demand. Elastic capacity can increase for a test and decrease afterward, avoiding the cost and inflexibility of permanently provisioned static test environments. Google Cloud recommends automated nonfunctional testing, often combined with performance or load testing, to verify that an application scales as expected.

**Learn more:** [Patterns for scalable and resilient apps](https://cloud.google.com/architecture/scalable-and-resilient-apps) · [Take advantage of elasticity](https://cloud.google.com/architecture/framework/performance-optimization/elasticity)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are deploying a new three-tier application to Compute Engine instances in one Virtual Private Cloud (VPC). The architecture is divided into three subnets: a web-tier subnet, an application-tier subnet, and a database-tier subnet.  
  
- The web tier must receive traffic only from an external load balancer.  
- The application tier must receive traffic only from the web tier.  
- The database tier must receive traffic only from the application tier.  
  
You need to enforce strict traffic-flow control while following Google-recommended practices. What should you do?

options.text: Configure Cloud NAT for each subnet, and create Google Cloud Armor policies to filter traffic between the tiers based on their IP address ranges.
Create a single VPC firewall rule with a high priority that allows ingress traffic on all ports between the IP address ranges of the three subnets.

Use a combination of network tags and service accounts. Apply a unique network tag and a dedicated service account to the instances in each tier. Then create specific firewall rules that allow ingress traffic based on the source service account or tag of the upstream tier.
Set up VPC Network Peering between the web tier and application tier subnets, and another peering connection between the application tier and database tier subnets.

questions.explanation:
VPC firewall rules should follow least privilege: allow only the required protocols, ports, sources, and targets. Tier-specific service accounts (or, less strictly, network tags) enable ingress rules that permit only the upstream tier to reach each downstream tier. Google recommends service-account-based source and target filtering when strict control is needed because service accounts are IAM-controlled identities, whereas network tags can be changed by principals able to edit an instance. A firewall rule cannot mix service-account and network-tag criteria in the same rule, so the rules should consistently use one compatible method—preferably service accounts.

**Learn more:** [VPC firewall rules](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/firewalls) · [Use VPC firewall rules](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/using-firewalls)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building an application with several microservices that must remain internal to the cluster. You need to configure each microservice with a particular number of replicas. You also need every microservice to be reachable from any other microservice in a consistent way, irrespective of how many replicas it scales to. You must implement this solution on Google Kubernetes Engine. What should you do?

options.text: Deploy each microservice as a Deployment. Expose the Deployment in the cluster using a Service, and use the Service DNS name to address it from other microservices within the cluster.
Deploy each microservice as a Deployment. Expose the Deployment in the cluster using an Ingress, and use the Ingress IP address to address the Deployment from other microservices within the cluster.
Deploy each microservice as a Pod. Expose the Pod in the cluster using a Service, and use the Service DNS name to address the microservice from other microservices within the cluster.
Deploy each microservice as a Pod. Expose the Pod in the cluster using an Ingress, and use the Ingress IP address name to address the Pod from other microservices within the cluster.

questions.explanation:
A Deployment manages the desired number of replicated Pods. A Kubernetes Service provides a stable internal endpoint and DNS name for the selected Pods, and load-balances requests across them as replicas scale. This keeps service-to-service addressing independent of changing Pod IPs and replica counts.

**Learn more:** [Understand Kubernetes Services](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/service) · [About kube-dns for GKE](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/kube-dns)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your customer is migrating its corporate applications to Google Cloud Platform. The security team needs detailed visibility into every project in the organization. You provision Google Cloud Resource Manager and configure yourself as the organization administrator.  
  
Which Google Cloud Identity and Access Management (Cloud IAM) roles should you assign to the security team?

options.text: Org viewer, project owner
Org viewer, project viewer
Org admin, project browser
Project owner, network admin

questions.explanation:
The Organization Viewer role provides visibility into the organization, and the Project Viewer role provides read-only visibility into project resources. A role granted at the organization level is inherited by its descendant projects, giving the security team visibility across all projects without owner or administrator privileges.

**Learn more:** [Resource Manager roles and permissions](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/roles-permissions/resourcemanager) · [Manage access to projects, folders, and organizations](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/granting-changing-revoking-access)

A company has a stateless web API that performs scientific calculations. The web API runs on one Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster, currently deployed in `us-central1`. The company has expanded to provide its API to customers in Asia and wants to reduce latency for users there.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create a second GKE cluster in asia-southeast1, and expose both APIs using a Service of type LoadBalancer. Add the public IPs to the Cloud DNS zone.
Use a global HTTP(s) load balancer with Cloud CDN enabled.
Create a second GKE cluster in asia-southeast1, and use kubemci to create a global HTTP(s) load balancer.
Increase the memory and CPU allocated to the application in the cluster.

questions.explanation:
A second GKE cluster in an Asian region places API workloads nearer to Asian users. A multi-cluster global HTTP(S) load balancer provides a single globally reachable endpoint with backends across clusters and supports proximity-based routing, reducing latency to a suitable regional backend. Cloud CDN is primarily useful for cacheable responses and does not make uncached scientific calculations execute nearer to users.

**Learn more:** [Multi Cluster Ingress | GKE networking](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/multi-cluster-ingress) · [Setting up Multi Cluster Ingress | GKE networking](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/multi-cluster-ingress-setup)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to store critical business information in Cloud Storage buckets. The information changes regularly, but previous versions must be referenced regularly. You need to ensure there is a record of every change to any information in these buckets. You also need accidental edits or deletions to be easily rolled back. Which feature should you enable?

options.text: Bucket Lock
Object Versioning
Object change notification
Object Lifecycle Management

questions.explanation:
Cloud Storage Object Versioning preserves an overwritten or deleted live object as a noncurrent version. These versions can be listed, accessed by generation, and restored, providing version history and rollback capability.

**Learn more:** [Object Versioning | Cloud Storage | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/object-versioning?hl=en) · [Use versioned objects | Cloud Storage | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/using-versioned-objects?hl=en)

questions.question:
Your company has several on-premises systems that act as sources for reporting. The data has not been well maintained and has degraded over time.  
  
You want to follow Google-recommended practices to detect anomalies in your company data. What should you do?

options.text: Upload your files into Cloud Storage. Use Cloud Datalab to explore and clean your data.
Upload your files into Cloud Storage. Use Cloud Dataprep to explore and clean your data.
Connect Cloud Datalab to your on-premises systems. Use Cloud Datalab to explore and clean your data.
Connect Cloud Dataprep to your on-premises systems. Use Cloud Dataprep to explore and clean your data.

questions.explanation: Cloud Dataprep is intended for visually exploring and cleaning data, including detecting data-quality problems, before downstream analysis. Files from on-premises sources should be uploaded to Cloud Storage so they can be prepared in Cloud Dataprep.

questions.domain: Designing and planning a cloud solution architecture
questions.question:
Your company has several on-premises systems that act as sources for reporting. The data has not been well maintained and has degraded over time.  
  
You want to follow Google-recommended practices to detect anomalies in your company data. What should you do?

options.text: Use Cloud SQL for time series data, and use Cloud Bigtable for historical data queries.
Use Cloud SQL to replace MySQL, and use Cloud Spanner for historical data queries.
Use Cloud Bigtable to replace MySQL, and use BigQuery for historical data queries.
Use Cloud Bigtable for time series data, use Cloud Spanner for transactional data, and use BigQuery for historical data queries.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Bigtable is designed for high-throughput, low-latency time-series data. Cloud Spanner provides scalable, strongly consistent ACID transactions for transactional data, and BigQuery is a serverless data warehouse optimized for large-scale historical and analytical queries.

**Learn more:** [Bigtable overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigtable/docs/overview) · [Transactions overview — Spanner](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/transactions)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your team runs applications on a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster that has a private endpoint. You have configured a Cloud Deploy pipeline, but deployments to the GKE cluster are failing. You need to fix the issue. What should you do?

options.text: Use VPC Service Controls with Cloud Build Update the Cloud pipeline to use Cloud Build as its execution environment.
Create a Cloud Build private pool in the default VPC. Use Cloud Build to deploy the applications to the GKE cluster.
Create a Cloud Build private pool that is peered with the same VPC network as your GKE cluster. Update the Cloud Deploy pipeline to use this private pool as its execution environment.
Create a custom target in Cloud Deploy Update the deploy pipeline to use the custom target for the application deployment.

questions.explanation:
Deploying to a private GKE cluster through its private endpoint requires a Cloud Build private worker pool with connectivity to the cluster’s VPC network. Cloud Deploy can use that private pool as the target execution environment for its deployment operations; the default worker pool does not provide the required private-network access.

**Learn more:** [Deploy to a Google Kubernetes Engine cluster](https://docs.cloud.google.com/deploy/docs/gke-targets) · [Using Cloud Deploy execution environments](https://docs.cloud.google.com/deploy/docs/execution-environment)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to create a continuous-delivery pipeline for a containerized application on Google Cloud. You want every test to run within the pipeline to improve the quality of your application. What should you do?

options.text: 1. After the developers push the code to a central repository, trigger Cloud Build to run unit tests. If all unit tests are successful, build the application container and push it to a central registry.2. Trigger Cloud Build to deploy the container to a testing environment and run integration tests and acceptance tests.3. If all tests are successful, deploy the application to the production environment and run the smoke tests.

1. After the developers push the code to a central repository, trigger Cloud Build to build the application container. Then run unit tests.2. If unit tests are successful, deploy the container to a testing environment and run integration tests.3. If the integration tests are successful, deploy the container to a production environment and run acceptance tests.

1. Automatically run unit tests in a local environment once the code is changed. If all tests are successful, build a container.2. Trigger Cloud Build to deploy the container to a testing environment, and run integration tests and acceptance tests.3. If all tests are successful, tag the code as production ready. Trigger Cloud Build to build and deploy the container to the production environment.

1. Run unit tests in the developer's local environment before committing and pushing the code to a central repository.2. After the code is pushed, trigger Cloud Build to build the application container and deploy the container to a testing environment, and run integration tests.3. If the integration tests are successful, deploy the container to your production environment and run acceptance tests.

questions.explanation:
A delivery pipeline should gate artifact creation and promotion on automated tests: run unit tests from the committed source, build and publish the container only after they pass, validate that same artifact with integration and acceptance tests in a test environment, and promote it to production only after successful validation. Smoke tests verify the production deployment. Cloud Build triggers can start CI/CD workflows from repository changes, and Cloud Build build configurations can run unit and integration tests as ordered build steps.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Build overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/build/docs/overview?hl=en) · [Cloud Build triggers](https://docs.cloud.google.com/build/docs/triggers)

You manage a highly distributed hybrid- and multi-cloud IT environment, and your developers depend heavily on Prometheus for their workflows. You need a cloud-based, highly scalable, low-maintenance enterprise solution that supports Prometheus Query Language (PromQL) queries, rapid metric viewing, and effective issue diagnosis. What should you do?

options.text: Deploy a Prometheus operator in your existing Kubernetes and Serverless setup across multi-cloud environments.
Set up Cloud Monitoring as a single pane of glass across multi-cloud environments.
Enable Google Cloud Managed Service for Prometheus to monitor and alert on your workloads at scale.
Build a SaaS-based, Prometheus-compatible solution to display metrics for each cloud in a customizable way.

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud Managed Service for Prometheus is a fully managed, globally scalable, hybrid- and multi-cloud Prometheus solution. It supports PromQL, global querying and visualization through Cloud Monitoring or Grafana, and monitoring and alerting without operating Prometheus infrastructure at scale.

**Learn more:** [Google Cloud Managed Service for Prometheus overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/managed-prometheus) · [Query using the Prometheus API or UI](https://docs.cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/managed-prometheus/query-api-ui)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],For this question, refer to the EHR Healthcare case study. You are a developer on the EHR customer portal team. Your team recently migrated the customer portal application to Google Cloud. Load on the application servers has increased, and the application is now logging many timeout errors. You recently incorporated Pub/Sub into the application architecture, and the application is not logging any Pub/Sub publishing errors. You want to improve publishing latency.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Increase the Pub/Sub Total Timeout retry value.
Move from a Pub/Sub subscriber pull model to a push model.
Turn off Pub/Sub message batching.
Create a backup Pub/Sub message queue.

questions.explanation:
Pub/Sub publisher batching improves throughput and efficiency, but it can add latency to individual messages because they wait for a batch to fill. Turning off message batching removes that batching wait. Increasing the total retry timeout is intended to reduce publish timeout failures, while subscription delivery mode and an additional queue do not reduce publisher latency.

**Learn more:** [Best practices to publish to a Pub/Sub topic](https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/publish-best-practices) · [Batch messaging](https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/batch-messaging)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],For this item, refer to the Altostrat Media case study. Altostrat's development team uses a microservices architecture for its application. You need to choose the most appropriate testing approach to ensure that individual microservices operate correctly in isolation. What should you do?

options.text: Run unit testing.
Use load testing.
Perform end-to-end testing.
Execute integration testing

questions.explanation:
Unit testing verifies the behavior of an individual microservice or its code units independently of other services and external dependencies. Load testing assesses performance under demand, whereas integration and end-to-end testing validate interactions across components or complete workflows. Google Cloud recommends unit tests for the bulk of testing because they execute quickly and are generally straightforward to maintain.

**Learn more:** [Patterns for scalable and resilient apps | Google Cloud Architecture Center](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/scalable-and-resilient-apps)
